Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s reassurance from terrors and disquieting things that open the door to whispering, thereby fortifying its soul that is at rest in Allaah.
9. Distinguishing familiar faces from strange ones.
The method of direction: It is embraced often and frequently brought to meet the people of faith and love, so that by its innate disposition it grows familiar with the environment of goodness and its people.
First: Treating it through tasfiyah
The educator surrounds the child with the faces of the people of righteousness, so that its innate disposition grows familiar with the environment of goodness and its people. He establishes a righteous milieu from the very beginning.
Second: Treating it through tazkiyah
The educator couples the meeting of the righteous with love and reassurance, so that its sense of intimacy becomes bound to the people of faith. He intends to implant love for the people of goodness.
Third: Treating it through tarbiyah — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator supplicates for the child and remembers Allaah when meeting the people of righteousness. He repeats this at their meetings.
Fourth: Treating it through tarbiyah — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator often embraces the child and brings it to meet the people of faith and love. He makes this his habit.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator surrounds the child with the faces of the people of righteousness, thereby establishing an environment in which it grows familiar with goodness and its people, and its soul is led to the companionship of the righteous.
Through leading the emotions: The educator couples the meeting of the righteous with love and reassurance, so that the emotion of intimacy becomes bound to the people of faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): By endearing the child to the people of goodness, the educator intends to prepare it for righteous companionship for the sake of Allaah, not for a worldly interest.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The educator implants in the child familiarity with the people of faith and love for them, and keeps it away from the people of evil, so that it grows up upon loving and detesting for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: The educator brings the child often to meet the people of righteousness, with constancy and patience, until its familiarity with them takes root.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator brings the child to meet the people of righteousness as an example, counseling it by his state to choose good companionship from its tenderest age.
Through regulating time: The educator sets regular times in the child’s life for the gatherings of the righteous, so that its familiarity with them takes root through constancy.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator protects the child from growing familiar with evil companions, who are among the soldiers of Satan, thereby establishing the companionship of goodness from the cradle.
10. Attraction to rhythm and gentle sounds.
The method of direction: It is made to hear the measured recitation of the Qur’aan and wholesome speech instead of idle amusement and harmful sounds, so that its auditory taste is reared upon what Allaah loves.
First: Treating it through tasfiyah
The educator founds the child’s auditory taste upon the measured recitation of the Qur’aan and wholesome speech. He makes the first thing it is drawn to the cadences of revelation.
Second: Treating it through tazkiyah
The educator couples wholesome melodies with serenity and love, so that its taste becomes bound to the atmosphere of faith. He intends to implant love for the Qur’aan.
Third: Treating it through tarbiyah — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator lets the child hear the measured recitation of the Qur’aan and the remembrances instead of idle amusement. He makes this part of his day.
Fourth: Treating it through tarbiyah — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator (murabbie) keeps harmful sounds away from the child’s surroundings and sets the wholesome alternative in their place. He adheres to this constantly in the child’s environment.
Direction through the branches of veneration (ta3dhiem):
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator grounds the child’s auditory taste upon the measured recitation of the Qur’an, so that the first thing that attracts him is the melodies of the revelation (wahy) by which the soul is led.
Through leading the emotions: The educator couples the wholesome melodies with tranquility and love, so that the emotion of his taste becomes bound to the atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In letting him hear the Qur’an, the educator intends to make it beloved to him for the sake of Allaah, not mere entertainment or melodious delight.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal (walaa’ and baraa’): The educator makes the sounds of remembrance and of the Qur’an beloved to the child and turns him away from the sounds of forbidden idle amusement, so that he grows familiar with what Allaah loves.
Through patience (sabr): The educator perseveres in letting him hear the Qur’an with patience and repetition, until his love of listening to it takes firm root.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator lets the child hear the Qur’an as an example who loves it himself, counseling him by his own state to bind his heart to the speech of Allaah from an early age.
Through the governance of time: The educator sets aside fixed times for letting him hear the Qur’an, such as at sleeping and waking, so that his love for it takes root through their regularity.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s hearing from the sounds of falsehood and idle amusement, granting the enemy no hold over his taste and his ears.
11. Long, recurrent sleep.
The method of direction: He is put to sleep in a state of ritual purity insofar as possible, with the recitation of al-Mu3awwidhaat (the soerahs of seeking refuge), light blowing, and supplication, so that his sleep unfolds under the protection of Allaah.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that protection comes from Allaah, and so puts the child to sleep with remembrance and al-Mu3awwidhaat. He makes his sleep carry the meaning of taking refuge in Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator puts the child to sleep in tranquility, love, and faith-filled serenity. He intends that the child’s sleep unfold under the protection of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator recites al-Mu3awwidhaat and blows lightly over the child at his bedtime. He keeps this up every night.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator puts the child to sleep in a state of ritual purity insofar as possible, and in calm. He makes this his constant habit when putting him to bed.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator puts the child to sleep with remembrance and al-Mu3awwidhaat, thereby establishing that protection during sleep comes from Allaah, so that his soul is led to take refuge in Him.
Through leading the emotions: The educator puts the child to sleep in tranquility, love, and serenity, so that his emotions are formed upon a sense of safety coupled with faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): When putting the child to sleep, the educator calls to mind the hope of reward and the fulfillment of the child’s right for the sake of Allaah, not merely being relieved of him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator places the child’s sleep under the shelter of the remembrance of Allaah, so that he grows up upon the knowledge that tranquility and protection lie in loyalty to Allaah.
Through patience: The educator bears patiently the late hours of putting the child to sleep and hopes for reward, thereby training himself in patience in fulfilling the child’s right.
Through sincere counsel: The educator fulfills the child’s right in putting him to sleep as an example who hopes for reward, counseling him by his own state toward giving and mercy, not vexation.
Through the governance of time: The educator fixes the child’s bedtime and prepares its means, so that his sleep becomes regular and his staying up late diminishes through the governance of his time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator fortifies the child’s sleep with al-Mu3awwidhaat against Satan and his scheming, thereby establishing the protection of the soul through remembrance from its earliest days.
12. Gradual control of the head and of bodily movements.
The method of direction: Allaah is praised for every growth in his body, and supplication is made for him for strength and well-being in the obedience of Allaah, so that his bodily growth becomes coupled with gratitude to his Creator.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that the growth of the body is a blessing from Allaah, and so praises Him for every development. He makes the child’s growth coupled with gratitude to his Creator.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices at the child’s growth with a joy coupled with the praise of Allaah and love of Him, so that his growth becomes bound to an atmosphere of gratitude. He intends to implant veneration of the Creator.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator praises Allaah and supplicates for the child’s well-being at every growth in his movement. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator assists the child in his bodily movement with gentleness, accompanied by supplication. He adheres to this constantly in his care.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator praises Allaah for the growth of the child’s movement, thereby establishing that strength and growth are a blessing from Allaah, whose energy is to be directed toward His obedience.
Through leading the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s growth with a joy coupled with praise and love, so that the emotion of his joy becomes bound to gratitude to the Creator.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In assisting the child in his movement, the educator intends to raise him strong in the obedience of Allaah, not to boast of his superiority.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator directs the child’s growing movement toward what Allaah loves of goodness and obedience in the future, so that he grows up loving the good.
Through patience: The educator assists the child in the growth of his movement with gentleness and patience with its stages, neither hastening nor being harsh.
Through sincere counsel: The educator assists the child in his movement with gentleness, as an example, counseling him by his own state to encourage him, not to discourage him or treat him harshly.
Through the governance of time: The educator provides the child with regular times for safe movement, so that he grows in a balanced rhythm free of disorder.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator directs the energy of the child’s growing movement toward the good, so that it is not left aimless for desire or Satan to exploit later.
The Second Category: from six months to ten months
In this stage the child is characterized chiefly by sitting and crawling, voluntary grasping, babbling, separation anxiety, and the beginnings of social interaction and the imitation of expressions; among his innate traits are:
1. Sitting independently and gaining command of the body’s posture.
The method of direction: Allaah is praised before him for the blessing of sitting and of bodily command, and he is seated in gatherings of remembrance and of the Qur’an, so that he grows familiar with sitting in goodness.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator praises Allaah before the child for the blessing of sitting and of bodily command, and establishes that strength comes from Allaah. He repeats this with every development.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices at the child’s sitting with a joy coupled with the praise of Allaah, so that his newfound command becomes bound to an atmosphere of gratitude. He intends to implant veneration of the Creator.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator seats the child in a gathering of remembrance or of recitation and lets him hear it. He keeps this up.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator assists the child to sit, gently, in a wholesome environment. He makes this his constant habit.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator praises Allaah for the child’s mastery of sitting, thereby establishing that strength is a gift from Allaah, to be directed toward His obedience, and by it the soul is led.
Through leading the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s sitting with a joy coupled with praise, so that the emotion of his achievement becomes bound to gratitude to his Creator, not to self-conceit.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In accustoming the child to sitting in gatherings of goodness, the educator intends to prepare him for gatherings of remembrance for the sake of Allaah, not to boast of his progress.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator seats the child in the gatherings of the people of righteousness and remembrance, so that he grows familiar with the gatherings of those whom Allaah loves and shrinks from the gatherings of idle amusement.
Through patience: The educator assists the child to sit with gentleness and with patience for his gradual progress, neither hastening his growth nor burdening him beyond his capacity.
Through sincere counsel: The educator assists the child to sit gently and does not burden him beyond his capacity, counseling him by his own state to be mindful of his strength.
Through the governance of time: The educator trains the child to sit for short, gradually increasing periods, neither exhausting him nor hastening his growth.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator takes care that the child’s sitting be in goodness, not in a gathering of heedlessness that Satan might exploit, thereby establishing the habit of keeping company with the good.
2. Crawling and the beginning of creeping.
The method of direction: A safe, clean place is prepared for him, Allaah is praised for his movement, and it is directed toward what is wholesome, so that his first movements become coupled with a righteous environment.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that movement is a blessing from Allaah, and so praises Him for it before the child. He repeats this.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices at the child’s movement with a love coupled with the remembrance of Allaah. He intends to bind his movement to the good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator remembers Allaah and supplicates for the child as he crawls. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator prepares a safe, clean place for the child and directs his creeping toward the wholesome. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator prepares for the child a safe place in which he creeps toward the wholesome, thereby establishing that movement is a blessing to be directed toward what benefits, and by it the soul is led.
Through leading the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s movement with a joy coupled with love and gratitude, so that the emotion of his exploration becomes bound to the atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In enabling the child to move, the educator intends to raise him active in goodness for the sake of Allaah, not mere amusement.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator directs the child’s creeping toward what Allaah loves, such as drawing near to one who is praying, and keeps him away from what harms, so that he grows familiar with the direction of the good.
Through patience: The educator patiently follows the creeping child and protects him without irritation, and trains himself in watchfulness and forbearance.
Through sincere counsel: The educator protects the creeping child with gentleness and watchfulness, as an example, counseling him by his own state to safeguard his safety without irritation.
Through the governance of time: The educator sets aside safe times for creeping in a prepared place, so that he invests the child’s energy in an organized, protected time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s creeping from perils and injurious spots, leaving the enemy no door open through heedlessness of his protection.
3. Babbling and the repetition of syllables.
The method of direction: The words “Allaah” and “Bismillaah” are repeated within his hearing with gentleness and softness, so that the first thing his tongue imitates is from the words of remembrance.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that the blessing of speech is from Allaah, and so praises Him for it. He makes the first thing the child imitates the words of remembrance.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices at the child’s babbling and treats him tenderly with a love coupled with the remembrance of Allaah. He intends to make remembrance beloved to him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator repeats within the child’s hearing “Allaah” and “Bismillaah” gently, so that he may imitate them. He keeps this up daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator meets his babbling with a cheerful face and a tender touch, encouraging him. He repeats this.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator repeats within the child’s hearing the word “Allaah” so that he may imitate it in his babbling, thereby establishing that the first thing he utters is the remembrance of Him to whom the soul is led.
Through leading the emotions: The educator responds tenderly to the child’s babbling with cheerfulness and love, so that the emotion of his first speech becomes bound to intimacy with the remembrance of Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In instilling the words of remembrance in the child, the educator intends the devoting of his tongue to the service of Allaah, not boasting of his early speech.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes the repetition of the words of remembrance beloved to the child, so that his tongue is formed upon the goodly speech that Allaah loves.
Through patience: The educator repeats the instilling with patience and constancy until the child imitates the goodly words, and he does not hasten.
Through sincere counsel: The educator instills what is goodly in the child, as an example and with constancy, counseling him by his own state to make the first of his words the remembrance of Allaah.
Through the governance of time: The educator seizes the child’s moments of serenity for repeated instilling, thereby investing the best of times in planting the goodly word.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator takes care not to instill in the child idle or ugly speech in which Satan would find delight, thereby guarding his budding tongue from its very beginning.
4. Voluntary grasping of objects and passing them between the hands.
The method of direction: He is given wholesome, clean things to hold and is kept away from what is harmful, while Allaah is praised before him for the blessing of the hands.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that the blessing of the hands is from Allaah, and so praises Him for it before the child. He repeats this.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices at the child’s grasping with a love coupled with gratitude. He intends to bind the child’s abilities to the good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator praises Allaah and names the wholesome things the child holds. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator gives the child wholesome, clean things and removes the harmful. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator gives the child wholesome, beneficial things to hold, thereby establishing that the blessing of the hand is from Allaah, to be used in what benefits, and by it the soul is led.
Through leading the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s ability to grasp with a joy coupled with gratitude, so that his emotions become bound to the praise of his Creator.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In accustoming the child to holding the wholesome, the educator intends to prepare a hand that works for Allaah, not one for adornment and boasting.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator gently places the child’s hand upon what Allaah loves, such as the page of the mushaf, and removes it from what He detests, so that his hand grows familiar with the good.
Through patience: The educator bears patiently the child’s fiddling with his hands and directs him gently, thereby training himself in forbearance in disciplining him.
Through sincere counsel: The educator directs the child’s fiddling with his hands gently, as an example, counseling him by his own state to turn his hands to the beneficial, not the harmful.
Through the governance of time: The educator occupies the child’s hands in his waking hours with what benefits, filling his idle moments with the useful rather than with idle fiddling.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator removes from the child’s reach whatever harms him and whatever the enemy might use to injure him, thereby establishing the guarding of the hand from what harms.
5. The appearance of the first teeth and exploration of the mouth.
The method of direction: Allaah is praised for every growth in his body, what is harmful is gently kept away from his mouth, and supplication is made for his well-being.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that every growth is a blessing from Allaah, and so praises Him. He repeats this with every development.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator bears the child’s distress patiently, with tenderness and supplication coupled with faith. He intends mercy toward him for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator supplicates for the child’s well-being and remembers Allaah when he is distressed. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator treats the child tenderly and gently keeps what is harmful away from his mouth. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator praises Allaah for the growth of the child’s teeth, thereby establishing that every growth is a blessing from Allaah, so that his soul is led to gratitude to Him.
Through leading the emotions: The educator bears the child’s distress at teething with tenderness and supplication, thus governing the atmosphere of agitation and implanting serenity.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): When caring for the child in pain, the educator calls to mind the hope of reward with Allaah, not merely settling him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes his gentleness with the child in pain an act of compliance with a mercy that Allaah loves, so that the child grows up upon the value of mercy.
Through patience: The educator bears the child’s repeated distress patiently and hopes for reward, thereby training himself in forbearance and implanting a sense of safety in the child.
Through sincere counsel: The educator endures the child’s distress with forbearance, as an example, counseling him by his own state that distress is to be met with mildness and reassurance.
Through the governance of time: The educator anticipates the child’s distress by organizing the times of his needs, so that his discomfort lessens through the governance of the rhythm of his day.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator keeps away from the child’s mouth whatever harmful things he might explore, leaving the enemy no door open through heedlessness of his safety.
6. Anxiety at separation from the mother.
The method of direction: The mother reassures him with her calm presence coupled with remembrance, and does not frighten him, so that he is formed upon serenity, not fear.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that safety comes from Allaah, and so reassures the child with his calm presence. He makes the child’s serenity coupled with faith.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The mother reassures her child with love and tranquility coupled with the remembrance of Allaah, and does not frighten him. She intends to implant a faith-rooted security.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The mother remembers Allaah and supplicates for the child when he is anxious, soothing him. She repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The mother embraces her child gently when he is anxious and does not frighten him. She adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator reassures the child with his calm presence, thereby establishing that true safety comes from Allaah, who is never absent, so that his soul is led to attach itself to Him.
Through leading the emotions: The mother reassures her child’s anxiety with love and tranquility, not agitation, thereby implanting in him a faith-rooted serenity that governs his feelings.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In reassuring the child, the mother intends to raise him upon security in Allaah, not merely to silence him, and she makes her patience with him for the sake of Allaah.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The mother makes her reassurance of the child a door to binding his sense of safety to the love and remembrance of Allaah, so that he grows up upon the knowledge that tranquility lies in taking refuge in Him.
Through patience: The mother bears her child’s anxiety patiently and does not frighten him, hoping for reward, thereby training herself in forbearance and implanting in him a sense of safety.
Through sincere counsel: The mother calms her child’s anxiety and does not frighten him, as an example, counseling him by her own state to be a repose, not a source of terror.
Through the governance of time: The mother makes firm the child’s reassuring routine, so that his anxiety lessens through the regularity of his times and the steadiness of his rhythm.
Through knowing the enemies: The mother protects her child from excessive anxiety that would open the door to whisperings (waswaas), thereby fortifying his tranquil soul with the remembrance of Allaah.
7. Fear of strangers.
The method of direction: He is gently brought near to the people of righteousness and is not forced, so that by his innate disposition he grows familiar with the company of the good without terror.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes a righteous environment with which the child grows familiar, and so brings him near to the people of righteousness. He repeats this without compulsion.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator brings the child near to the righteous with love and serenity, so that he grows familiar with them. He intends to make the people of goodness beloved to him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator remembers Allaah and supplicates for the child when meeting people. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator brings the child gently near to the people of righteousness and does not force him. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator brings the child gradually near to the people of righteousness, thereby establishing familiarity with goodness and its people, and his soul is led to the company of the righteous.
Through leading the emotions: The educator brings the child near to people with gentleness and reassurance, not compulsion, thereby governing his fear and transforming it into a balanced familiarity.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In attuning the child to the righteous, the educator intends to prepare him for companionship for the sake of Allaah, not for courtesy or ostentation.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator puts the child at ease with the people of faith while preserving his innate wariness of the people of evil, so that he grows up upon loving and detesting for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: The educator bears patiently the child’s gradual progress in familiarity and does not force him upon those he fears, thereby training himself in gentleness.
Through sincere counsel: The educator leads the child by degrees into familiarity and does not force him upon those he fears, counseling him by his own state toward gentleness and unhurriedness.
Through the governance of time: The educator grants familiarity its sufficient time, by degrees, and does not hasten a fruit before its season.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator turns the child’s innate wariness to good account, sparing him the evil companions from among the hosts of Satan, thereby establishing the companionship of the good.
8. The beginning of the awareness of the permanence of objects.
The method of direction: He is played with in ways that develop his awareness (such as appearing and hiding), in an atmosphere of merriment coupled with naming, so that his awareness is nurtured in a wholesome environment.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator develops the child’s awareness in a wholesome environment, and so plays with him in ways that develop it. He makes the child’s learning take place in a righteous atmosphere.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator plays with the child with merriment coupled with naming and love. He intends to bind his awareness to the good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator mentions the name of Allaah and jests with the child in goodly speech during play. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator plays with the child at appearing and hiding in a wholesome atmosphere. He keeps this up.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator develops the child’s awareness through purposeful play, thereby laying the foundation of a mind that will later grasp the truth, and by which the soul is led to Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: The educator plays with the child with merriment coupled with naming and love, so that the emotion of his awareness becomes bound to the atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In developing the child’s awareness, the educator intends to prepare him to know his Lord and to work for Him, not to boast of his intelligence.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator binds his play with the child to the wholesome that Allaah loves, so that his awareness is formed in connection with the good.
Through patience: The educator repeats his play with the child patiently until his awareness grows, neither hastening nor wearying.
Through sincere counsel: The educator plays with the child with patience and love, as an example, counseling him by his own state to develop his awareness through purposeful play.
Through the governance of time: The educator sets aside regular, purposeful times of play, so that the child’s awareness grows in fruitful, not squandered, time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s play from idle amusement that Satan would exploit, making the development of his awareness take place in an atmosphere of goodness.
9. Responding to his name when called.
The method of direction: He is called by a beautiful name his parents have chosen for him, and his being called is coupled with tenderness, so that he grows familiar with his goodly name by which he is summoned to the good.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that the child’s beautiful name is a blessing and a supplication of good for him. He calls him by it repeatedly.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator calls the child by his name with love and tenderness, so that he grows familiar with it. He intends to bind his name to love for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator calls the child by his beautiful name and supplicates for him. He repeats this gently.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator meets the child’s response to his name with a cheerful face and a tender touch. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator calls the child by his beautiful name, thereby establishing that his goodly name is a blessing and a supplication, and his soul is led to respond to the good.
Through leading the emotions: The educator calls the child by his name with love and tenderness, so that the emotion of his response becomes bound to intimacy and love.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In accustoming the child to respond, the educator intends to prepare him for responding to Allaah and His Messenger, not for merely formal obedience.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator binds the child’s response to his name to the good, so that he grows up loving to respond to the people of faith and shunning the callers to evil.
Through patience: The educator repeats the call with patience until the child responds, being neither harsh nor hasty.
Through sincere counsel: The educator repeats the call gently and is not harsh, as an example, counseling him by his own state to accustom him to responding through mildness.
Through the governance of time: The educator calls the child at times suited to his attentiveness, thereby making use of his alertness, not his heedlessness.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator establishes the child’s responsiveness to the one who calls to the good, lest he grow up quick to respond to every shouter, even one calling to falsehood.
10. Imitation of facial expressions and simple sounds.
The method of direction: Cheerfulness, the smile, and the words of remembrance are modeled before him, so that by his innate disposition he picks up imitation from a righteous model.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that what the child imitates be good, and so displays before him cheerfulness and remembrance. He repeats this.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator displays before the child feelings of love and serenity, which the child then imitates. He intends to implant goodly feelings.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator moves his lips in remembrance before the child, that he may imitate him. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator smiles at the child and treats him tenderly, that he may imitate cheerfulness. He keeps this up.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator displays cheerfulness and remembrance before the child for him to imitate, thereby establishing that the first thing he imitates is good, so that his soul is led to follow the righteous example.
Through leading the emotions: The educator displays before the child feelings of love and serenity, which he imitates, so that his emotions are formed upon the good.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): By the excellence of his example before the child, the educator intends to raise him upon the good for the sake of Allaah, not to put on a performance before him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator models before the child the deeds of those whom Allaah loves, so that the child grows up imitating the people of good, not the people of evil.
Through patience: The educator repeats the display of good before the child with patience and constancy until he imitates it, thereby training himself in perpetual exemplariness.
Through sincere counsel: The educator displays the good before the child as a perpetual example, counseling him by his state before his speech, so that the child imitates him in the good.
Through the governance of time: The educator perseveres in displaying the good before the child at all his times, so that it becomes imprinted in him through constancy, not through a single occasion.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is wary lest the child imitate, from him or from those around him, an evil that Satan adorns, thereby guarding his example before him.
11. Seeking eye contact and social interaction.
The method of direction: His contact is met with cheerfulness, goodly speech, and supplication, so that his social interaction grows within the frame of love and goodness.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator grounds the child’s contact in a righteous environment, and so meets it with good. He makes his contact coupled with the wholesome.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator meets the child’s contact with love and cheerfulness coupled with supplication. He intends to implant love for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator speaks to the child with goodly words and remembrance when he makes contact. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator exchanges with the child glances, cheerfulness, and the tender touch. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator meets the child’s contact with good and with remembrance, thereby establishing that contact is a means to the good, and by it the soul is led to what benefits.
Through leading the emotions: The educator meets the child’s contact with love and cheerfulness coupled with supplication, so that his emotions are formed upon love for the sake of Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): By the excellence of his contact with the child, the educator intends to attune him to the good for the sake of Allaah, not for any worldly aim.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes the child’s contact with the people of faith one of familiarity and love, and spares him the contact of the people of evil, so that he grows up upon love for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: The educator exchanges contact with the child with constancy and with patience in caring for him, so that his intimacy with the good and its people becomes firm.
Through sincere counsel: The educator exchanges contact with the child as a tender example, counseling him by his own state to bind his intimacy to the good and its people.
Through the governance of time: The educator keeps to regular times of contact with the child, so that his intimacy becomes firm through the regularity of their meeting.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s contact from evil companions and influences from among the hosts of Satan, thereby establishing the contact of the good.
The Third Category: from ten months to one year
In this stage the child is characterized chiefly by standing and the beginning of walking, pointing with the finger, uttering the first words, understanding simple commands, imitating actions, and intense attachment; among his innate traits are:
1. Standing with assistance and the beginning of walking.
The method of direction: Allaah is praised for the blessing of walking, he is encouraged toward what is wholesome, and supplication is made for him that his feet may walk in the obedience of Allaah.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator establishes that the blessing of walking is from Allaah, and so praises Him before the child. He supplicates that the child’s feet may walk in the obedience of Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices at the child’s walking with a love coupled with gratitude. He intends to bind his movement to the good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator remembers Allaah and supplicates for the child as he walks. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator assists the child in walking and directs him toward the wholesome. He adheres to this constantly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: The educator supplicates for the child that his feet may walk in the obedience of Allaah, and establishes that the blessing of walking is to be directed toward the good, and by it the soul is led.
Through leading the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s walking with a joy coupled with praise, so that the emotion of his achievement becomes bound to gratitude to his Creator, not to self-conceit.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): In teaching the child to walk toward the good, the educator intends to prepare a foot that strives for Allaah, not to boast of his being ahead of others.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator directs the child’s steps toward what Allaah loves, such as walking to the place of prayer, and turns him from what harms, so that his foot grows familiar with the good.
Through patience: The educator assists the child in walking with gentleness and with patience for his stumbling, neither hastening nor being harsh when he falls.
Through sincere counsel: The educator assists the child in walking and is not harsh when he falls, as an example, counseling him by his own state toward encouragement, not discouragement.
Through the governance of time: The educator provides regular, safe times of training in walking, so that his growth advances by degrees in an organized time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s steps from injurious spots and perils, leaving the enemy no door open through heedlessness of his protection.
2. Pointing with the finger at what he wants.
The method of direction: He is guided to point at what is wholesome, and it is named for him (the sky, the mosque), so that his first pointing becomes coupled with the meanings of good.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator directs the child’s pointing toward what is wholesome and names it for him. He makes his first pointing be for the meanings of good.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
The educator rejoices with love at the child’s pointing toward the wholesome. He intends to bind his expression to the good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
The educator names the wholesome things the child points at, and remembers Allaah. He repeats this.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
The educator guides the child’s hand to point at the wholesome, such as the sky and the mosque. He repeats this.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator directs the child’s pointing toward what is good and names it for him, thereby establishing that his first expression is of the meanings of good, so that the soul is led by it.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices with love at the child’s pointing toward what is good, so that the emotion of his expression becomes bound to an atmosphere of good.
Through sincerity: By directing the child’s pointing, the educator intends to acquaint him with good for the sake of Allaah, not to train him to draw attention to himself.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator directs the child’s pointing toward what Allaah loves, such as the sky and the mosque, and turns it away from what He detests, so that he gives expression to the love of good.
Through patience: The educator repeats the directing of the child’s pointing and the naming of what he points to, with patience and gentleness, until he grows accustomed to expressing what is good.
Through sincere counsel: The educator directs the child’s pointing and his naming of what is beneficial as a role model and with gentleness, so that he counsels him by his own state to express what is good.
Through the regulation of time: The educator seizes the times of the child’s interaction to name what is beneficial, thereby investing the moments of his attentiveness in instilling beneficial expression.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s pointing from being habituated to pointing toward what is harmful, thereby establishing an expression of good from its very outset.
3. The Utterance of the First Words.
Method of direction: He is taught the word “Allaah” gently alongside “papa” and “mama,” so that the name of Allaah is among the first things his tongue utters.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that speech is a blessing from Allaah, so he teaches the child the word “Allaah” alongside his first words. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s uttering the word of remembrance with a joy conjoined with love. He intends to make remembrance beloved to him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator teaches the child “Allaah,” “papa,” and “mama” gently. He repeats that daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator meets the child’s utterance with cheerfulness and encouragement. He keeps to that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator teaches the child the word “Allaah” alongside his first words, thereby establishing that the first thing he utters is the name of the One to whom the soul is led.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s uttering the word of remembrance with a joy conjoined with love, so that the emotion of his first speech becomes bound to intimacy with Allaah.
Through sincerity: By teaching the child the words of remembrance, the educator intends to devote his tongue to Allaah, not to boast of his early eloquence.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes the words of remembrance beloved to the child and keeps him away from ugly speech, so that his tongue is raised upon what Allaah loves.
Through patience: The educator repeats the teaching with patience and perseverance until the child utters the good word, and he does not rush.
Through sincere counsel: The educator teaches the child the good word as a loving role model, so that he counsels him by his own state that his first utterance be a remembrance of Allaah.
Through the regulation of time: The educator sets aside regular times for repeated teaching, thereby investing the best of times so that the child may utter what is good.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is careful not to teach the child bad speech that is found charming, thereby guarding his budding tongue from the words of the people of falsehood.
4. Waving, Clapping, and Imitating Movements.
Method of direction: The raising of the hands in supplication is imitated before him, so that he imitates it by his innate disposition, and his first movements become bound to the forms of worship.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that the child’s movements be bound to worship, so he imitates before him the raising of the hands in supplication. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s imitation with a love conjoined with gratitude. He intends to bind his movements to good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator supplicates while raising his hands before the child so that he imitates him. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator gently moves the child’s hands in supplication. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator imitates before the child the raising of the hands in supplication so that he imitates him, thereby establishing that his movements are directed toward worship, so that the soul is led by them.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s imitation with a love conjoined with gratitude, so that the emotion of his movements becomes bound to an atmosphere of good.
Through sincerity: By habituating the child to the movements of good, the educator intends to raise him upon them for the sake of Allaah, not to show off before people.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator habituates the child to movements Allaah loves, such as raising the hand in supplication, and turns him away from movements of frivolity, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: The educator repeats teaching the child the movements of good with patience until he masters imitating them, and he does not grow weary.
Through sincere counsel: The educator teaches the child the movements of good as a practical role model, so that he counsels him by his own state and he imitates him in the good deed.
Through the regulation of time: The educator repeats teaching the movements of good at regular times, so that his imitation of them takes firm root through perseverance.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is wary lest the child imitate movements of frivolity or evil that Satan adorns, thereby guarding what he imitates from its very outset.
5. Precise Grasping and Attempting to Feed Oneself.
Method of direction: His attempts are opened with the invocation of Allaah’s name and he is praised gently, so that eating develops in him conjoined with the name of Allaah.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that provision is from Allaah, so he opens the child’s meal with the invocation of Allaah’s name. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s attempt with a love conjoined with gratitude. He intends to bind his eating to the remembrance of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator invokes Allaah’s name before feeding the child and praises Him afterward. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator gently assists the child in eating along with the invocation of Allaah’s name. He keeps to that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator habituates the child to the invocation of Allaah’s name before eating, thereby establishing that provision is from Allaah, so that his soul is led to attributing blessings to Him.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s attempt to eat by himself with a joy conjoined with gratitude, so that his emotion becomes bound to the praise of the Provider (al-Razzaaq).
Through sincerity: By habituating the child to the etiquettes of eating, the educator intends to prepare him to eat thankful to Allaah, not merely for the sake of independence.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator habituates the child to eating the wholesome that Allaah has made lawful and keeps him away from the foul, so that he grows familiar with what Allaah loves of food and etiquette.
Through patience: The educator is patient with the child’s disorder in learning to eat and directs him gently, so he is neither harsh nor hasty for his mastery.
Through sincere counsel: The educator directs the child in learning to eat with gentleness rather than harshness as a role model, so that he counsels him by his own state to proceed unhurriedly and with regard for his stage.
Through the regulation of time: The educator organizes the times of the child’s meals and trains him therein with deliberateness, so that he masters eating at an organized time free of disorder.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator keeps away from the child what is harmful for him to eat and habituates him to the invocation of Allaah’s name by which Satan slinks away from his food.
6. Understanding Simple Words and Commands.
Method of direction: He is addressed with good, simple words conjoined with tenderness, and he hears “al-hamdu lillaah” and “bismillaah” at their appropriate occasions, so that he understands them as his perception grows.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator addresses the child with good words he understands, conjoined with remembrance. He repeats that so that he may understand as he grows.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator addresses the child with love and tenderness conjoined with tranquility. He intends to bind his understanding to good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator lets the child hear “al-hamdu lillaah” and “bismillaah” at their appropriate occasions. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator conjoins the speaking of good with a visible act the child understands. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator addresses the child with good words he understands, conjoined with remembrance, thereby establishing an intellect by which he will later understand the command of Allaah, and by which the soul is led.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator addresses the child with love and tenderness conjoined with tranquility, so that the emotion of his understanding becomes bound to an atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity: By habituating the child to understanding commands, the educator intends to prepare him to obey the command of Allaah, not merely to submit to himself.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes the child understand the commands of good and makes them beloved to him, and keeps him away from understanding evil, so that he is raised upon loving what Allaah loves.
Through patience: The educator repeats addressing the child with patience until he understands, and he neither rushes his comprehension nor is harsh.
Through sincere counsel: The educator addresses the child gently until he understands, as a role model, so that he counsels him by his own state with mildness and without rebuking the slowness of his comprehension.
Through the regulation of time: The educator chooses the times of the child’s clarity to address him, thereby investing his wakefulness rather than his heedlessness in making him understand.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is careful not to habituate the child to understanding commands of evil or idle talk, thereby guarding what is imprinted upon his understanding from its very outset.
7. Imitating Simple Actions.
Method of direction: The good act (such as raising the hand in supplication and kissing the mushaf gently) is performed before him so that he imitates it, for imitation at this stage is a gateway of instilling.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that what the child imitates be good, so he performs the good act before him. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s imitation of good with love. He intends to make good beloved to him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator remembers Allaah while performing the good act before the child so that he imitates him. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator performs a prostration or a raising of the hand in supplication before the child so that he imitates him. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator performs the good act before the child, such as prostration, as a symbol so that he imitates it, thereby establishing that what he imitates is good, so that the soul is led by it.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s imitation of good with love, so that the emotion of his imitation becomes bound to an atmosphere of obedience.
Through sincerity: By the goodness of his action before the child, the educator intends to raise him upon good for the sake of Allaah, not to feign before him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator performs before the child the deeds of those whom Allaah loves so that he imitates them, and keeps him away from imitating the people of evil, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: The educator repeats the good act before the child with patience and perseverance until he imitates it, thereby raising his own self upon being a role model.
Through sincere counsel: The educator repeats the good act before the child as a role model, so that he counsels him by his state before his speech and he imitates him in good.
Through the regulation of time: The educator persists in the good act at all his times before the child, so that it is imprinted upon him through constancy.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is wary lest the child imitate from him or from those around him an evil act that Satan adorns, thereby guarding his example before him.
8. Searching for the Hidden Object.
Method of direction: He is played with in a way that develops his perception in an atmosphere of good cheerfulness, so that his budding intelligence is nurtured in a wholesome environment.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator develops the child’s perception in a good environment with cheerfulness conjoined with the invocation of Allaah’s name. He makes his learning in a wholesome atmosphere.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator plays with the child with love and joy conjoined with the remembrance of Allaah. He intends to bind his perception to good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator invokes Allaah’s name and jests with the child with good speech. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator plays with the child by hiding a good thing and revealing it. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator develops the child’s perception with purposeful play, thereby establishing an intellect by which he comprehends the truth, and by which the soul is led to Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator plays with the child with cheerfulness conjoined with love and the invocation of Allaah’s name, so that the emotion of his perception becomes bound to an atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity: By developing the child’s perception, the educator intends to prepare him to know his Lord and work for Him, not to boast of his cleverness.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator binds playing with the child to the good that Allaah loves, so that his perception is raised connected to good.
Through patience: The educator repeats the play with patience until the child’s perception grows, and he neither rushes nor grows weary.
Through sincere counsel: The educator plays with the child with love as a role model, so that he counsels him by his state to develop his perception through purposeful play.
Through the regulation of time: The educator sets aside regular, purposeful times of play, so that his perception grows at a fruitful time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator guards the child’s play from frivolity that Satan exploits, thereby making the development of his perception in an atmosphere of good.
9. Intense Attachment to the Caregiver.
Method of direction: His attachment is met with tenderness and tranquility conjoined with remembrance, so that his first attachment develops sound and secure.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that security is from Allaah, so he meets the child’s attachment with a reassuring presence. He makes his attachment sound.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator meets the child’s attachment with love and tranquility conjoined with faith. He intends that it grow toward the love of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator remembers Allaah and supplicates for the child, gently tending his attachment. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator embraces the child with tenderness and reassures him. He keeps to that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator meets the child’s attachment to him with a reassuring presence, thereby establishing that lasting security is from Allaah, so that his soul is led to attachment to Him.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator meets the child’s attachment with love and tranquility, not anxiety, thereby instilling a sound emotion that grows toward the love of Allaah.
Through sincerity: By caring for the child’s attachment, the educator intends to raise him upon attachment to Allaah, not to enslave the child to himself for his own sake.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes the child’s attachment to him a bridge to a love that gradually ascends toward Allaah, His Messenger, and the people of faith, so that he is raised upon loyalty to good.
Through patience: The educator is patient with the intensity of the child’s attachment and does not become vexed, and he gradually habituates him to patience during his absence.
Through sincere counsel: The educator is gentle with the intensely attached child as a role model, so that he counsels him by his state to habituate him to reassurance rather than anxiety.
Through the regulation of time: The educator habituates the child to a slight absence at gradual times, so that he is trained in patience through the regulation of the moments of separation.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator protects the child’s attachment from deviating into an anxiety that Satan exploits through whispering (waswasah), thereby making it a sound attachment to Allaah.
10. Displaying Affection and Emotion.
Method of direction: His affection is met with love and supplication for him, and Allaah is praised for the blessing of love between hearts.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that love is a blessing from Allaah, so he meets the child’s affection with praise. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator meets the child’s affection with love and supplication conjoined with faith. He intends to instill love for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator supplicates for the child and praises Allaah at his affection. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator returns the child’s affection with an embrace and a tender touch. He keeps to that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator meets the child’s affection with praise of Allaah, thereby establishing that love is a blessing from Allaah directed to Him, so that the soul is led by it.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator meets the child’s affection with love and supplication, thereby instilling a balanced emotion of love for the sake of Allaah.
Through sincerity: By exchanging affection with the child, the educator intends to raise him upon love for the sake of Allaah, not for a worldly purpose.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator directs the child’s affection so that it grows toward the love of Allaah, His Messenger, and the people of faith, so that he is raised upon love for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: The educator returns the child’s affection with perseverance and patience in caring for him, so that his love for good and its people is made firm.
Through sincere counsel: The educator returns the child’s affection as a tender role model, so that he counsels him by his state to bind his love to good and its people.
Through the regulation of time: The educator persists in regular times for displaying affection, so that his love for good is made firm through the regularity of meeting him.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator directs the child’s affection toward the direction of good, so that it is not later turned to an unlawful love adorned by caprice and Satan.
11. Responding to Praise and Encouragement.
Method of direction: He is praised at the good deed by binding it to Allaah’s joy (“Allaah loves you”), so that he is raised upon the understanding that good gladdens Allaah.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that good pleases Allaah, so he praises the child at his good deed by binding it to Allaah. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator praises the child by saying “Allaah loves you” at good, so that he rejoices. He intends to bind his joy to the pleasure of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator says to the child “Well done, Allaah loves you” at good. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator conjoins his praise of the child with a pat or an encouraging embrace. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator praises the child at his good deed by binding it to Allaah, thereby establishing that the return of all merit is to Allaah, so that his soul is led to His pleasure.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator praises the child with balanced joy conjoined with the pleasure of Allaah, thereby instilling an emotion of joy in obedience rather than in mere praise.
Through sincerity: By praising the child, the educator intends to make good beloved to him for the sake of Allaah, and habituates him to work for the pleasure of Allaah, not for the praise of people.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator binds his praise of the child to Allaah’s love for the good deed, so that he is raised upon loving what Allaah loves and His pleasure.
Through patience: The educator praises the child at his patience and perseverance, thereby making patience upon good beloved to him, and he does not praise him for falsehood.
Through sincere counsel: The educator praises the child for his patience and not for falsehood, as a truthful role model, so that he counsels him by his state to bind praise to the truth.
Through the regulation of time: The educator seizes the times of the child’s excellence to praise him therein, thereby investing the moment to consolidate the good character.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is wary of habituating the child to work for praise, lest he open the door of ostentation (riyaa’) that Satan exploits, so he binds his work to the pleasure of Allaah.
12. Displaying Preferences and the Beginning of Choice.
Method of direction: His choice is directed toward what is good, and choices all of which are good are made available to him, so that his will grows within the framework of good.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator directs the child’s choice toward what is good, so he makes available to him choices all of which are good. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s choosing what is good with love. He intends to bind his will to good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator invokes Allaah’s name and makes the good beloved to the child at his choosing. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator makes available to the child good, visible choices. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator makes available to the child choices all of which are good, thereby establishing that his will is directed toward good, so that the soul is led by it.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s choosing what is good with love, thereby instilling a balanced emotion of inclination toward good.
Through sincerity: By directing the child’s choice, the educator intends to raise him upon preferring what pleases Allaah, not merely to enable him to follow his caprice.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes beloved to the child the choosing of what Allaah loves and keeps him away from choosing what He detests, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: The educator trains the child in patience if he does not attain some of what he loves, thereby habituating him to restraining his will gently.
Through sincere counsel: The educator trains the child gently in patience if what he loves escapes him, as a role model, so that he counsels him by his state to restrain his will.
Through the regulation of time: The educator habituates the child to waiting a little while for what he wants, thereby training him in self-restraint by deferring his desire.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator directs the child’s budding will toward good, so he does not habituate him to following everything he craves of what caprice and Satan adorn.
The Fourth Age-Group: From One to Two Years
In it, walking and running predominate in the child, along with the explosion of language, intensive imitation, the beginning of imaginative play, the emergence of will and independence, and the beginning of self-awareness; and among its innate characteristics:
1. Walking, Running, Climbing, and Increased Motor Energy.
Method of direction: His motor energy is directed toward what is beneficial and safe, and Allaah is praised for the blessing of movement, and it is supplicated for him that his feet may walk in the obedience of Allaah.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that strength is a blessing from Allaah, so he directs the child’s energy toward what is beneficial. He supplicates that his feet may walk in obedience.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s movement with a love conjoined with gratitude. He intends to bind his energy to good.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator teaches the child a short remembrance at his movement, such as the invocation of Allaah’s name. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator directs the child’s energy into beneficial, safe movement. He keeps to that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator directs the child’s motor energy toward what is beneficial, thereby establishing that strength is a blessing by which the soul is led to the obedience of Allaah rather than to frivolity.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator restrains the child’s motor impulsiveness gently, thereby transforming his zeal into activity in good rather than disorder.
Through sincerity: By directing the child’s activity, the educator intends to raise him strong, serving his religion for the sake of Allaah, not merely to expend his energy.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator directs the child’s movement toward what Allaah loves of beneficial activity and restrains him from what is harmful, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: The educator is patient with the abundance of the child’s movement and directs it with forbearance, so he neither suppresses it with harshness nor leaves it in vain.
Through sincere counsel: The educator directs the child’s movement with forbearance rather than suppression, as a role model, so that he counsels him by his state to turn his activity toward what is beneficial.
Through the regulation of time: The educator makes available to the child organized times of movement, thereby turning his activity toward a fruitful time free of disorder.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator directs the child’s energy toward the direction of good, so he does not leave it an emptiness that Satan and caprice exploit in frivolity and harm.
2. The Explosion of Language and Learning New Words.
Method of direction: The good words (“bismillaah,” “al-hamdu lillaah,” “Allaahu akbar”) are taught to him and repeated, so that his linguistic lexicon grows with the words of remembrance.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that speech is a blessing from Allaah, so he teaches the child the good words. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s uttering of remembrance with love. He intends to make the words of remembrance beloved to him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator teaches the child “bismillaah,” “al-hamdu lillaah,” and “Allaahu akbar” and repeats them. He persists in that daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator meets the child’s uttering of remembrance with cheerfulness and encouragement. He keeps to that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator teaches the child the good words and the words of remembrance, thereby establishing a tongue that utters that by which the soul is led to Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s uttering of the good word with love, so that the emotion of his speech becomes bound to intimacy with remembrance.
Through sincerity: By teaching the child remembrance, the educator intends to devote his tongue to Allaah, not to boast of his eloquence.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator makes the words of remembrance and good speech beloved to the child and keeps him away from ugly speech, so that his tongue is raised upon what Allaah loves.
Through patience: The educator repeats the teaching of the good word with patience until it takes firm root in the child’s tongue, and he does not grow weary.
Through sincere counsel: The educator teaches the child the good word as a role model, so that he counsels him by his state to fill his tongue with the remembrance of Allaah.
Through the regulation of time: The educator persists in the teaching at regular times, so that the good takes firm root in his tongue through perseverance.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator is careful lest the child pick up bad speech that is found charming, thereby guarding his tongue from what Satan adorns.
3. Intensive Imitation of Adults.
Method of direction: Care is taken that his role model in movement and speech be righteous, and good is performed before him (prayer, remembrance, the basmalah), so that he imitates it by his innate disposition.
First: Addressing it through purging
The educator establishes that his role model be righteous, so he performs good before the child. He repeats that.
Second: Addressing it through purification
The educator rejoices at the child’s imitation of good with love. He intends to make good beloved to him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the tongue
The educator remembers Allaah and says the basmalah before the child so that he imitates him. He repeats that.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — formation of the limbs
The educator prays and remembers Allaah before the child so that he imitates the acts of worship. He persists in that.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the seeking of knowledge: The educator makes his example before the child righteous, thereby establishing that what he imitates is good, by which the soul is led to Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s imitation of good with love, so that the emotion of his emulation becomes bound to an atmosphere of obedience.
Through sincerity: By the goodness of his example, the educator intends to raise him upon good for the sake of Allaah, not to feign before him one hour and contradict it another.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The educator performs before the child the deeds of those whom Allaah loves — prayer and remembrance — so that he imitates them, and keeps him away from the example of evil, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: The educator persists in the good example with patience until the child’s imitation of good takes firm root, and he does not cease.
Through sincere counsel: The educator persists in the good example as a steadfast role model, so that he counsels him by his state that his imitation of good may take firm root.
Through the regulation of time: The educator consolidates the good example at all his times, so that the child’s emulation takes firm root through perseverance rather than interruption.
