Fourthly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He assigns him small real tasks daily (wiping a table, tidying up toys). He praises him for them.
Governance through the branches of veneration (ta3dhiem):
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator links the child’s helping to the love of Allaah, thereby establishing that beneficial work is that by which one is led to the pleasure of Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator rejoices at the child’s helping and instills in him the love of aid and excellence.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to helping for the sake of Allaah and seeking the reward, not for praise, thereby instilling sincerity.
Through love, fear, loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child the aiding of his family and the people of good, which Allaah loves, so that he grows up upon dutifulness and love for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): The educator trains the child in patience and in completing the work and perfecting it.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator trains the child to perfect his work by way of example, counseling him through his own conduct to be excellent in all that he does.
Through the disciplining of time: The educator gives the child sufficient time to perfect his work, thereby accustoming him to excellence rather than to the haste that spoils.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator accustoms the child to activeness in good, so that he does not leave his free time to the laziness that Satan loves.
21. Greater flexibility in play and interaction.
Firstly: Addressing it through purging and refinement (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that flexibility with peers is part of the good character that Allaah loves. He invests it for that.
Secondly: Addressing it through the purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of preferring others over himself. He rejoices before him when he yields in a situation.
Thirdly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “It’s alright, let’s play as you wish” in a concession that Allaah loves. He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to give up what he loves at times for his brother. He praises him for his selflessness with joy.
Governance through the branches of veneration (ta3dhiem):
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator develops the child’s flexibility within the bounds of good, thereby establishing a manner of dealing by which the self is led to the good character that Allaah loves.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator teaches the child to control his feelings in dealings and to be gentle with people.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to good dealings for the sake of Allaah, thereby instilling sincerity.
Through love, fear, loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child gentleness with the people of faith, and teaches him steadfastness upon the truth with the one who opposes it, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): The educator trains the child in patience and in bearing with people in dealings.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator trains the child to bear with people by way of example, counseling him through his own conduct to be forbearing and of good character with them.
Through the disciplining of time: The educator sets aside times of interaction with people for the child, thereby training him in forbearance through practice at the appropriate moment.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator teaches the child that flexibility has no place in the religion of Allaah, so that he does not compromise in a way that pleases Satan and the people of falsehood.
22. Love of independence in some daily tasks.
Firstly: Addressing it through purging and refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator invests the child’s desire for independence to teach him that independence is a form of worship for the sake of Allaah. He explains that in simplified words.
Secondly: Addressing it through the purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart a trust that Allaah is his Helper. He rejoices before him when he places his reliance upon Allaah at the task.
Thirdly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “In the name of Allaah; I place my reliance upon Allaah” before every task. He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He assigns him small independent tasks (fetching his food, putting on his shoes). He praises him for accomplishing them.
Governance through the branches of veneration (ta3dhiem):
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator directs the child’s independence towards reliance upon Allaah together with action, thereby establishing that strength is through Allaah, by which the self is led.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator instills in the child a balanced confidence coupled with a sense of need for Allaah, so that his emotion is formed upon reliance (tawakkul).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to acting independently for the sake of Allaah, thereby instilling sincerity.
Through love, fear, loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child an independence in the good that Allaah loves, and keeps him away from an independence in disobedience, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience (sabr): The educator trains the child in patience in perfecting his tasks independently.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator trains the child to perfect his tasks independently by way of example, counseling him through his own conduct to rely on himself in what he is able to do.
Through the disciplining of time: The educator sets for the child tasks that he accomplishes by himself at their proper times, thereby accustoming him to independence and to the disciplining of his time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator teaches the child not to let his independence drag him towards arrogance and self-sufficiency away from the obedience of Allaah, which Satan makes alluring to him.
23. Showing jealousy or pride in possessions.
Firstly: Addressing it through purging and refinement (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that pride is forbidden and jealousy is blameworthy, and that blessings are from Allaah, given for gratitude. He invests his feeling in guiding him.
Secondly: Addressing it through the purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the humility of being in need of Allaah. He rejoices before him when he attributes the blessing to Allaah rather than to himself.
Thirdly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “This is a blessing from Allaah; praise be to Allaah” instead of pride. He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him at times to give away to others that of which he boasts. He makes almsgiving a habit.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator teaches the child that the true Owner and Giver is Allaah, thereby establishing that every blessing comes from Him, so that his soul is led to gratitude rather than boasting.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator governs the child’s pride in his possessions so that it does not become excessive, and instills in him humility.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child not to boast of what he possesses, thereby instilling sincerity and humility toward Allaah.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child the giving and sharing that Allaah loves, and makes hateful to him stinginess and boasting, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience (sabr): The educator trains the child in patience, contentment, and the absence of envy toward what others possess.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator trains the child in contentment by example, counseling him through his own state to be content with what Allaah has granted him and to be grateful for it rather than deeming it little.
Through the governance of time: The educator accustoms the child to being satisfied with the blessing present in his time, so that he does not waste his time in an endless yearning.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator teaches the child that boasting and stinginess are among Satan’s adornments, and so endears to him gratitude and giving.
24. At times, the ability to discern the intention behind an action.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the child that the intention is more important than the action in the sight of Allaah. He invests the child’s awareness of this in his instruction.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of sincerity. He rejoices before him at a deed done for Allaah alone.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I intend this for Allaah” before his deeds. He repeats it with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to perform a deed that he conceals from people at least once (a secret act of charity). He praises him for his sincerity.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator invests the child’s ability to discern intention to teach him that the pivot of every deed is the intention, so that his soul is led to making it sincere for Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator instills in the child love for the righteous intention and hatred for the evil one, so that his emotions are formed upon what is good.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to reviewing his intention and making it sincere for Allaah, thereby instilling the very root of sincerity.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child the good intention that Allaah loves, and makes hateful to him the evil intention, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): The educator teaches the child patience in correcting his intention and watching over it.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator teaches the child to correct his intention by example, counseling him through his own state to make his deeds sincere for Allaah and to watch over his heart.
Through the governance of time: The educator reminds the child to summon the intention before his deed, so that he assigns to every span of time an intention that sets it aright.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator teaches the child that Satan corrupts intentions through ostentation (riyaa’), and so accustoms him to correcting them for Allaah.
25. The love of displaying what one has accomplished before others.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that the best of accomplishments is that which pleases Allaah, even if it remains hidden from people. He invests his enthusiasm in guiding him.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the concealed deed. He rejoices before him at a hidden righteous act.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “Allaah sees my deed” instead of displaying it. He instills this in him in place of boasting.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to perform a righteous deed of which he informs no one. He praises him for it in private.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator directs the child’s desire to display his accomplishment toward attributing the merit to Allaah, thereby establishing that success comes from Him, by which the soul is led to gratitude.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator governs the child’s joy at displaying his accomplishment so that it does not turn into conceit (3udjb), and instills in him humility.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to work for Allaah rather than to display his deed to people, thereby instilling sincerity and guarding against ostentation (riyaa’).
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child the concealment of the deed that Allaah loves, and makes hateful to him showing off, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): The educator teaches the child patience in concealing some of his deeds, seeking reward (ihtisaab).
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator teaches the child to conceal some of his deeds, seeking reward, by example, counseling him through his own state to seek the Face of Allaah rather than the notice of people.
Through the governance of time: The educator sets aside for the child private times of goodness, such as hidden remembrance (dhikr), thereby accustoming him to filling his time for Allaah alone.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator teaches the child that the love of prominence is a gateway to ostentation which Satan exploits, and so endears to him sincerity.
26. The development of the capacity for long-term recollection of events.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator invests the child’s memory in teaching him hadiths and transmitted supplications. He connects his memorization to pleasing Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for memorizing the words of Allaah and His Messenger. He rejoices before him when he recalls a long-learned remembrance.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to recall a verse or a remembrance he learned long ago. He repeats this with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He makes the memorization of the Qur’an a part of his day. He keeps at it with him gently and with praise.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator employs the child’s memory for memorizing the Qur’an and the Sunnah, thereby establishing a store by which the soul is led to goodness.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator connects the goodness the child memorizes with joy and love, so that his memory becomes bound to an atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to memorize for Allaah and to act upon it rather than to show off, thereby instilling sincerity.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator has the child memorize what Allaah loves, and keeps him away from memorizing idle and false talk, so that his memory grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience (sabr): The educator trains the child in patience in memorization and long-term review.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator trains the child in memorization and review by example, counseling him through his own state to persevere with the Book of Allaah.
Through the governance of time: The educator sets aside regular times for memorization and review, so that what is memorized becomes firmly rooted through consistency in its appointed time.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator fills the child’s memory with goodness, leaving in it no void for Satan to fill with falsehood.
27. Seeking logical explanations for commands.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that Allaah’s commands contain wisdom, even if it is hidden. He invests his curiosity to teach him submission (tasliem).
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart submission to Allaah. He rejoices before him at an act of obedience rendered without dispute.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instills in him the saying “We hear and we obey” upon the prescribed commands. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to carry out a small prescribed command without delay. He praises him for his promptness.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator answers the child’s question (“Why were we commanded?”) with wisdom, while grounding submission to Allaah, thereby establishing that the intellect serves the revelation, by which the soul is led.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator instills in the child a tranquil trust in Allaah’s wisdom in His command, so that his emotions are formed upon contentment.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to submit to Allaah’s command for Allaah’s sake while perceiving the wisdom, thereby instilling sincerity.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child compliance with Allaah’s command out of love, and teaches him that submission is among the necessary concomitants of love, so that he is raised upon love for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): The educator answers the child’s questions with patience, and teaches him submission where intellects fall short.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator answers the child’s questions by example, counseling him through his own state to submit to Allaah where intellects fall short.
Through the governance of time: The educator seizes the moments of the child’s questioning to teach him submission, thereby investing his curiosity without wearying his mind.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator fortifies the child against a whispering, cast by Satan, that would make him reject Allaah’s command for want of understanding its wisdom.
28. Being influenced by role models outside the scope of the family (the teacher, friends).
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the child that the true role model is one who helps him toward Allaah, not one who diverts him from Him. He chooses righteous role models for him.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions. He keeps them ever present in his memory.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I love the Prophet ﷺ, I love the Companions.” He repeats it with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He imitates with him a deed from the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ (breaking the fast with dates, the tooth-stick [siwaak]). He makes this a natural disposition.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator directs the child toward a righteous role model — a teacher and virtuous company — thereby establishing an emulation by which the soul is led to goodness.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator instills in the child love for the people of goodness and the emulation of them, so that his emotions are formed upon what is good.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to emulate the righteous for Allaah’s sake and not out of mere admiration, thereby instilling sincerity.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child the righteous role model and warns him against the evil role model, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): The educator monitors the child’s role models with patience and care and guides him gently.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator monitors the child’s role models with care by example, counseling him through his own state to choose those he emulates from among the people of goodness.
Through the governance of time: The educator monitors at all times those whom the child mixes with and emulates, thereby safeguarding his time from an evil role model.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator safeguards the child from evil role models that Satan adorns within his surroundings and his media.
29. Readiness to practice the prescribed acts of worship.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the child the pillars of Islam and prepares him for them. He invests his readiness to bring him into worship.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the prayer, fasting, and the Qur’an. He rejoices before him when he shows eagerness toward them.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He teaches him the recitation of al-Faatihah and the remembrances of the prayer. He asks him to repeat them daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He keeps him at prayer alongside himself, even if only a brief prostration. He trains him in ablution (wudoe’) and some of the prayers.
Governance through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the soul and the pursuit of knowledge: The educator prepares the child for worship such as the prayer, thereby establishing that the soul’s ultimate purpose is the worship of Allaah, toward which it is led.
Through the leadership of the emotions: The educator instills in the child love for worship and intimacy with it, so that his emotions are formed upon loving obedience rather than finding it burdensome.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): The educator accustoms the child to perform worship purely for Allaah, thereby instilling the very root of its acceptance.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The educator endears to the child the worship that Allaah loves, and teaches him that it is to be done according to the guidance of His Messenger ﷺ, so that he is raised upon love and following (ittibaa3).
Through patience (sabr): The educator trains the child in patience in learning worship and performing it gradually.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): The educator trains the child in learning worship by example, counseling him through his own state to perform worship according to the guidance of the Sunnah, gradually.
Through the governance of time: The educator accustoms the child to the times of worship such as the prayer, gradually, thereby binding his worship to its appointed times from an early age.
Through knowing the enemies: The educator teaches the child that Satan discourages from worship and whispers within it, and so accustoms him to seeking refuge (isti3aadhah) and to perseverance.
The age group from seven to nine years
The application of the governance of time in this age group through the four tracks (which the educator embodies and directs):
Through purging (tasfiyah): He is taught that time is a blessing from Allaah for which he will be questioned, and that the prayer has an appointed time, and the time of work is distinguished for him from the time of play; for he has reached the age of discernment (tamyiez) and so is addressed with the value of time.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him an ever-present awareness that Allaah sees how he spends his time, and the prayer times are linked to the veneration of Allaah, and the seizing of time in what is beneficial is made beloved to him.
Through the training of the tongue: He is trained to abandon idle talk and superfluous speech, and to engage in remembrance (dhikr) during his free time, and he is praised when he seizes his time well.
Through the training of the limbs: He is commanded to pray at its time (at seven) gently and gradually, and is accustomed to a simple schedule for his day (prayer, study, play, early sleep), and to seizing the early morning, so that time becomes associated in his mind with appointed times and order.
The application of the virtue of sincere counsel (nasiehah) in this age group through the four tracks (which the educator embodies and directs):
Through purging (tasfiyah): He is taught the pillars of sincere counsel and that it is a part of the religion, and that counsel is a private matter, not a public exposure, and he is trained to accept counsel from his parents without obstinacy; for he has reached the age of discernment and so is addressed with instruction and command, gently.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled the sincerity of counsel for Allaah and the desire of goodness for his siblings and companions, and sincere counsel is linked to the veneration of Allaah, the awareness of His watching, and modesty before Him.
Through the training of the tongue: He is trained to counsel with a good word in private and to enjoin the right gently, in emulation of Luqmaan’s counsel to his son: he opened it with the tender address ﴿O my son﴾ [Luqmaan 31:13] and ordered it with wisdom and gentleness.
Through the training of the limbs: He is commanded to pray gently and gradually (at seven), and is trained to act upon what he counsels and to conceal his brother’s fault, and is reminded to preserve the limits of Allaah: “Preserve Allaah and He will preserve you” (Narrated by al-Tirmidhie (no. 2516), and declared authentic (sahieh) by al-Albaanie).
The most beautiful names of Allaah and their pedagogical application in this age group
Building upon the names of the previous age groups (al-Rahmaan, al-Rahiem, al-Razzaaq, and al-Khaaliq; al-Samie3, al-Basier, al-3Aliem, and al-Malik; al-3Adhiem, al-Kariem, and al-Ghafoer), they are here deepened in a manner suited to the age of discernment and the command to pray, when the child prepares for [religious] accountability (taklief) and his awareness of responsibility matures: so the meanings of [Allaah’s] all-encompassing observance (al-Samie3, al-Basier, al-3Aliem) are carried over from mere knowledge to its necessary corollary of watchfulness (muraaqabah) and reckoning, and what he has learned of [Allaah’s] greatness is linked to the obligation of obedience. Then are added the names of watchfulness, reckoning, wisdom, and justice, which build the responsible conscience.
The name of Allaah: al-Raqieb (the All-Watchful)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Raqieb,” which by its full correspondence denotes the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of watchfulness and all-encompassing observance; He is the Preserver from whom nothing is absent, the One aware of things outward and of innermost consciences, the One who oversees every soul according to what it has earned.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of perpetual watchfulness.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, hearing, sight, life, and power (for the All-Watchful is All-Knowing, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Powerful); Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And ever is Allaah, over all things, an Observer﴾ [al-Ahzaab 33:52], and He said: ﴿And Allaah, over all things, is Witness﴾ [al-Mudjaadilah 58:6].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is All-Watchful over you in your movements and your stillness; He numbers your breaths and your passing thoughts, and with you are angels who record; and this name gathers the fruit of al-Samie3, al-Basier, and al-3Aliem into the meaning of practical watchfulness. So whoever senses Allaah’s watching is ashamed to disobey Him in his seclusion just as he would be ashamed to disobey Him before people.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: the All-Watchful watches your obedience in secret and rewards you for it more greatly than He rewards what is done openly, so be sincere. Warning: He watches your disobedience where there is no watcher from among creation, so there is no escape from His watching.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the child that Allaah is All-Watchful over him in every state, thereby founding in his mind the very root of watchfulness: summoning the awareness of Allaah’s observance before every word and deed.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him watchfulness of Allaah in seclusion and modesty before Him, so that his emotions are formed upon excellence (ihsaan) where no one sees him.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to calling his tongue to account and to being ever mindful that the All-Watchful numbers his speech, so that he is raised upon guarding the tongue out of watchfulness.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to abandon disobedience in his seclusion (even if slight) out of a sense of Allaah’s watching, and is charged with the prayer while being mindful that Allaah watches him in it, so that his limbs act in accordance with watchfulness.
The name of Allaah: al-Hasieb (the Reckoner)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Hasieb,” which by its full correspondence denotes two inseparable meanings: that He is the One who calls His servants to account for their deeds, and the One who suffices whoever relies upon Him; He is the One who numbers deeds and requites them, and He is the sufficiency of His servant and the One who suffices him.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the two attributes of numbering and requital, and of sufficiency for the one who relies upon Him.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, justice, power, and self-sufficiency; Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And sufficient is Allaah as Accountant﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:6], and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah is ever, over all things, an Accountant﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:86].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah calls His servants to account on the Day of Resurrection for the smallest speck and the thinnest filament, wronging not so much as an atom’s weight; and whoever believes that he will be called to account for his deed calls himself to account before he is called to account. And He, glorified is He, is the sufficiency of whoever relies upon Him, so whoever has Allaah as his sufficiency is sufficed.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: whoever takes Allaah as his sufficiency, He suffices him and calls him to an easy reckoning by His mercy, so make Him your sufficiency. Warning: the reckoning is inevitably coming, and whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished, so prepare for a Day on which you will be called to account.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that every deed is numbered and will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection, thereby founding in his mind the linkage of deed to requital, and that nothing is lost.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him the calling of the self to account before the deed and after it, and preparation for the Day of Reckoning, so that his emotions are formed upon watchfulness and initiative.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to weigh his words before uttering them and to call himself to account for his idle talk, so that his tongue is raised upon caution.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to call himself to account throughout his day (“what good did I do and what wrong did I commit?”), and to rectify wherein he fell short, so that his limbs act in accordance with the ever-present awareness of the reckoning.
The name of Allaah: al-Hakiem (the All-Wise)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Hakiem,” which by its full correspondence denotes the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of wisdom; and it is the placing of things in their proper places and the perfecting of creation and command, so that He creates nothing in vain nor legislates anything false.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of wisdom, and the perfection of knowledge upon which it is built.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, power, justice, and mercy (for His wisdom requires the perfecting of everything for a benefit); Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And He is the Wise, the Acquainted [with all]﴾ [al-An3aam 6:18].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Everything Allaah has created is for a wisdom, and everything He has commanded or forbidden is for a wisdom—known to whoever knows it and unknown to whoever is ignorant of it; so when the servant is certain of Allaah’s wisdom, he submits to His command even if its wisdom is hidden from him, and is set at ease with His decree even if he does not understand its aspect. And this cultivates in the child submission rather than objection.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: the commands of the All-Wise are all good and benefit, so obeying Him is the very essence of wisdom, and in it lies your happiness. Warning: opposing the All-Wise is folly and harm to oneself, so whoever rejects His ruling has rejected wisdom itself.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child’s question “Why?” is answered by [affirming] that Allaah has in every command a wisdom, and he is taught some of the wisdoms of the acts of worship, thereby founding in his mind that the religion in its entirety is wisdom and benefit.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him a tranquil trust in Allaah’s wisdom and submission to His command, so that his emotions are formed upon contentment rather than objection.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to say “We hear and we obey” upon a command, and to ask about the wisdom as one seeking guidance, not as one objecting, so that his tongue is raised upon submission.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to comply with the prescribed command even if he does not fully grasp its wisdom, out of trust in the wisdom of the Commander, so that his limbs act in accordance with submission to the All-Wise.
The name of Allaah: al-3Adl (the Just)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): Allaah is described with justice; He is the One who is never unjust in His ruling nor wrongs in His decree; His deeds are all justice, His ruling is all equity, placing everything in its rightful place.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the perfection of justice in His ruling and His decree, and the negation of injustice from Him.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, wisdom, and power (for He does not wrong owing to His knowledge and His self-sufficiency), and it entails that everything He has decreed is justice even if its aspect is hidden; Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf 18:49], and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom’s weight﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:40].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah has forbidden injustice for Himself and has made it forbidden among His servants; on the Day of Resurrection He will exact retribution for the wronged from the one who wronged them, even for the hornless ewe from the horned one; so whoever knows the justice of Allaah deals fairly of his own accord, wrongs no one, and is set at ease that his right will never be lost.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: Allaah’s justice guarantees that no right of yours will be lost nor any deed of yours squandered, so be at ease with His justice. Warning: His justice exacts retribution from the wrongdoer even after a time, so beware of wronging anyone, for the supplication of the wronged is answered.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught — at the age of grasping fairness — that Allaah is Just and wrongs no one, and that every act of injustice will be recompensed by retribution, thereby founding in his mind the scale of truth.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him love of justice and hatred of injustice, and a tranquil trust in Allaah’s justice in what is hidden, so that his emotions are formed upon fairness and contentment.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to speaking the truth even against himself, and not to lie in support of his own falsehood, so that his tongue is raised upon justice.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in fairness in his dealings with his siblings and peers, in restoring rights, and in refraining from transgression, so that his limbs act in accordance with love of justice.
The name of Allaah: al-Hakam (the Judge)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Hakam,” which by its full correspondence denotes the Essence of Allaah, the One who judges between His creation, to whom belongs all judgment; He is the One who decrees and adjudicates between the servants with truth—none can repel His ruling nor overturn His decree.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of judging and adjudicating.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, justice, wisdom, and power, and that His ruling is executed throughout the universe, in [His] law (shar3) and in [His] decree (qadar).
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Then is it other than Allaah I should seek as judge while it is He who has revealed to you the Book explained in detail?﴾ [al-An3aam 6:114], and He said: ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾ [al-A3raaf 7:87].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: All judgment belongs to Allaah: His legislative judgment in His command and prohibition, His decreed judgment in His governance, and His requiting judgment on the Day when He adjudicates between all creatures; so whoever is content with Allaah’s judgment in law, and submits to His judgment in decree, is saved. So when the child knows that Allaah is the Judge, he refers his disputes to His law and does not refer them to his own whim nor to a custom that contravenes the truth.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: Allaah’s judgment is all justice and wisdom, so whoever refers his disputes to Him and is content with His ruling attains happiness. Warning: whoever rejects Allaah’s judgment or refers his disputes to other than Him has contended with Allaah over the most exclusive of His rights.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that judgment and adjudication belong to Allaah alone, and that what He has ruled in His Book is the truth, thereby founding in his mind the referral of disputes to the law of Allaah.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him love of Allaah’s judgment, contentment with it, and submission to it, so that his emotions are formed upon compliance rather than objection.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to say “the judgment of Allaah” and “we are content with Allaah as judge,” so that his tongue is raised submitting to Allaah’s judgment.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to refer his disputes to truth and fairness, and not to seek arbitration from whim, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Judge.
The name of Allaah: al-Hafiedh (the Preserver)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Hafiedh,” which by its full correspondence denotes the Essence of Allaah, the Preserver of all things; He preserves the deeds of His servants and numbers them, He preserves His creation and cares for them, and He preserves from evils whoever He takes into His protection.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the two attributes of preservation-through-numbering and preservation-through-care.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, power, and mercy, and that whoever preserves the limits of Allaah, Allaah preserves him.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is, over all things, Guardian﴾ [Hoed 11:57], and He said: ﴿But Allaah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful﴾ [Yoesuf 12:64]. And the Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn 3Abbaas while he was a boy: “Preserve Allaah and He will preserve you; preserve Allaah and you will find Him before you” (Narrated by al-Tirmidhie (no. 2516), who said it is hasan sahieh, and declared authentic (sahieh) by al-Albaanie).
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah preserves the servant’s deeds, the minute of them and the momentous, so that nothing of them is lost, and He preserves in his religion, his self, and his family whoever preserves His limits; and the meaning of “Preserve Allaah” is: preserve His commands, His prohibitions, and His limits, and Allaah will preserve you. So when the child knows that his Lord is the Preserver, he guards his limbs against the forbidden so that Allaah may preserve him.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: whoever preserves Allaah through obedience to Him, Allaah preserves him in his religion and his worldly life, so preserve His limits and He will preserve you. Warning: whoever squanders the limits of Allaah, Allaah abandons him and consigns him to himself, and nothing preserves him.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that Allaah preserves his deed and preserves whoever obeys Him, thereby founding in his mind that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed: preserve Allaah and He will preserve you.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him a tranquil trust in Allaah’s preservation and a love that Allaah should preserve him, so that his emotions are formed upon watchfulness and reliance (tawakkul).
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to the remembrances of preservation (such as Aayat al-Kursie and the protective chapters [al-mu3awwidhaat]) in the morning and evening, so that his tongue is raised flourishing with the seeking of Allaah’s preservation.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to guard his limbs against the forbidden (guarding the tongue, the sight, and the hand) so that Allaah may preserve him, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Preserver.
The name of Allaah: al-Shahied (the Witness)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Shahied,” which by its full correspondence denotes the Essence of Allaah, the One aware of all things with the awareness of One who witnesses matters and is present at them; no word and no deed is absent from Him, and He is Witness over His servants for their deeds.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of witnessing and complete awareness.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails knowledge, hearing, and sight, and that He will bear witness over the servants on the Day of Resurrection for what they did.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allaah, over all things, is Witness﴾ [al-Mudjaadilah 58:6], and He said: ﴿Indeed Allaah is ever, over all things, a Witness﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:33].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is a present Witness who sees, hears, and knows; He witnesses your deed as you perform it, and He will bear witness against you on the Day of Resurrection; and this gathers the fruit of al-Samie3, al-Basier, and al-Raqieb into the meaning of witnessing that necessitates modesty. So when the child is certain that Allaah is Witness over him, he is ashamed that He should witness him committing anything vile.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: the Witness witnesses your good deed and rewards you and honors you on the Day when He bears witness, so do good while knowing that He witnesses you. Warning: He witnesses your evil, and your own limbs will bear witness against you, so beware that He should witness you doing what will grieve you on the Day of Meeting.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the child that Allaah is a present Witness over everything he does, thereby founding in his mind that his deeds are witnessed and recorded.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him watchfulness of the Witness and modesty before Him, so that his emotions are formed upon excellence (ihsaan) in private and in public.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to truthful testimony and to speaking the truth because Allaah is Witness, so that his tongue is raised truthful.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to abandon whatever it would grieve him for Allaah to witness against him on the Day of Resurrection, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Witness.
The name of Allaah: al-Mudjieb (the Responsive)
The meaning and its three significations:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-Mudjieb,” which by its full correspondence denotes the Essence of Allaah, the One who answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, and responds to His servants’ request, near to whoever calls upon Him.
The signification of inclusion (tadammun): It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of answering supplication.
The signification of implication (iltizaam): It entails hearing, knowledge, power, and generosity, and that He is near to those who call upon Him, answering them.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive﴾ [Hoed 11:61], and He said: ﴿And your Lord says, “Call upon Me; I will respond to you”﴾ [Ghaafir 40:60].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah answers the call of whoever calls upon Him, and He loves that His servant should ask of Him and importune Him; He answers and so grants his request, or averts from him an evil, or stores up for him a greater good. So when the child knows — while he is at the age of learning supplication — that his Lord is Responsive, he supplicates Him abundantly and does not turn in his needs to any other than Him.
Encouragement and warning (targhieb and tarhieb): Encouragement: the Responsive answers whoever calls upon Him and does not turn his hands back empty, so supplicate Him abundantly, confident of the answer. Warning: whoever is too proud to supplicate Him, or calls upon another for that which none but Allaah has power over, has turned away from the Responsive.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that Allaah hears the supplication and answers it, and that supplication is to be directed to Allaah alone, thereby founding in his mind that the Fulfiller of needs is Allaah.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him love of supplication, confidence in the answer, and [a sense of] utter need of the Responsive, so that his emotions are formed upon attachment to Allaah.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to supplicating for his small needs with his tongue (in his prayer and at his bedtime), so that his tongue is raised supplicating the Responsive.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to raise his hands in supplication and to observe good manners in it, and not to ask of other than Allaah for that over which none but He has power, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Responsive.
The name of Allaah: al-3Afuww (the Pardoner)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by correspondence: “al-3Afuww” (the Pardoner) is that which signifies, by way of full correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who is abundant in pardon, who erases sins and effaces them until it is as though they had never been. Pardon (3afw) is more emphatic than forgiveness (maghfirah), for forgiveness is a covering (satr) whereas pardon is an effacement (mahw).
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of effacement and overlooking.
Signification by entailment: It entails mercy, forbearance, generosity, and power, and that He loves pardon from His servants.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿For those it is expected that Allaah will pardon them, and Allaah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:99]; and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ [al-Hadjdj 22:60].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah pardons and so erases the sin from the record, and does not content Himself with merely covering it; and among His [attributes] is that He loves pardon, so He loves that His servant pardon whoever has wronged him. So when the child knows that his Lord is the Pardoner, he hopes for His pardon and pardons his brothers in emulation of Him.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement (targhieb): that the Pardoner erases your sins if you ask Him, and He loves from you that you pardon people, so He rewards you [for it]. Admonition (tarhieb): that whoever’s breast is so constricted that he does not pardon people has contravened a character trait that Allaah loves.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that Allaah pardons and erases sins, and that He loves those who pardon, so that hope and the trait of pardon are established in his mind.
Through purification (tazkiyah): The sentiment of pardoning and of overlooking the wrongdoer is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon magnanimity rather than revenge.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught [to say] “O Allaah, pardon me” and “may Allaah pardon you” when wronged, so that his tongue is nurtured upon seeking pardon and bestowing it.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained — when someone wrongs him — to pardon and to restrain revenge, so that his limbs act in accordance with the love of the Pardoner.
The Name of Allaah: al-Tawwaab
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Tawwaab” (the Ever-Accepting of repentance) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who abundantly accepts repentance, who brings His servant back from disobedience to obedience, turning to him first by granting him the enabling grace [to repent] and finally by [His] acceptance.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of accepting repentance and granting success in it.
Signification by entailment: It entails mercy, forgiveness, forbearance, and generosity, and that the door of repentance is open.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:37]; and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:222].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah accepts the repentance of the repentant every time he returns, and He rejoices in it; and He loves those who repent often, who frequently return to Him. So when the child errs, he is taught to repent, and [taught] that repentance effaces what came before it, so that he neither despairs nor deems the act of returning too slight.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Ever-Accepting of repentance accepts your repentance and loves you if you repent often, so hasten to it. Admonition: that repentance has as its condition desisting [from the sin] and remorse, so do not procrastinate over it, nor persist [in sin] relying [merely] upon His acceptance.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah accepts repentance and loves the one who repents, so that the remedy of error through returning [to Allaah] is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of remorse and returning, and the love of repentance, is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon hastening to set matters right.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught [to say] “I repent to Allaah” together with remorse, so that his tongue grows up ever-returning [to Allaah].
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to follow error with practical repentance and to repair what he has damaged, so that his limbs act in accordance with the love of the Ever-Accepting of repentance.
The Name of Allaah: al-Haliem
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Haliem” (the Forbearing) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described by perfect forbearance; and it is the granting of respite and the not hastening to punish despite perfect power to do so.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of forbearance coupled with power.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, mercy, and generosity.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And know that Allaah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:235]; and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease [to exist] … Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [Faatir 35:41].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah sees the disobedient defying Him openly with acts of disobedience, yet He grants them respite and provides for them in hope of their repentance; and had He willed, He would have seized them. Whoever adorns himself with forbearance masters himself when angered. So when the child is taught the forbearance of Allaah, he becomes gentle, restrains his rage, and does not act in haste.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that Allaah’s forbearance grants you respite so that you may set matters right, so seize His respite through repentance. Admonition: that forbearance is not neglect, so when He seizes the wrongdoer He does not let him escape.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah’s granting of respite is forbearance and not heedlessness, and that restraining rage is the character of the noble, so that self-mastery of one’s impulses is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of forbearance and of restraining rage is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon mastering anger.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to silence when angry and to seeking refuge [in Allaah], so that his tongue grows up forbearing.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to restrain his limbs when angry, so that his limbs act in accordance with the love of the Forbearing.
The Name of Allaah: al-Waasi3
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Waasi3” (the All-Encompassing) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who is vast in His attributes and His acts; vast in knowledge, mercy, forgiveness, giving, and dominion, who encompasses all things.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the vastness of His attributes.
Signification by entailment: It entails knowledge, self-sufficiency, generosity, and power, and that His vastness is bounded by no limit.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allaah is all-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:247]; and He said: ﴿And Allaah is ever Encompassing and Wise﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:130].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: His mercy encompasses all things, His knowledge comprehends all things, and His giving is inexhaustible; so whoever asks of the All-Encompassing is not constricted [in what He grants him]. So when the child knows the vastness of his Lord, he thinks well of Him and does not deem anything of His bounty too much [to ask for].
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that Allaah’s vastness is inexhaustible, so ask of His vastness and do not regard His bounty as scant. Admonition: that whoever constricts himself through thinking ill of Allaah is ignorant of His vastness.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah’s mercy and giving are vast, without limit, so that vastness of hope is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of hope and of thinking well of the All-Encompassing is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon aspiring for His bounty.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to asking Allaah of His vast bounty, so that his tongue grows up hopeful.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to be expansive in his dealings with people and in giving to them, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the All-Encompassing.
The Name of Allaah: al-Fattaah
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Fattaah” (the Opener) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who opens for His servants the doors of His mercy, His provision, and His knowledge, and who judges among His servants with truth and thereby decides between them, and who opens what is locked shut.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the two attributes of opening through provision and mercy, and opening through judgment.
Signification by entailment: It entails knowledge, wisdom, power, and generosity.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And He is the Opener, the Knowing﴾ [Saba’ 34:26]; and He said: ﴿Whatever mercy Allaah opens for people, none can withhold it﴾ [Faatir 35:2].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Opener opens the doors of provision, mercy, relief, and knowledge; what He opens none can shut, and what He shuts none can open besides Him. So when the child knows that his Lord is the Opener, he asks Him for opening in his affairs, his knowledge, and his provision, and does not despair when doors are shut.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Opener opens for you what has become locked shut if you ask Him, so turn to Him in times of hardship. Admonition: that what He has shut none opens besides Him, so do not seek opening from other than Him.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah opens the doors of good and decides with truth, so that the seeking of opening from Allaah is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of hope in the Opener during hardship is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon not despairing.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught [to say] “My Lord, open for me” and “O Allaah, grant us opening”, so that his tongue grows up seeking opening.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to exert the [material] means alongside seeking opening from Allaah, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Opener.
The Name of Allaah: al-Qaabid
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Qaabid” (the Withholder) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who withholds provision, seizes souls, and grips the hearts by His wisdom and justice; He constricts whomever He wills by His effective will.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of withholding with wisdom.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, wisdom, and justice.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is Allaah who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:245].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Withholder withholds provision from whomever He wills, as a trial or out of wisdom, and seizes souls at their appointed terms, and grips the hearts, turning them about; and His withholding is justice and wisdom. So when the child knows that withholding is in Allaah’s hand, he is content with what has been withheld from him, knowing that behind it lies wisdom.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that what the Withholder has withheld from you is for a wisdom and a mercy, so be content with it and think well [of Allaah]. Admonition: that whoever frets over what Allaah has withheld or attributes it to other than Him is ignorant of His wisdom.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that withholding and prevention are in Allaah’s hand with wisdom, so that contentment with His decree is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of contentment and of patience upon being prevented is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon submission.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to [say] “Praise be to Allaah in every state” when prevented [of something], so that his tongue grows up content.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to patience when he misses what he loves, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Withholder.
The Name of Allaah: al-Baasit
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Baasit” (the Expander) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who spreads and enlarges provision for whom He wills, and spreads mercy, and expands hearts with joy and tranquility.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of expansion and enlargement.
Signification by entailment: It entails generosity, self-sufficiency, mercy, and power.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is Allaah who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:245]; and He said: ﴿Allaah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]﴾ [al-Ra3d 13:26].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Expander enlarges provision for whom He wills, and spreads mercy, and expands the breasts; abundance is in His hand alone. So when the child knows that expansion is from Allaah, he thanks Him in times of abundance, does not attribute wealth to his own cleverness, and asks Him to expand his breast.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Expander enlarges [His bounty] upon you if you thank Him and ask Him, so seek His abundance. Admonition: that whoever has abundance spread out for him yet becomes insolent and attributes the bounty to himself has denied the Bestower of favor.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that abundance and expansion are from Allaah, so that thanking the Bestower of favor in times of abundance is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of gratitude upon expansion is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon thankfulness rather than insolence.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to praise and thanks in times of abundance, so that his tongue grows up thankful.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to spread out to people what Allaah has spread out upon him (such as giving and charity), so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Expander.
The Name of Allaah: al-Raafi3
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Raafi3” (the Exalter) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who raises whom He wills through faith, knowledge, and obedience, and who raises the ranks of His allies, and who raises the truth and its people.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of raising with wisdom.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and wisdom, and that true elevation is in His hand.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿[He is] the Exalted in ranks, Owner of the Throne﴾ [Ghaafir 40:15]; and He said: ﴿Allaah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees﴾ [al-Mudjaadilah 58:11].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Exalter raises the people of faith, knowledge, and piety, and raises their ranks in this world and the Hereafter; for true elevation is not by wealth and status but by obedience. So when the child knows that elevation is in Allaah’s hand, he seeks it through its means—faith, knowledge, and deeds—not through arrogance and ostentation.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Exalter raises whoever humbles himself before Him and obeys Him, so seek elevation through obedience. Admonition: that whoever seeks elevation through arrogance and disobedience, Allaah abases him.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that true elevation is through faith, knowledge, and obedience, not through worldly things, so that the [proper] scale of elevation is established in his mind.
Through purification: The love of elevation before Allaah through obedience is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon seeking its heights.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to asking Allaah for elevation in both abodes, so that his tongue grows up seeking lofty matters.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained upon the means of elevation—knowledge, deeds, and humility—so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Exalter.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muhyie
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Muhyie” (the Giver of Life) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who gives life to the dead, and revives the earth after its death, and gives life to hearts through faith; the One unique in bestowing life.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of giving life.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and life, and His uniqueness in bringing life into being.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿So observe the effects of the mercy of Allaah - how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed, that [same One] will give life to the dead﴾ [al-Roem 30:50].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah revives the dead earth with rain, so that it brings forth growth after its barrenness, and whoever is able to do that is able to give life to the dead for the resurrection; and He gives life to dead hearts through faith just as He gives life to bodies. So when the child knows that the giving of life is in Allaah’s hand, he becomes certain of the resurrection and asks Him for the life of his heart through faith.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Giver of Life gives life to your heart through faith and resurrects you for bliss, so ask Him for the life of your heart. Admonition: that whoever’s heart has died through disobedience has missed out on the greatest [form of] life.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah gives life to the dead and gives life to the hearts, so that certainty in the resurrection and the seeking of the life of the heart are established in his mind.
Through purification: The love of the life of the heart through faith is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon seeking [that] revival.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught the remembrance of Allaah that gives life to the hearts, so that his tongue grows up flourishing with remembrance.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained upon that which gives life to the heart—obedience and remembrance—so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Giver of Life.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mumiet
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Mumiet” (the Bringer of Death) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who brings death to the living by His wisdom at their appointed terms; the One unique in taking souls, so none brings death besides Him.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of causing death.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, wisdom, and knowledge, and that the appointed terms are in His hand.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾ [al-Najm 53:44]; and He said: ﴿Allaah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [al-Zumar 39:42].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah brings death to creatures at their written appointed terms, neither advancing nor delaying [them]; and death is a certainty upon every soul. So when the child knows that death is in Allaah’s hand and that it is coming inevitably, he prepares for it through righteous deeds and is not deceived by lengthy hopes.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that whoever prepares for death through obedience meets his Lord secure. Admonition: that death comes suddenly, so whoever is heedless of it and is excessive against his own soul, it takes him by surprise in [a state of] heedlessness.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that death is a certainty [that lies] in Allaah’s hand, and that each [person] has an appointed term, so that preparation and the taking of heed are established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of preparing to meet Allaah and of shortening [one’s worldly] hopes is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon hastening to good.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to the remembrance of death and to seeking refuge from an evil end, so that his tongue grows up mindful of the Hereafter.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to hasten to righteous deeds in preparation for death, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Bringer of Death.
The Name of Allaah: al-Baa3ith
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Baa3ith” (the Resurrector) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who resurrects creatures from their graves on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning and the recompense, and who sends the messengers with guidance.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of resurrecting.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and justice, and the inevitability of resurrection for recompense.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And [that] Allaah will resurrect those in the graves﴾ [al-Hadjdj 22:7].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah resurrects those in the graves, [bringing them forth] alive for the reckoning; as He originated them, He restores them; and the resurrection is a certainty in which there is no doubt. So when the child is certain of the resurrection, he knows that there is a Day on which he will be recompensed for his deeds, so he prepares for it and does not reckon that death is the end of the road.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Resurrector resurrects you so that you may be recompensed for your good deeds with the most abundant recompense, so work for that Day. Admonition: that He resurrects you for the reckoning over the weights of atoms, so beware of meeting Him with your evil deeds.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah resurrects the dead for the reckoning, so that certainty in the resurrection and the recompense is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of preparing for the Day of Resurrection is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon working for the Hereafter.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to the remembrance of the Day of Resurrection and belief in it, so that his tongue grows up affirming the Return.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to righteous deeds in preparation for the Day of Resurrection, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Resurrector.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mu3ied
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Mu3ied” (the Restorer) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who restores creation after its perishing as He originated it; for He is the Originator, the Restorer, who restores creation for the resurrection.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of restoration.
Signification by entailment: It entails power and knowledge, and that the One who began creation is able to restore it.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates [creation] and repeats﴾ [al-Buroedj 85:13]; and He said: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ [al-Anbiyaa’ 21:104].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah restores creation after their death as He originated them the first time, and restoration is, in the conception of [human] minds, easier for Him than origination; for whoever originated creation from nothing, its restoration is [all the] more fitting [to affirm]. So when the child knows that Allaah restores creation, he becomes certain of the resurrection and does not deem it far-fetched.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Restorer restores you so that you may meet the reward of your righteous deeds. Admonition: that He restores you for the reckoning, so no one escapes Him; so prepare to meet Him.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The child is taught that Allaah restores creation as He originated them, so that certainty in the restoration and the resurrection is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of certainty in the Return and of preparation for it is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon [good] deeds.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to affirming the resurrection and the restoration, so that his tongue grows up believing in the Return.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to act in accordance with certainty in the restoration and the recompense, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Restorer.
The Name of Allaah: al-Khaafid
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Khaafid” (the Abaser) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who abases whom He wills through humiliation and disgrace by His wisdom and justice; He abases the tyrants, the wrongdoers, and the disbelievers.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of abasing with wisdom.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, justice, and might, and that abasement is in His hand alone.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said, describing the Resurrection: ﴿It will bring down [some] and raise up [others]﴾ [al-Waaqi3ah 56:3], for it is He, glorified is He, who abases some peoples and raises others by His wisdom; ﴿and You abase whom You will﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:26].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Abaser abases the arrogant and the disobedient, so He humiliates them; and He, together with the Exalter, are two paired names, one of which is generally not mentioned except with the other; for in His hand are the raising and the abasing. So when the young person knows that abasement is in Allaah’s hand, he becomes wary of its causes—arrogance and disobedience—and does not fear the abasement of any creature in [the course of] obeying Allaah.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that whoever humbles himself before Allaah, He raises him and does not abase him. Admonition: that the Abaser abases every arrogant one and every wrongdoer, so beware the causes of abasement.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that the abasing and the raising are in Allaah’s hand with wisdom, so that [the truth] that might is through obeying Him and not through arrogance is established in his mind.
Through purification: The fear of the causes of abasement and the love of the causes of elevation are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon humility.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to venerating Allaah and to casting off boastfulness, so that his tongue grows up humble.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to abandon the arrogance and wrongdoing that necessitate abasement, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Abaser.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mu3izz
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Mu3izz” (the Bestower of Honour) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who bestows honour upon whom He wills of His servants through His obedience and His support; for all honour is in His hand, He grants it to whom He wills.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of bestowing honour with wisdom.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, might, and wisdom, and that honour is from Him and not from other than Him.
