The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, “O Allaah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will, and You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will”﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:26].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Bestower of Honour honours whoever obeys Him and takes Him as an ally; and true honour is in obeying Allaah, not in status and wealth. So whoever seeks honour through other than Allaah, Allaah abases him, and whoever seeks it through obeying Him, He honours him. So when the young person knows that honour is from Allaah, he seeks it through faith and piety, and does not debase himself before any creature seeking honour.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Bestower of Honour honours whoever seeks honour through Him and obeys Him, with an honour after which there is no abasement. Admonition: that whoever seeks honour through disobeying Allaah or through allying with His enemies, Allaah abases him.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that all honour is from Allaah through obedience, so that the seeking of honour through faith is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of seeking honour through Allaah is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon [seeking] honour through His obedience.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught [to say] “Honour belongs entirely to Allaah”, so that his tongue grows up honoured through Allaah.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to seek honour through obedience and to not debase himself before other than Allaah, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Bestower of Honour.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mudhill
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Mudhill” (the Humiliator) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who humiliates whom He wills by His justice and wisdom; He humiliates whoever is arrogant, disobeys, and opposes Him, so there is no honour for whomever Allaah humiliates.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of humiliating with justice.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, justice, and might, and that humiliation is in His hand.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:26].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: The Humiliator humiliates whoever is too arrogant to obey Him and opposes His command; and the Bestower of Honour and the Humiliator are two paired names in His hand alone. So when the young person knows that humiliation is in Allaah’s hand, he becomes wary of its causes—arrogance and disobedience—and knows that true abasement is in disobeying Allaah, and true honour is in obeying Him.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that whoever submits to Allaah, He honours him and does not humiliate him. Admonition: that the Humiliator humiliates everyone who is arrogant toward His command or disobeys Him, so beware the causes of humiliation.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that humiliation is in Allaah’s hand for whoever disobeys Him, so that [the truth] that abasement lies in disobedience is established in his mind.
Through purification: The fear of the causes of abasement and the love of submission to Allaah are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon debasing itself before Allaah alone.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to submission to Allaah in his speech, so that his tongue grows up humble before its Lord.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained upon submission to the command of Allaah and the abandonment of arrogance, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Humiliator.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mubdi’
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Mubdi’” (the Originator) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who initiated the creation of things and brought them into being from nothing, at the very outset; for He is the One who begins creation and then restores it.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of origination and bringing into being.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and will, and that the One who began creation is able to restore it.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates [creation] and repeats﴾ [al-Buroedj 85:13]; and He said: ﴿Have they not considered how Allaah begins creation and then repeats it?﴾ [al-3Ankaboet 29:19].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: Allaah began creation from nothing, bringing it into being upon no prior model; and the Originator and the Restorer are two inseparable names: the One who began [creation] is able to restore [it]. So when the young person knows that Allaah began his creation from nothing, he becomes certain of His power to restore it for the resurrection, and knows that his creation was not in vain.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that contemplating the beginning of creation increases certainty in the resurrection. Admonition: that whoever affirms the beginning [of creation] then denies the restoration has contradicted himself.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that Allaah began creation from nothing, so that the inferring of the restoration from the beginning [of creation] is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of certainty in the resurrection is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon working for it.
Through the training of the tongue: He is habituated to affirming that Allaah is the Originator of creation and its Restorer, so that his tongue grows up believing in the Return.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to contemplate the beginning of creation and to take heed from it, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Originator.
The Name of Allaah: al-Naafi3
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Naafi3” (the Bestower of Benefit) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah in whose hand is all benefit, who benefits whom He wills with what He wills; so no one possesses [the power to bring] benefit except by His leave.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of conveying benefit.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, mercy, and wisdom, and that all benefit is from Him.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿and if He touches you with good - then He is over all things competent﴾ [al-An3aam 6:17]; and He said: ﴿Say, “I hold not for myself [the power of] benefit or harm, except what Allaah has willed”﴾ [al-A3raaf 7:188].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: All benefit is in Allaah’s hand; were the whole of creation to gather together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something that Allaah had decreed for you. So when the young person knows that benefit is from Allaah, he seeks it from Him alone, and does not attach his heart to a creature hoping for its benefit, and knows that the means bring no benefit except by the leave of the One who made them means.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that the Bestower of Benefit drives benefit toward you from where you do not reckon, if you rely upon Him. Admonition: that whoever attaches [the hope of] his benefit to a creature besides Allaah is forsaken.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that all benefit is from Allaah, and that the means are in His hand, so that the attaching of hope to Allaah is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of attachment to the Bestower of Benefit is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon hoping in Him alone.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught to ask Allaah for what benefits him, so that his tongue grows up hopeful in the Bestower of Benefit.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to exert the [material] means alongside attaching benefit to Allaah, and to benefit people seeking His countenance, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Bestower of Benefit.
The Name of Allaah: al-Daarr
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Daarr” (the Bringer of Harm) is that which signifies, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah in whose hand is all harm; no harm befalls anyone except by His leave and decree; He decrees harm by His wisdom, as a trial, or a punishment, or an elevation. And this name is not [mentioned] in isolation but is paired with the Bestower of Benefit.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, and that harm is by His decree and His wisdom.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and wisdom, and that the removal of harm is in His hand alone.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And if Allaah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him﴾ [al-An3aam 6:17]; and He said: ﴿and if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty﴾ [Yoenus 10:107].
The scholarly and exhortatory explanation: No harm occurs in the universe except by the leave and decree of Allaah; and none removes it except Him, for the Bringer of Harm and the Bestower of Benefit are two paired names. So when the young person knows that harm is in Allaah’s hand, he is patient at the time of affliction, and turns to Him alone to remove it, and does not fear the harm of any creature in [the course of] obeying Allaah, and knows that what has befallen him was never going to miss him.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: that whoever turns to Allaah, He removes his harm, for none removes it besides Him. Admonition: that whoever fears the harm of a creature and so disobeys Allaah for its sake is ignorant [of the fact] that harm is in Allaah’s hand.
The pedagogical application through the four pathways in this age group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that harm occurs only by the leave of Allaah and none removes it except Him, so that [the truth] that fear and hope are for Allaah is established in his mind.
Through purification: The sentiment of patience at [the time of] harm and of turning to Allaah is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon reliance [upon Allaah].
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught to say “Remove the harm, O my Lord” at times of affliction, so that his tongue grows up taking refuge in Allaah.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to be patient in the face of harm and not to despair, and not to fear the creation when it comes to the truth, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the One who brings both harm and benefit.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muqsit (the Utterly Just)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Muqsit” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who judges between His servants with equity and justice and loves equity from His creation; He does not wrong anyone by the weight of an atom.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of equity in judgment.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails knowledge, justice, and wisdom, and His love of equity on the part of the servants.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿and act justly. Indeed, Allaah loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Hudjuraat 49:9], and He said: ﴿maintaining [creation] in justice﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:18].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah maintains justice; He judges between His creation with justice and loves those who are just and equitable in their rulings and with their families; He never acts unjustly in His judgment. So when the growing child comes to know that his Lord is the Utterly Just who loves equity, he acts justly in all his affairs: in dividing things among his brothers, and in his judgment concerning those around him.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: al-Muqsit loves the just and honors them, so be just and Allaah will love you. Admonition: whoever acts unjustly and oppresses has contravened what al-Muqsit loves, and he will not escape His equity on the Day of Resurrection.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that Allaah is just and loves justice, so that the love of equity in his deeds is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The love of justice and the hatred of injustice are planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon fairness.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to speaking truth and justice in his speech, so that his tongue grows up just.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to be just among his brothers and to be fair even against himself, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muqsit.
The Name of Allaah: al-Djaami3 (the Gatherer)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Djaami3” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who gathers all creatures for the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning, gathers what is scattered, and joins together disparate things by His power.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of gathering.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails power, knowledge, and justice, and the inevitability of the gathering of creation for recompense.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:9].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah gathers the first and the last upon one plain on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning, and He gathers the scattered parts of the bodies after their disintegration and restores them; the gathering of what has been scattered does not incapacitate Him. So when the growing child becomes certain of Allaah’s gathering of creation, he prepares for that momentous Day and knows that he will be gathered together with all people for the reckoning.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: al-Djaami3 will gather you together with the prophets and the righteous if you love them and act as they acted. Admonition: He will gather you for the reckoning over every matter, small and great, so prepare for His gathering.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that Allaah gathers creation for the reckoning, so that certainty in the Day of Gathering is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of preparing for the Day of Gathering is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon working for the Hereafter.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to mentioning the Day of Gathering and believing in it, so that his tongue grows up affirming the Return (al-ma3aad).
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to perform righteous deeds and to keep the company of the righteous in preparation for the Day of Gathering, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Djaami3.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muhsie (the Enumerator)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Muhsie” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, whose knowledge has encompassed everything in number, so that He has enumerated the deeds of His servants, their very breaths, and all that is in the universe; nothing escapes Him, and nothing eludes Him.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of complete enumeration.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails all-encompassing knowledge and power, and that every deed is preserved and enumerated.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Allaah has enumerated it, while they forgot it﴾ [al-Mudjaadilah 58:6], and He said: ﴿and He has enumerated all things in number﴾ [al-Jinn 72:28].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah has enumerated everything in number: He has enumerated the deeds of the servants, the minute and the momentous alike, and He has enumerated their breaths, their steps, the drops of rain, and the leaves of the trees; creation forgot it, but Allaah enumerated it. So when the growing child comes to know that his Lord has enumerated his deeds, he becomes watchful over himself in the small and the great of his conduct, and he knows that he will be recompensed for every atom.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: al-Muhsie has enumerated your good deeds, so not a single one of them is lost. Admonition: He has enumerated your evil deeds while you forgot them, and He will bring them forth on the Day of Resurrection, so beware.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that Allaah has enumerated every deed and everything, so that it is established in his mind that his deeds are preserved and counted.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): Consciousness of al-Muhsie and eagerness for good deeds are planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon excellence (itqaan).
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to counting up his good deeds through remembrance (such as glorification after the prayer), so that his tongue grows up flourishing with the remembrance of Allaah.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to multiply his good deeds and to avoid evil deeds, out of his knowledge that they are all enumerated, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muhsie.
The Name of Allaah: al-Baari’ (the Originator)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Baari’” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who created creation free of disparity and discord, each part distinguished from another; He is the One who brought created entities into being, differentiated them, and fashioned them flawlessly in the most perfect form.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of flawless origination and masterful creation.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails knowledge, power, and wisdom, and His being alone in bringing into existence.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿He is Allaah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names﴾ [al-Hashr 59:24].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Al-Khaaliq (the Creator), al-Baari’ (the Originator), and al-Musawwir (the Fashioner) are three interlinked names corresponding to the stages of creation: the measuring out and determining (al-Khaaliq), then the bringing into being and differentiation without disparity (al-Baari’), then the shaping and forming (al-Musawwir). So when the growing child reflects upon Allaah’s mastery in originating creation without discord or disorder, he venerates his Originator and knows that such perfect precision cannot come about by chance.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: reflecting upon the mastery of Allaah’s origination increases faith in al-Baari’ and love of Him. Admonition: whoever sees this mastery and then attributes it to nature or to chance has denied his Originator.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that Allaah brought creation into being with perfect mastery, without disparity, so that reasoning from this mastery to al-Baari’ is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of venerating and loving al-Baari’ is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon reverent awe.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught to glorify Allaah when reflecting upon His creation, so that his tongue grows up glorifying al-Baari’.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to reflect upon the mastery of Allaah’s creation and to take heed from it, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Baari’.
The Name of Allaah: al-Musawwir (the Fashioner)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Musawwir” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who fashioned created things and ordered their forms according to what His wisdom required; He is the One who fashions the embryos in the wombs however He wills, and who has granted every creature its form.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of fashioning and shaping.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails knowledge, power, and wisdom, and His being alone in granting forms.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:6], and He is ﴿the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner﴾ [al-Hashr 59:24].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah fashions every creature in the form He has willed: He fashions the fetus in the womb within three layers of darkness, and He diversifies the forms of creation so that no two are identical in complete correspondence. So when the growing child reflects upon the wondrous artistry of Allaah’s fashioning of creation, he venerates his Fashioner, thanks Him for having made his form excellent, and does not disparage the creation of Allaah.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: al-Musawwir has made your form excellent, so thank Him and do not despise yourself or anyone else. Admonition: whoever disparages his own form or that of another has disparaged the handiwork of al-Musawwir.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that Allaah fashioned every creature as He willed and made its form excellent, so that gratitude to al-Musawwir is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of gratitude for the beauty of one’s creation and the aversion to disparaging Allaah’s handiwork are planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon contentment.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught to praise Allaah for the beauty of his form (“Praise be to Allaah who fashioned me and made my form excellent”), so that his tongue grows up thankful.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to give thanks for the blessing of his creation and not to mock the creation of Allaah, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Musawwir.
The Name of Allaah: al-Waalie (the Governor)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Waalie” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who takes charge of the affair of the entire universe, the Owner who governs the affairs of His creation; He is the One who has charge over the affairs of creatures and directs them by His wisdom.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of taking charge of the governance of the universe.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails power, knowledge, and wisdom, and the efficacy of His governance in all things.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allaah … And they have not besides Him any patron﴾ [al-Ra3d 13:11].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is the Governor of the affair of the universe; He governs it and directs it however He wills, and none but He has charge over the affairs of creation; nothing occurs except by His governance and His guardianship. So when the growing child comes to know that the Governor of the universe is Allaah, he entrusts his affair to Him, is content with His governance, and knows that what Allaah chooses for him is better than what he would choose for himself.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: whoever is content for Allaah to take charge of his affair, Allaah governs it for him in the finest manner. Admonition: whoever objects to the governance of al-Waalie is ignorant of His wisdom.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that Allaah takes charge of the governance of everything with wisdom, so that contentment with His governance is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of entrustment and contentment with the governance of al-Waalie is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon submission.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to saying “I am content with Allaah as Lord,” so that his tongue grows up content with Allaah’s governance.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to entrust his affairs to Allaah and to be content with His decree, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Waalie.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muqiet (the Nourisher)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Muqiet” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who conveys sustenance to all creatures and creates it — the Preserver, the Witness, the All-Powerful over everything; He is the One who provides bodies with their sustenance, preserves deeds, and witnesses them.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the twin attributes of conveying sustenance and of all-encompassing power and preservation.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails power, knowledge, provision, and preservation.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a portion [of responsibility] therefrom. And ever is Allaah, over all things, a Keeper﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:85].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Al-Muqiet conveys to every creature the nourishment that sustains it, and He has power over everything, so He preserves it and witnesses it; He does not forget the provision of any creature that moves upon the earth, nor is He heedless of the nourishment of any creature. So when the growing child comes to know that his Lord is al-Muqiet, who has taken it upon Himself to provide his nourishment, he is set at ease regarding his provision, greed for sustenance does not drive him to any act of disobedience, and he knows that the One who created him will not forget him.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: al-Muqiet has taken it upon Himself to provide your nourishment, so be at ease and do not crave as the ignorant crave. Admonition: whoever seeks his nourishment through the unlawful, or fears poverty and so withholds the due of Allaah, is ignorant of the fact that al-Muqiet is his Provider.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that Allaah has taken it upon Himself to provide the nourishment of every creature and that He is a Keeper over all things, so that tranquility regarding Allaah’s provision is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of tranquility regarding the provision of al-Muqiet is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon trust rather than greed.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to asking Allaah for provision and thanking Him for it, so that his tongue grows up thankful to al-Muqiet.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to seek lawful provision while trusting in Allaah’s guarantee, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muqiet.
The Name of Allaah: al-Maani3 (the Withholder)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Maani3” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who withholds His giving from whomever He wills by His wisdom and justice, and who wards off the causes of destruction from His allies (awliyaa’) and so protects them; none can withhold what He gives, and none can give what He withholds. This name is not used in isolation but is paired with al-Mu3tie (the Bestower).
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of withholding with wisdom.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails wisdom, justice, power, and mercy, and that His withholding may itself be the very essence of giving.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: The Prophet ﷺ said after every prayer: “There is no deity but Allaah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent. O Allaah, none can withhold what You have given, and none can give what You have withheld.” (Agreed upon — al-Bukhaarie and Muslim; narrated by al-Bukhaarie, no. 844, and Muslim, no. 593.) And Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Whatever Allaah grants to people of mercy — none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds — none can release it thereafter﴾ [Faatir 35:2].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Al-Maani3 withholds what He wills from whomever He wills by His wisdom, and His withholding may be a good for the servant and a kindness toward him; He withholds from His allies whatever would harm them; no one can withhold what Allaah wishes to give, nor give what He wishes to withhold. So when the child comes to know that withholding is in the hand of Allaah, he is content with whatever is withheld from him, knows that behind it lies wisdom and mercy, and does not ask any creature to give him what Allaah has withheld.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: whatever al-Maani3 withholds from you is for a wisdom and a kindness, so be content with it and think well of Allaah. Admonition: whoever despairs at Allaah’s withholding, or attributes giving and withholding to other than Him, is ignorant of the fact that the whole affair is in the hand of Allaah.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The child is taught that giving and withholding are in the hand of Allaah with wisdom, and that His withholding may be a good, so that contentment and submission are established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of contentment and patience when withheld from is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon thinking well of Allaah.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to saying “Praise be to Allaah” when withheld from just as when given, so that his tongue grows up content.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to be patient when he loses what he loves and not to importune the creation, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Maani3.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muqaddim (the Advancer)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Muqaddim” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who advances whomever He wills of His creation and brings him near by His grace, and who places things forward and sets them in their proper positions according to what His wisdom requires; advancement is in His hand alone. This name has not come in the Qur’an as a single term, but has come in the authentic Sunnah.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of advancing with wisdom.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails knowledge, wisdom, and power, and that the raising of ranks is in His hand.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: The Prophet ﷺ used to say in his night vigil (tahajjud): “O Allaah, forgive me what I have sent before and what I have left behind … You are the One who advances and You are the One who defers; there is no deity but You.” (Agreed upon — al-Bukhaarie and Muslim; narrated by al-Bukhaarie, no. 1120, and Muslim, no. 771, from the hadieth of Ibn 3Abbaas.)
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah advances whomever He wills through success, victory, and elevation, and He places things in their proper positions by His wisdom; whomever Allaah advances, none can put back. So when the growing child comes to know that advancement is in the hand of Allaah, he asks Him to advance him in the ranks of the people of goodness, strives for the means of advancement — obedience and racing toward good deeds — and does not push himself forward through falsehood.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: al-Muqaddim advances whoever races ahead to His obedience and raises his rank, so race toward good deeds. Admonition: whoever seeks to advance through arrogance or falsehood, Allaah puts him back.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that advancement and elevation are in the hand of Allaah with wisdom, so that seeking advancement through obedience is established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The aspiration to race ahead to goodness, seeking that Allaah advance him, is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon competing in obedience.
Through the training of the tongue: He is taught to ask Allaah for advancement in goodness, so that his tongue grows up seeking the loftiest of matters.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to race toward good deeds and to the first row in prayer, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muqaddim.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mu’akhkhir (the Deferrer)
The meaning and its three significations:
Signification by direct correspondence: “Al-Mu’akhkhir” denotes, by direct correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, who defers whomever He wills and so places him in the rear by His wisdom and justice, and who defers things and appointed terms to their ordained times; deferment is in His hand alone. Al-Muqaddim and al-Mu’akhkhir are two paired names, neither mentioned except together with the other.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of deferring with wisdom.
Signification by implication: It necessarily entails knowledge, wisdom, and power, and that the appointed terms and destinies are deferred to their times.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿But never will Allaah delay a soul when its time has come﴾ [al-Munaafiqoen 63:11], and the Prophet ﷺ said: “You are the One who advances and You are the One who defers; there is no deity but You.” (Agreed upon — al-Bukhaarie and Muslim; narrated by al-Bukhaarie, no. 1120, and Muslim, no. 771.)
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah defers whomever He wills by His wisdom, and He defers the appointed terms and provisions to their ordained times, which neither come early nor come late; whomever Allaah defers for a wisdom, none can advance. So when the growing child comes to know that deferment is in the hand of Allaah, he is content with His decree when what he loves is delayed from him, knows that everything has an appointed term, and so neither hastens nor despairs.
Encouragement and admonition: Encouragement: whatever al-Mu’akhkhir defers from you is for a wisdom, and He may store up for you something better than it. Admonition: whoever defers repentance, relying upon the respite granted him, is taken by surprise by the appointed term that cannot be deferred.
The pedagogical application across the four pathways for this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The growing child is taught that deferment is in the hand of Allaah with wisdom, and that the appointed terms are ordained, so that contentment and the absence of haste are established in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The disposition of contentment and patience when what is sought is delayed is planted within him, so that his soul is raised upon submission.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to saying “Allaah has decreed, and what He willed He has done,” so that his tongue grows up content with Allaah’s governance.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to be patient when what he loves is delayed and to hasten to repentance before the appointed term passes, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Mu’akhkhir.
The detailed innate traits (khasaa’is fitriyyah) specific to this developmental stage, and how to direct them pedagogically toward the veneration of Allaah and the governance and direction of the deeds of the hearts
Children at this developmental stage possess a number of innate traits, among them:
1. An increasing ability to discern the intention behind an action.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the child that a deed is measured by its intention: a righteous intention elevates it, and an evil one lowers it. He repeats this in every situation.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of righteous intention. He rejoices before him at a sincere intention, even in a small deed.
Third: Addressing it through formation — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I intend this for Allaah” before every deed. He repeats it with him daily in every situation.
Fourth: Addressing it through formation — the training of the limbs
He trains him in a deed that he conceals, seeking the Face of Allaah. He praises him for sincerity in secret, with a quiet joy.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the governance of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His ability to discern intentions is put to use to teach him that the pivot of a deed is its intention, so that he is led to review his intention and make it sincere for Allaah the moment he begins to act.
Through the governance of the emotions: His gaze is directed toward motives, so that goodness of intention is made beloved to him and evil intention is made hateful to him, and thus his emotion is set straight upon what is wholesome.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is trained to inspect his intention and purify it for Allaah before the deed and after it, so that the root of sincerity is planted within him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Sincerity of intention, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and ostentation (riyaa’) is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is accustomed to patiently correcting his intention whenever it strays, and to watching over it in every deed.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to counsel others with an intention purely for Allaah, just as he corrects his own intention, so that he seeks the Face of Allaah in his counsel rather than vindication for himself.
Through the disciplining of time: He is accustomed to bringing his intention to mind at the outset of his time, so that he assigns to every deed of his day an intention that makes it sound.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is alerted that Satan corrupts intentions through ostentation and self-admiration (3udjb), so that he is accustomed to renewing his sincerity and repelling evil thoughts.
2. A growing capacity for simple logical thinking: and connecting cause and effect with greater precision.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that everything has a cause, and the greatest Cause is Allaah. He puts his thinking to use in directing him toward reliance upon Allaah (tawakkul).
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart reliance upon Allaah together with taking the means. He rejoices before him when he combines the two.
Third: Addressing it through formation — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “In the name of Allaah; I place my trust in Allaah” before acting through the means. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through formation — the training of the limbs
He trains him to take the means together with supplication. He makes this his constant approach in solving problems.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the governance of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His connecting of cause and effect is directed toward reflecting upon the signs of Allaah, so that his mind is led to reason from the effects to their Creator.
Through the governance of the emotions: His rational reasoning is linked to the veneration of the One who perfected the causes, so that his emotion is raised upon reverent awe rather than mere admiration.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to using his mind in the service of truth, seeking the knowledge of Allaah rather than disputation, so that sincerity is planted within him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The exercise of the mind in the beneficial reflection that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from disputation by falsehood, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient in reflection and to be deliberate before judging, so that he does not act rashly.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to verify before he counsels or judges, so that he does not counsel out of ignorance nor hasten to blame his brother before clarification.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to be deliberate in ordering his time and not to be hasty, so that he gives precedence to the most important over the merely important with careful consideration.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is fortified against being dragged by Satan into setting his intellect up as an arbiter so as to reject what is authentically established of revelation, and he is taught that the intellect serves revelation and does not oppose it.
3. A love of justice and fairness: he complains when he feels wronged, even if the wrong comes from adults.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that Allaah is just and commands justice, even against yourself. He puts his love of justice to use in teaching him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the support of the wronged, even against oneself. He rejoices before him when he speaks the truth with fairness.
Third: Addressing it through formation — the training of the tongue
He asks him to speak the truth even if it is bitter in a situation of injustice. He teaches him courteous expressions for that.
Fourth: Addressing it through formation — the training of the limbs
He trains him to render what is due even to his adversary. He makes this a tangible daily habit.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the governance of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His love of justice is put to use to teach him that justice is the command of Allaah, so that he is led to deal fairly, holding himself to account before others.
Through the governance of the emotions: His anger at injustice is disciplined and channeled into a measured objection, and the love of justice for the sake of Allaah is planted within him.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to being just in seeking the Face of Allaah, not to be praised or to vindicate himself, so that sincerity is planted within him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: Justice, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and injustice is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is taught patience and contentment with Allaah’s decree if a wrong befalls him, while seeking his right in an honorable manner.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to counsel the one who wronged him gently and to seek his right in an honorable manner, so that he does not meet ill-treatment with reviling or foul speech.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained not to waste his time in rancor against the wrongdoer, but to turn it to what benefits him and to seek his right at its proper time.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is alerted that injustice is among the adornments of Satan, and that Satan may lure him, in the name of supporting the truth, into transgression, so that he is taught fairness.
4. The ability to memorize longer texts: such as the Noble Qur’an and short prophetic hadieths.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child the merit of memorizing the Book of Allaah and the words of His Messenger ﷺ. He puts his capacity for memorization to use in guiding him.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of the Qur’an and hadieth. He rejoices before him when he memorizes a verse or a hadieth.
Third: Addressing it through formation — the training of the tongue
He has him memorize a verse each week and a hadieth each week. He asks him to recite them back daily at a fixed time.
Fourth: Addressing it through formation — the training of the limbs
He seats him with himself in a fixed daily memorization session. He makes this the most important cognitive routine of the day.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the governance of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His memorization is employed in the Qur’an and the Sunnah, so that by what he has memorized he is led to a guidance by which he governs himself.
Through the governance of the emotions: His memorization is linked to the love and veneration of the speech of Allaah, so that his emotion is raised upon intimacy with revelation.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to memorizing for the sake of Allaah and acting upon what he has memorized, not for boasting, so that sincerity is planted within him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The memorization of what Allaah loves — His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet — is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from memorizing idle speech, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient in memorization, review, and diligent striving, so that he does not grow weary.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to remind his companions to review and to counsel them to persevere, so that he counsels by his own example through his diligent striving in memorization.
Through the disciplining of time: Fixed times are set aside for memorization and review, so that what he has memorized becomes firmly rooted through constancy at its appointed time.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan makes him forget and discourages him, so that he is accustomed to seeking refuge in Allaah and to persevering in review.
5. A love of organized competition: in sports or intellectual games.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that good competition is in goodness and the obedience of Allaah. He redirects his inclination toward that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that the measure of success is the pleasure of Allaah. He rejoices before him when he wins with a righteous intention.
Third: Addressing it through formation — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “O Allaah, bless him” to his competitor when he wins. He teaches him to abandon self-admiration and arrogance.
Fourth: Addressing it through formation — the training of the limbs
He provides him with competitions in memorizing the Qur’an or in beneficial skills. He praises him for his effort more than for the victory.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the governance of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His competitiveness is directed toward racing in goodness and knowledge, so that his ambition is led to what raises him in the sight of Allaah.
Through the governance of the emotions: His love of winning is disciplined so that it does not turn into envy, and joy at another’s winning in goodness is planted within him.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to competing for Allaah and His pleasure, not for boasting, so that sincerity is planted within him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: Competing in the goodness that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from cheating and transgression, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and contentment when he loses, and in graciousness when he wins.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to console the loser and counsel him, and to conduct himself well when he wins so that he does not gloat, thus linking victory with humility.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to turn his time after a loss toward a new and beneficial attempt, not toward regret.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that the love of prevailing may be exploited by Satan to drag him into arrogance and cheating, so that he is directed toward praiseworthy competition.
6. A strong susceptibility to external role models: such as the teacher or the coach.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that the true role model is the one who helps him to worship Allaah. He assists him in distinguishing righteous role models.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of the Prophet ﷺ and of the people of knowledge and righteousness. He makes them the highest role models in his life.
Third: Addressing it through formation — the training of the tongue
He asks him: “If the Prophet ﷺ were here, what would he say?” He repeats the question in various situations.
Fourth: Addressing it through formation — the training of the limbs
He takes him to gatherings of knowledge and circles of the Qur’an. He chooses righteous teachers for him with joy.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the governance of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is directed toward a righteous role model, so that by emulating it he is led to that whereby he governs himself upon goodness.
Through the governance of the emotions: The love of the righteous and the emulation of them are planted within him, so that his emotion is raised upon what is wholesome.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to emulating the righteous person for the sake of Allaah, not merely out of admiration for his personality, so that sincerity is planted within him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The people of goodness are made beloved to him as role models, and he is warned against the evil role model, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is followed up in his choice of role models with patience and care, and is gently directed toward the more righteous.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to choose his role model from the people of goodness, and is gently counselled toward the most upright, so that he grows accustomed to distinguishing the good role model.
Through time management: Whoever he mixes with and emulates during his leisure time is monitored, so that he safeguards his time from a role model who squanders it.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against evil role models that Satan beautifies within his surroundings and media, so that he is taught the criterion of role models according to the Sacred Law.
7. Distinguishing between fixed principles and temporary conventions.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that the Sacred Law of Allaah is fixed and does not change, whereas human laws are ever-changing. He invests the child’s grasp of this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the veneration of the fixed tenets of the Sacred Law. He rejoices before him when he holds firmly to a fixed principle even as people change.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “This is the ruling of Allaah” regarding the fixed tenets of the Sacred Law. He repeats it with him in real situations.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him in the constancy of acts of worship (the prayer, truthfulness) despite changing circumstances. He makes this a settled disposition.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that the fixed tenets of the religion are not to be altered and that whatever lies beyond them follows benefit, so that he is led to the veneration of the fixed tenets of the Sacred Law.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him awe and love for the fixed tenets of the religion, so that his emotion is nurtured upon venerating what Allaah has magnified.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to hold firmly to the fixed principle for Allaah’s sake, not to conform to people, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Firmness upon what Allaah has established is made beloved to him, and the dilution of the fixed tenets is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in holding firm to the truth even if it contradicts changing custom.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to hold firm to the truth even if it contradicts custom, and to counsel others toward the truth gently, without conforming to falsehood.
Through time management: He is trained not to follow every passing fad that squanders his time, so that he remains steadfast upon what benefits him even if others abandon it.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan beautifying for him the dilution of the fixed tenets in the name of progress, so that he is taught to distinguish the fixed from the changing.
8. Noticing a clear development in long-term memory.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator invests the child’s memory in memorizing the Most Beautiful Names of Allaah and their meanings. He links his memorization to pleasing Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the Most Beautiful Names of Allaah. He rejoices before him when he mentions one of them together with its meaning.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to memorize five of the Most Beautiful Names each week. He repeats them with him daily along with their meanings.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He supplicates to Allaah by His Most Beautiful Names before him when in need. He keeps to this consistently with him in daily situations.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His memory is employed to store up the Qur’an and beneficial knowledge, so that he is led by what he has stored toward goodness.
Through leading the emotions: Whatever good he stores up is linked to love and joy, so that his memory becomes associated with the atmosphere of faith.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to memorize for Allaah’s sake and to act upon it, not for show, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: His mind is filled with what Allaah loves, and he is kept away from storing up idle talk and falsehood, so that his memory grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in long-term memorization and review.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to urge his brothers toward constant review, so that he counsels by his very state through his perseverance with the Book of Allaah.
Through time management: A fixed daily portion is assigned for memorization and review, so that he bears fruit through steady constancy in his time rather than through sudden bursts.
Through knowing the enemies: His store is filled with good, so that no emptiness is left for Satan to fill with the memorizing of falsehood.
9. An increased sense of responsibility when tasks are entrusted to him.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that trustworthiness in responsibility is among what Allaah loves. He invests his sense of it to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the greatness of the trust. He rejoices before him when he carries out the task with excellence and trustworthiness.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “I will do this for Allaah, with trustworthiness” before the task. He repeats it with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He assigns him real daily responsibilities (waking his brother, prayer on time). He praises him for his trustworthiness.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: Tasks suited to him are entrusted to him, so that by carrying them out he is led to bear the trust of servitude to Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him the sense of the sweetness of trust and the joy of accomplishment in good, so that his emotion is nurtured upon responsibility.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to carry out what is entrusted to him for Allaah’s sake and to perfect it seeking reward, not for praise, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Fulfilling the trust that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and negligence and betrayal are made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in completing the task and bearing its hardship.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to help his companions complete their tasks and to counsel them to persevere, so that he counsels by his very state through completing his own work.
Through time management: A time is set for him to complete his task, so that he is habituated to commit to the time of his work and not to procrastinate.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan discourages him and beautifies negligence, so that he is habituated to steadfast vigilance in fulfilling the trust.
10. The emergence of an inclination to belong to a group (friends, the team).
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that the best of groups is the group of the believers. He directs his inclination toward belonging to the people of faith.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the believers and pride in belonging to them. He rejoices before him when he belongs to a righteous gathering.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “I am with the believers” when making a choice. He repeats it with him in real situations.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He takes him to the mosque and the gatherings of remembrance. He makes this his actual, lasting belonging.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His belonging is directed toward the company of goodness and the community of the Muslims, so that by his belonging he is led toward what aids him in his religion.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him love for the people of faith and intimacy with them, so that his emotion is nurtured upon brotherhood for Allaah’s sake.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to belong for Allaah’s sake and not out of partisanship, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Belonging to the people of goodness and allying with them is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from evil companionship, so that he is nurtured upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and excellent conduct in the company of the group and in bearing with its members.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in excellent conduct in the company of the group and in counselling its members gently, and in bearing what issues from them without reproach.
Through time management: Times for righteous, beneficial companionship are set aside, so that he cultivates his familiarity with good people within organized time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against evil groups that are among the soldiers of Satan, so that he is taught the criterion of belonging by religion and not by whim.
11. A love of helping with serious work: and not only play.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that serving one’s family and close relatives is an act of worship. He invests his desire for seriousness to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for benefiting people. He rejoices before him when he applies himself seriously to a beneficial work.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “I help for Allaah’s sake, not for reward” before the task. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He assigns him real, serious works (organizing, repairing, delivering). He praises him for completing them with excellence.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His desire for serious work is invested, so that through his helping in what is beneficial he is led to bear responsibility for Allaah’s sake.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him love of helping and the joy of doing good, so that his emotion is nurtured upon giving.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to help for Allaah’s sake and to seek the reward, not for praise, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Helping his family and the people of goodness — which Allaah loves — is made beloved to him, so that he is nurtured upon righteousness and love for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in completing the work, perfecting it, and bearing its hardship.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to perfect his work and to counsel others to do good, so that he counsels by his very state through his excellence and his bearing of hardship.
Through time management: He is given sufficient time to perfect his work, so that he is habituated to excellence within his time rather than ruinous haste.
Through knowing the enemies: He is habituated to activity in good, so that his free time is not left to the laziness that Satan loves.
12. The ability to regulate behavior in formal environments (such as school and the mosque).
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that Allaah loves good manners and dignity in every place. He invests his capacity for self-regulation.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that Allaah sees him in every place. He rejoices before him when he conducts himself with good manners in a formal gathering.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He teaches him the supplication for concluding a gathering: “Glory be to You, O Allaah, and praise be to You…”. He repeats it with him upon leaving gatherings.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He accompanies him in the mosque or the school. He trains him in good manners in them through his own practical example.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught the etiquette of the mosque and gatherings, so that by regulating his behavior he is led to venerate the places of obedience.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him awe of the houses of Allaah and love for their etiquette, so that his emotion is nurtured upon veneration.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to regulate his behavior out of consciousness of Allaah, not merely out of fear of people, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The etiquette of the places of goodness that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and frivolity in them is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and self-restraint in long gatherings.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in the etiquette of the gathering and in counselling his neighbor gently, and in restraining himself so that he causes no harm through speech or idle talk.
Through time management: He is trained to invest the time of the gathering in what is beneficial, so that he does not waste it in idle talk or triviality.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan distracts him in the places of obedience, so that he is habituated to remembrance and seeking refuge so that his heart may be present.
13. Understanding that actions have long-term consequences.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that every small deed is recorded by Allaah, and that it has an effect in this world and the Hereafter. He invests his understanding of this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart a sense of responsibility for every act. He rejoices before him when he reflects upon the consequence of an act.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “Does this please Allaah?” before every important decision. He instills the question in him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him in daily self-accounting before sleep. He makes it a fixed routine before sleep.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that every deed has a consequence in this world and the Hereafter, so that by heeding consequences he is led to God-consciousness (taqwaa).
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him hope for the outcome of good and fear of the outcome of evil, so that his emotion is nurtured upon vigilant self-watchfulness.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to work for the outcome of the Hereafter for Allaah’s sake, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: That whose outcome is praiseworthy before Allaah is made beloved to him, and that whose outcome is evil is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and in preferring the lasting outcome over immediate pleasure.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to remind himself and others of the lasting outcome, so that he counsels by his very state by preferring the deferred over the immediate.
Through time management: He is trained to spend his time on that whose outcome endures, so that he does not consume it in a fleeting immediate pleasure.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan beautifies the immediate and makes one forget the outcome, so that he is habituated to consider ultimate ends.
14. The development of simple moral reasoning: he understands that some actions are wrong even if no one sees them.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that Allaah sees the hidden and the open, so that the secret deed is like the public one. He invests his understanding of this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the fear of Allaah in secret. He rejoices before him when he abandons a secret wrong for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He instills in him the saying “Allaah sees me when I am alone” when in seclusion. He repeats it with him gently.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
The educator deliberately leaves the child in a situation in which he is tested. He praises him for abandoning the wrong in secret.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: It is firmly established in him that Allaah sees him even when people are absent, so that through his vigilant awareness he is led to abandon the vile in seclusion.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him awe of Allaah’s full awareness and love for Him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon vigilant awareness in secret.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to abandon the vile in seclusion for Allaah’s sake, so that the root of sincerity and consciousness of Allaah is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: What Allaah loves, in secret and in the open, is made beloved to him, and the vile is made hateful to him even if hidden, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patient restraint from disobedience in seclusion, where there is no watcher but Allaah.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in the vigilant awareness of Allaah in seclusion, so that he counsels himself with the presence of the Watcher where no one sees him.
Through time management: He is trained to fill the times of his seclusion with what is beneficial, so that he does not leave his free time as a doorway to disobedience.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan emboldens him in his moments of seclusion, so that he is habituated to summon the awareness of Allaah’s watchfulness and to repel the whisperings.
15. An increase in empathy and understanding the feelings of others.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that mercy toward people is among the greatest traits of the believer. He invests his empathy to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart mercy toward the believers. He rejoices before him when he shares in his brothers’ joys and sorrows.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to supplicate for whoever harms him before he responds. He instills in him the supplication of the righteous.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him to visit the sick and console the grieving. He takes him along on those visits.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His mercy is invested so that he may be taught that Allaah loves mercy, so that he is led to do good to creation.
Through leading the emotions: His empathy is cultivated and directed, so that his emotion is nurtured upon gentleness toward the servants of Allaah.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to do good for Allaah’s sake, not to be seen as a doer of good, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Mercy toward the people of faith and doing good to them is made beloved to him, and harshness is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in doing good and in bearing the harm of those to whom he does good.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to do good and to counsel those to whom he does good even if they harm him, so that he bears their harm patiently, seeking the Face of Allaah.
Through time management: Times are set aside for doing good to people, so that he is habituated to expend his time in benefiting them rather than in revenge.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that harshness is among Satan’s beautifications, so that mercy — by which Allaah shows mercy — is made beloved to him.
16. Seeking the respect of adults: and he wants to be treated seriously.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that Allaah raises whoever respects his elders. He invests his desire to be taken seriously in teaching him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that the best respect is that the elders serve him with their supplication. He rejoices before him when he behaves with good manners.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “At your service, my father / my mother” with complete good manners. He repeats it with him in every matter.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him to stand for the elders and to honor them. He makes this a tangible daily disposition.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His seeking of respect is directed toward seeking the pleasure of Allaah first, so that he is led to weigh his worth by obedience to his Lord.
Through leading the emotions: His love of appreciation is regulated so that it does not turn into arrogance, and humility is instilled in him.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to work for the pleasure of Allaah and not for people’s exalting of him, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: What raises his worth with Allaah is made beloved to him, and seeking honor through falsehood is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience if he is not appreciated, and in not being deluded if he is appreciated.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained neither to collapse if he is not appreciated nor to be deluded if he is appreciated, so that he counsels himself that his reward is with Allaah and not with people.
Through time management: He is trained not to occupy his time with people’s appreciation or blame, so that he directs his concern toward his work and his sincerity.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that the love of elevation may be dragged by Satan into arrogance, so that he is habituated to humility for Allaah’s sake.
17. Being moved by heroic stories: such as the stories of the prophets, the Companions, and leaders.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He selects for the child the stories of the prophets, the Companions, and the Muslim leaders. He explains their heroic deeds and how they were for Allaah’s sake.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the true heroes among the people of faith. He rejoices before him when he is moved by them.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to recount the story of a Companion hero each week. He instills in him the authentic stories.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He emulates alongside him a deed from the heroic feats of the Companions (courage, truthfulness, generosity). He makes this a firm establishment.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: The biographies of the prophets and the Companions are related to him, so that by emulating them he is led to lofty matters in obedience to Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him love for the true heroes among the people of faith, so that his emotion is nurtured upon venerating the people of goodness.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to emulate them for Allaah’s sake, and is taught that their heroism was through their sincerity, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The friends of Allaah among the prophets and the Companions are made beloved to him, and their enemies are made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: The instances of their patience are highlighted for him, so that patience is made beloved to him and is emulated.
Through sincere counsel: The instances of the patient ones are highlighted for him so that he emulates them, and he is counselled to recount them to others so that they may benefit from them.
Through time management: A regular time is set aside for the biographies of the patient ones, so that the love of emulating them becomes firmly rooted through constancy.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught from their biographies how they strove against the enemies of Allaah, so that he comes to know his enemy and they are emulated in repelling him.
18. The beginning of comparing ideals with reality.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that the ideal is what Allaah has commanded, and that striving toward it is an act of worship. He directs his sentiment toward this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart patience in applying the ideal within a reality that contradicts it. He rejoices before him at his steadfastness.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “O Allaah, keep us firm upon the truth” when he sees something contrary. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him to do the ideal ordained by the Sacred Law even if reality contradicts it. He praises him for his steadfastness with joy.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that the ideal is the guidance of revelation, so that he is led to weigh reality by the scale of the Sacred Law and not the reverse.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him not to despair at the deficiency of reality, and striving to reform it is made beloved to him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon active hope.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to seek the perfection ordained by the Sacred Law for Allaah’s sake, not to distinguish himself over people, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The ideal that Allaah is pleased with is made beloved to him, and whatever of reality contradicts it is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience with the deficiency of reality while striving for reform without discontent.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to counsel toward reforming what has become corrupt without discontent or reproach, so that he combines patience with striving in good.
Through time management: He is trained to spend his time on beneficial reform rather than on complaint, so that he fills his time with building rather than grumbling.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan casting him into despair or repulsion under the pretext of the ideal, so that he is taught wisdom and gradualness.
19. A love of practical learning: experiments and manual skills.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that beneficial knowledge is an act of worship. He invests his passion for experiments to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for beneficial knowledge. He rejoices before him when he learns a beneficial, lawful skill.
