Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “My Lord, increase me in knowledge” with every act of learning. He repeats it with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He provides him with beneficial, lawful manual experiments. He links them to gratitude to Allaah for His blessings.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His practical learning is directed toward what benefits the Ummah, so that by his skill he is led to the service of his religion and his society.
Through leading the emotions: His skill is linked to the veneration of the One who granted him the ability, so that his emotion is nurtured upon gratitude rather than self-conceit.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to learn the skill for Allaah’s sake and for the benefit of people, not for boasting, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: What is beneficial among that which Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from employing the skill in what is harmful, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and diligent striving in mastering the skill.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in diligent striving to master his skill and to counsel others toward mastery, so that he counsels by his very state through his excellence.
Through time management: Regular times for practice are set aside, so that he masters his skill through steady constancy in his time rather than through sudden bursts.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against his skill being employed in what harms or diverts from Allaah through Satan’s beautification.
20. A growing ability to solve simple problems without adult intervention.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that Allaah is his helper if he takes the means and supplicates. He invests his ability to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart reliance upon Allaah (tawakkul) together with effort. He rejoices before him when he solves a problem through supplication and effort.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He instills in him “O Allaah, help me” before every problem. He repeats it with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He leaves him an opportunity to solve it himself after a supplication from him. He praises him for his effort and his supplication.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His ability to solve is cultivated while habituating him to seek Allaah’s aid, so that he is led to take the means together with reliance upon Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him trust in Allaah in times of hardship rather than anxiety, so that his emotion is nurtured upon reliance upon Allaah.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to seek the solution in pursuit of the pleasure of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The solution that pleases Allaah is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from unlawful stratagems, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and deliberateness in addressing problems without haste.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in deliberateness and in seeking the wise solution, so that he counsels others toward measured reflection rather than haste.
Through time management: He is trained to grant the problem sufficient time for thought, so that he does not rush into a solution that corrupts more than it reforms.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan may beautify for him unlawful solutions, so that he is habituated to seek the lawful way out.
21. Developing the ability to plan ahead (for a day or an activity).
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that planning together with reliance upon Allaah is a Sunnah. He invests his ability to plan to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that Allaah’s ordaining is greater than his own planning. He rejoices before him when he is content with Allaah’s decree.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “If Allaah wills” in every plan. He instills this in him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him to draw up a plan for his day that includes a time for worship. He praises him for adhering to it.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught planning while making the matter contingent upon the will of Allaah, so that he is led to take the means while entrusting the results to Him.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him tranquility in Allaah’s ordaining together with good planning, so that his emotion is nurtured upon reliance upon Allaah.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to plan for what pleases Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Planning for the good that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from scheming for falsehood, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in carrying out what he has planned and in avoiding haste.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to fulfill what he has planned and to persevere in it, so that he counsels himself to complete what he has resolved upon without haste.
Through time management: He is trained to carry out his plan at its arranged times, so that he is habituated to regulate his time and to adhere to his schedule.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan makes him promises, arouses false hopes in him, and beautifies for him a scheme involving disobedience, so that he is habituated to seek out the lawful in his planning.
22. The beginning of forming a personal opinion on certain matters.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that an opinion ought to rest upon the Sacred Law of Allaah. He invests his awareness to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the veneration of Allaah’s Sacred Law above his own opinion. He rejoices before him when he yields an opinion to the Sacred Law.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “This is my opinion, and Allaah knows best” out of humility. He instills in him the avoidance of bigotry.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him to ask the people of knowledge before adopting an opinion. He makes this a tangible habit.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught to build his opinion upon evidence and not upon whim, so that his intellect is led to make revelation the arbiter.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him love of the truth even if it opposes his own desire, so that his emotion is nurtured upon preferring the truth.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to seek the truth in his opinion for Allaah’s sake, not to vindicate himself, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: The truth that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and falsehood is made hateful to him, so that he is nurtured upon love and hatred for Allaah’s sake.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in seeking the truth and in returning to it once it becomes clear.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to accept counsel and to return to the truth once it becomes clear, so that he neither stubbornly resists nor disdains to return.
Through time management: He is trained not to prolong his clinging to a mistake that wastes his time, so that he returns to what is correct in its due time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan beautifying for him an opinion based on whim or contrary to the evidence, so that he is taught to refer disputes back to the Book and the Sunnah.
23. Displaying loyalty to close friends.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that true loyalty is to Allaah, His Messenger, and the believers. He invests his sense of loyalty in order to direct it.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that his loyalty should be for Allaah’s sake. He rejoices before him when he leaves a corrupt friend.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He instills in him the saying “I love you for Allaah’s sake” to his righteous friend. He repeats it with him upon meeting.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He selects righteous friends for him. He invites them to visit him and increases their sitting together in his presence.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His loyalty is directed to be for Allaah’s sake, so that he is led such that his love, his hatred, and his allegiance are all for Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him love for his brothers for Allaah’s sake, so that his emotion is nurtured upon the brotherhood of faith.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to give allegiance for Allaah’s sake and not for self-interest, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty, and disavowal: Allying with the people of faith and supporting them in truth is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from supporting his friend in wrongdoing, so that he is nurtured upon loyalty for Allaah’s sake and not out of whim.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and excellent conduct in companionship, and in counselling his friend even if it is hard.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to counsel his friend with the truth even if it is hard upon him — secretly and mercifully, not by exposing or reproaching him.
Through time management: A time is set aside for his righteous companionship and for counselling it, so that he cultivates his beneficial affection within organized time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that allegiance upon falsehood is among Satan’s beautifications, so that he is taught the governing principle of loyalty for Allaah’s sake.
24. Being affected by public praise: which motivates him to exert further effort.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that the praise of Allaah is greater than the praise of people. He turns his sentiment toward seeking the pleasure of Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that praise is a trial, so that he fears ostentation (riyaa’). He rejoices before him when he returns the merit to Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — training the tongue
He asks him to say “Praise be to Allaah; O Allaah, make me better than what they think” when praised. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — training the limbs
He trains him in a righteous deed that he conceals from people. He praises him for his sincerity in secret.
Directing through the branches of veneration:
Through steering the soul and seeking knowledge: The effect of praise upon him is directed toward seeking Allaah’s good pleasure, so that he is led to work for Allaah and not for commendation.
Through steering the emotions: His joy at praise is regulated so that it does not turn into self-admiration (3udjb), and humility is planted in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to work for Allaah and not for praise, and is taught the danger of loving commendation, so that sincerity is planted in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Sincerity, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and ostentation (riyaa’) is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained in patience upon abandoning that which brings praise if it is mixed with ostentation.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to abandon that which brings praise if ostentation is mixed with it, so that he counsels his own soul to make the deed sincerely for Allaah alone.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to fill his times with secret, pure deeds, so that he does not bind his time to being seen by people.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that the love of praise is the gateway of ostentation which Satan exploits, so that he is accustomed to concealing his deeds at times.
25. The increasing sense of personal identity: He knows what he loves and what he hates.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
He explains to the child that his identity is to be a servant of Allaah. He invests the child’s increasing sense of self to teach him this.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart pride in Islam and in servitude to Allaah. He shows joy before him when he holds fast to his identity.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I am a Muslim, I love Allaah” when he is asked about his identity. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him that his love and his hatred be for the sake of Allaah. He instills this in him in daily situations.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through steering the soul and seeking knowledge: His awareness of his identity is founded upon his being a servant of Allaah, a Muslim, so that he is led to make his love and hatred follow his religion.
Through steering the emotions: The love of what Allaah loves and the hatred of what He detests are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon the scale of the Sacred Law (Sharie3ah).
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to make his allegiance to his faith-based identity for Allaah, not out of blind imitation, so that sincerity is planted in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal: It is made beloved to him to love what Allaah loves and to hate what He hates, for that is the core of his identity, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and steadfastness upon his faith-based identity before the one who opposes him.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to remain steadfast upon his faith-based identity, and to counsel the one who opposes him with wisdom, neither by going along [with falsehood] nor by harshness.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to consume his time in what dissolves his identity, but to spend it on what firms up his faith.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan and the callers to falsehood dissolving his faith-based identity, so that his belonging is founded upon revelation (wahy).
26. The readiness to accept the logic of the innate disposition (fitrah) when the method of upbringing accords with it.
First: Addressing it through purging
He explains to the child that the innate disposition is upon Islam, so he should not deviate from it. He invests his heart’s readiness for this.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul
He plants in his heart adherence to the innate disposition. He shows joy before him when he is at ease with what accords with it.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation — the training of the tongue
He instills in him the saying “Praise be to Allaah who created me a Muslim.” He repeats it with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation — the training of the limbs
He keeps up with him a daily act of worship that consecrates the innate disposition. He makes the Fajr prayer the mark of the innate disposition.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through steering the soul and seeking knowledge: He is addressed with what accords with his sound innate disposition, so that, through the innate disposition’s agreement with the Sacred Law, he is led to submit to the truth.
Through steering the emotions: The tranquillity of the innate disposition toward tawhied is planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon intimacy with the truth.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to follow the truth that accords with his innate disposition for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is planted in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal: That upon which the innate disposition and the Sacred Law agree is made beloved to him, and that which corrupts the innate disposition is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in cultivating his innate disposition and guarding it from corrupting influences.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to guard his innate disposition from corrupting influences, so that he counsels his own soul to shun what defiles his heart.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to fill his time with the beneficial that guards his innate disposition, so that he does not leave his free time to corrupting influences.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan rallies against the innate disposition to corrupt it, so that he is accustomed to guarding it with knowledge and remembrance (dhikr).
27. The realization that faith is also a social system.
First: Addressing it through purging
He explains to the child that faith is not only between the servant and his Lord, but also with people. He invests his realization.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul
He plants in his heart the love of serving the Muslims. He shows joy before him when he benefits his brethren.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “O Allaah, forgive the Muslim men and the Muslim women.” He instills this in him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation — the training of the limbs
He involves him in visiting the neighbors and praying in congregation. He makes gathering upon good a habit.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through steering the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught that faith manifests in dealing with creation, so that he is led to realize his religion in his conduct with people.
Through steering the emotions: The love of the brotherhood of faith and of mutual support is planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon gathering for good.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to do good to people for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is planted in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal: Cooperation upon righteousness with the people of faith is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from cooperation upon sin, so that he grows up upon allegiance and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in associating with people and bearing their harm.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in good association with people and counseling them gently, and in bearing their harm without repaying it with evil.
Through the governance of time: Times are set aside for mixing with people in what is right, so that he is trained in forbearance (hilm) through practice in its due moments.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan sows division among the believers, so that he is accustomed to reconciliation and to preserving the brotherhood.
28. Mental readiness to understand concepts such as divine decree and destiny (al-qadaa’ wa-l-qadar) and intention, and to act on their basis.
First: Addressing it through purging
He explains to the child that everything is by Allaah’s decree, its good and its evil. He invests his mental readiness to receive these [concepts].
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul
He plants in his heart contentment with Allaah’s decree. He shows joy before him when he is patient over a small affliction.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation — the training of the tongue
He instills in him the saying “Allaah decreed, and what He willed He did.” He repeats it with him at times of small misfortunes.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation — the training of the limbs
He trains him in patience at disappointment or the loss of a toy. He praises him for seeking [Allaah’s] reward (ihtisaab).
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through steering the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught the pillars of belief in destiny and of acting by intention, so that he is led to contentment with Allaah’s decree and to taking the [appropriate] means.
Through steering the emotions: Contentment and tranquillity with Allaah’s decree are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon submission rather than anxious despair.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to correct his intention and to be content with his Lord’s decree for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is planted in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal: Contentment with what Allaah has decreed is made beloved to him, and discontent (tasakhkhut) is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience over what is decreed and in not objecting to Allaah’s ruling.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained in contentment with Allaah’s ruling and in not objecting, so that he counsels his own soul to submit to his Lord’s decree.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to waste his time in discontent over what is decreed, but to turn it toward contentment and action.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against the insinuations concerning destiny which Satan casts to make him fall into fatalism (jabr) or objection, so that he is taught to combine [taking] the means with [belief in] destiny.
The age group from ten to twelve years
The application of the governance of time in this group through the four tracks (which the educator embodies and directs):
Through purging: His understanding of the value of time is deepened, as well as that he will be questioned about it; he is taught the simple jurisprudence of priorities (the obligatory before play, and the prayer before every occupation), and to distinguish the beneficial from what wastes his time.
Through purification of the soul: There is firmly established in him the mindfulness that Allaah will hold him to account for his time, and the treating of the beginnings of laziness and procrastination; and the seizing of his time in what is beneficial is made beloved to him.
Through the training of the tongue: He is trained to abandon excessive speech and idle talk, to regulate the time of amusement and conversation, and to fill his tongue with remembrance and beneficial reading.
Through the training of the limbs: The command to pray at its appointed time is emphasized to him (as he has approached ten), and he is trained to set a daily schedule for himself and a simple self-reckoning at the end of his day, to seize the early morning, and to persevere upon a small daily portion [of worship] (wird) even if it be little.
The application of the virtue of sincere counsel in this group through the four tracks (which the educator embodies and directs):
Through purging: His understanding of the pillars of sincere counsel, its conditions, and its etiquettes is deepened; counsel is distinguished for him from reproach and backbiting; and he is trained to distinguish sincere advice from evil speech — for his mind is more mature, so he is addressed with detail and proof.
Through purification of the soul: There is firmly established the sincerity of counsel for Allaah and the love of good for people, and soundness of breast free from gloating and envy; and he is trained to accept counsel from the elder without arrogance or disdain.
Through the training of the tongue: He is trained to counsel privately with a fair word, to begin with praise before correction, to restrain the tongue from backbiting and mockery, and to enjoin the good gently in his surroundings.
Through the training of the limbs: The command to pray is emphasized to him (as he has approached ten), and he is trained in practical role-modeling, in concealing the faults of his siblings, and in patience in counseling them; and he is entrusted with a responsibility suited to his age that accustoms him to bearing counsel and carrying it out.
The most beautiful names of Allaah and their pedagogical application in this group
Building upon the names presented previously across the four groups (the comprehensive names such as al-Rahmaan and al-Khaaliq; the names of [Allaah’s] full awareness such as al-Samie3, al-Basier, and al-3Aliem; the names of grandeur such as al-3Adhiem; and the names of watchfulness, reckoning, wisdom, and justice), they are here deepened in a manner suited to the age of abstract thought, critical awareness, and the sense of dignity and independence: the meanings of watchfulness are elevated to Allaah’s subtle kindness (lutf) and His intimate acquaintance with hidden things, and what he has come to know of grandeur is linked to Allaah’s might (3izzah), through which his true dignity comes to be. Then are added the names of might, subtle kindness, intimate acquaintance, and gratitude.
The name of Allaah: al-3Aziez (the All-Mighty)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence (mutaabaqah): “al-3Aziez” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of might in its categories: the might of strength, the might of inaccessibility (so that He is neither overcome nor attained), and the might of rank (so that He has no peer).
The signification of implication (tadammun): It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of might in its kinds.
The signification of entailment (iltizaam): It entails power, subjugation, self-sufficiency, and absolute perfection, and it entails the abasement of all besides Him before Him. Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And to Allaah belongs [all] honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munaafiqoen 63:8].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: All might belongs to Allaah. Whoever seeks it in other than His obedience, Allaah abases him; and whoever draws might from Allaah is mighty even if he stands alone. The believer draws his might from his servitude to al-3Aziez, so he does not abase himself before any creature in disobedience to the Creator. This cultivates in the youth — at the age of seeking dignity — [the awareness] that his true dignity lies in obedience to his Lord, not in going along with people.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that whoever obeys al-3Aziez and draws might from Him attains might in both abodes, so seek your might with Him. Warning: that whoever seeks might through disobedience to Him or through allegiance to His enemies, Allaah abases him — so there is no might except through His obedience.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth that true might lies in obedience to Allaah, not in opposing the truth nor in the approval of peers, so that the legal scale of dignity is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: Might through his religion and refusal of abasement in disobedience to Allaah are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon taking pride in Islam.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed not to let his tongue debase itself with falsehood to please people, and to take pride in the word of truth, so that his tongue grows up mighty through the truth.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in steadfastness upon the truth in the face of peer pressure, and in not going along with them in falsehood for the sake of acceptance, so that his limbs act in accordance with the might of the believer.
The name of Allaah: al-Latief (the Subtle and Kind)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Latief” signifies, by correspondence, two meanings: subtlety in knowledge (so that He knows the minute and hidden things), and kindness in action (so that He conveys to His servant his benefits from where he does not perceive, with gentleness and subtlety).
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence, the subtlety of [His] knowledge, and the kindness of [His] handiwork.
The signification of entailment: It entails precise knowledge, intimate acquaintance, mercy, and wisdom. Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾ [Yoesuf 12:100], and He said: ﴿And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾ [al-Mulk 67:14].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah’s kindness toward His servant is that He drives good toward him from routes he does not reckon upon, that He turns evil away from him while he is unaware, and that He manages his affair in a way whose aspect is hidden from him, yet whose outcome is praiseworthy — for many an affliction has a blessing folded within it, and many a withholding has a gift folded within it. Whoever knows Allaah’s kindness thinks well of Him in every state.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that al-Latief manages good for you from where you do not know, so think well of Him and seek His kindness. Warning: that whoever thinks ill of his Lord and despairs at His decree has been ignorant of His kindness and His wisdom.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: The youth is taught — at the age of asking about the secrets of things — that Allaah has a hidden kindness in His management, so that thinking well of Allaah behind the outward appearances of events is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: Tranquillity and love of al-Latief at times of hardship are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon contentment and thinking well [of Allaah].
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to say “Perhaps there is good in it” and “Praise be to Allaah in every state” when something disliked occurs, so that his tongue grows up upon thinking well [of Allaah].
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in gentleness in his dealings with people and in kindness toward them, in emulation of Allaah’s kindness, so that his limbs act in accordance with the love of al-Latief.
The name of Allaah: al-Khabier (the All-Acquainted)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Khabier” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of intimate acquaintance, which is the knowledge of the inner realities of matters, their subtleties, and their hidden aspects, just as He knows their outward aspects.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of knowledge of the precise inner realities.
The signification of entailment: It entails the complete encompassing of secrets, intentions, and purposes. Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?﴾ [al-Mulk 67:14].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah is acquainted with the intentions that breasts conceal; He knows the motive behind your deed — whether it is for Allaah or for other than Him. So the beautifying of the outward with the corruption of the inward avails nothing before al-Khabier. This cultivates in the youth — at the age of building identity and image — that he should attend to his reality and not to his appearance.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that al-Khabier knows the truthfulness of your inner self and so rewards you for your intention even if people do not see your deed. Warning: that He is acquainted with the concealed [store] of your evil, your ostentation, and your ill intention — so nothing you hide is hidden from Him.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth that Allaah is acquainted with his inner realities and his intentions, so that the concern for rectifying the inward rather than beautifying the outward is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: The vigilant watchfulness over intention and the sincerity of the inward are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon truthfulness with Allaah.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to truthful speech in agreement with the inward, and to casting off duplicity and verbal hypocrisy, so that his tongue grows up truthful.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in sincerity of deed and in correcting the intention within it, and in abandoning affectation before people, so that his limbs act in accordance with his knowledge of Allaah’s intimate acquaintance.
The name of Allaah: al-Shakoer (the Most Appreciative)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Shakoer” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described as appreciating the little of His servant’s deed and so granting him abundant reward, multiplying the good deed, and praising the obedient and honoring them.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of recompensing the deed with its multiples.
The signification of entailment: It entails generosity, self-sufficiency, knowledge, and justice. Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Faatir 35:34], and He said: ﴿And whoever volunteers good — then indeed, Allaah is Appreciative and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:158].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah recompenses the little deed with much reward, and appreciates the servant’s obedience and does not let it go to waste; He gives for a single good deed tenfold, up to seven hundredfold, up to that which cannot be counted; He accepts the small and rewards it abundantly. So whoever knows that his Lord is Appreciative is energized for obedience, even if it be little.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that al-Shakoer does not let any deed go to waste, however small, but rather multiplies it — so do not belittle any act of kindness. Warning: that whoever meets the blessings of al-Shakoer with denial and ingratitude deserves the removal of the blessing and the descent of retribution.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: The youth is taught that Allaah appreciates the little deed and multiplies it, so that there is founded in his mind [the understanding] that every good — however small — is rewarded with Allaah.
Through purification of the soul: The love of Allaah al-Shakoer, energy for obedience, and gratitude for blessings are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon hope and thankfulness.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to abundant praise and thanks with his tongue for blessings, and to extolling Allaah, so that his tongue grows up thankful.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to give thanks for the blessing by acting in obedience to the Bestower, and to employ His blessings in what pleases Him, so that his limbs act in accordance with the love of al-Shakoer.
The name of Allaah: al-Muhaymin (the Overseeing Guardian)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Muhaymin” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah — the Watcher, the Preserver, the Witness over His creation; the One who stands over every soul for what it has earned, in full command over their affairs through the perfection of His awareness and His power.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attributes of watchfulness, preservation, witnessing, and standing over [all].
The signification of entailment: It entails knowledge, power, and might, and that everything is under His command and His awareness.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿He is Allaah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer﴾ [al-Hashr 59:23].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: al-Muhaymin gathers the meanings of the Watcher, the Preserver, and the Witness, with the addition of command and standing over [all]; He is aware of everything, overseeing it, and nothing escapes His grasp. So when the youth knows Allaah’s oversight, he senses that he is under His eye and within His grasp in every state.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that Allaah’s oversight has undertaken the preservation and care of whoever relies upon Him. Warning: that He oversees you and you are never absent from Him — so where is the escape from His oversight?
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth that Allaah is overseeing, in command, aware of everything, so that the perfection of [His] watchfulness is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: Awe of Allaah’s oversight and tranquillity in His care are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon vigilant mindfulness and reliance [upon Allaah].
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to the remembrance of Allaah and to keeping His oversight present in mind, so that his tongue grows up filled with mindfulness of Him.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in uprightness in secret and in public, out of his knowledge of Allaah’s oversight, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muhaymin.
The name of Allaah: al-Djabbaar (the Compeller)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Djabbaar” signifies, by correspondence, three meanings: highness and grandeur; subjugation and command; and the mending of the broken and the enriching of the poor. He is the Most High, the Subduer, who mends His servants and enriches them.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attributes of highness, subjugation, and mending.
The signification of entailment: It entails power, might, and mercy, and the submission of everything to His overwhelming majesty (djabaroet).
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allaah above whatever they associate with Him﴾ [al-Hashr 59:23].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: al-Djabbaar subdues everything by His overwhelming majesty, and along with His majesty He mends the hearts of the broken and enriches the poor; thus He combines subjugation and mercy. So when the youth knows Allaah’s overwhelming majesty, he submits to His grandeur, and when he is broken he takes refuge in Him to mend his brokenness.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that al-Djabbaar mends every broken one who takes refuge in Him, so seek His mending at your moment of weakness. Warning: that His overwhelming majesty subdues every arrogant tyrant who is domineering over His servants, so beware of tyranny.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: The youth is taught that overwhelming majesty belongs to Allaah, and that He mends the weak, so that submission to Allaah and mercy toward the weak are founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: Awe of Allaah’s overwhelming majesty and brokenness before Him are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon submission.
Through the training of the tongue: He is instilled with “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” in veneration, so that his tongue grows up submissive to al-Djabbaar.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained not to be domineering over people and to be gentle with the weak, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Djabbaar.
The name of Allaah: al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Mutakabbir” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah — the One singular in supreme greatness and grandeur, transcendent above the attributes of creation and their deficiencies. Supreme greatness belongs to Him alone as truth and perfection, while in the case of the creature it is a defect and a thing blameworthy.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of supreme greatness that befits Him.
The signification of entailment: It entails grandeur, might, and highness, and that supreme greatness is His cloak, over which He is not to be contended.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allaah above whatever they associate with Him﴾ [al-Hashr 59:23], and He said: ﴿And to Him belongs [all] grandeur within the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Djaathiyah 45:37].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Supreme greatness is an attribute of perfection belonging to Allaah alone, for He is the Magnificent, transcendent above every deficiency; whereas in the creature it is blameworthy arrogance, because he is a weak servant who magnifies himself with what is not his. So when the youth knows that supreme greatness belongs to Allaah alone, he becomes humble before Allaah and before creation, and detests arrogance within himself.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that whoever humbles himself before Allaah, Allaah raises him — so humility is the path to might with Him. Warning: that supreme greatness is Allaah’s cloak, and whoever contends with Him over it by arrogance toward creation, He punishes him; and none shall enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth that supreme greatness belongs to Allaah alone, and that arrogance toward creation is blameworthy and forbidden, so that humility is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: Hatred of arrogance and love of humility for Allaah’s sake are planted in him, so that his soul grows up upon humbling itself before Allaah and humility toward creation.
Through the training of the tongue: He is accustomed to the word of humility and to casting off boasting and conceit in speech, so that his tongue grows up humble.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in humility in his walking, his sitting, and his dealings, and in casting off conceit, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Mutakabbir alone.
The name of Allaah: al-Qahhaar (the All-Subduer)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Qahhaar,” in the intensive form, signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah — the Prevailer over everything, the Subduer above His servants, before whom all creatures have submitted and yielded to His subjugation so that nothing is beyond His power.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of subjugation and complete prevailing.
The signification of entailment: It entails power, might, and grandeur, and the abasement and submission of everything before Him.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And He is the One, the Prevailing﴾ [al-Ra3d 13:16], and He said: ﴿To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allaah, the One, the Prevailing﴾ [Ghaafir 40:16].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah is the Subduer above His servants, prevailing in His affair; He subdued the tyrants with death and annihilation. Every mighty one is abased before Him, and every strong one is weak before His subjugation. So when the youth knows Allaah’s subjugation, he submits to Him alone, and does not fear the subjugation of any creature in disobedience to the Creator.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that whoever seeks protection in al-Qahhaar, none can subdue him — so draw might from Him. Warning: that Allaah’s subjugation is above every power, so do not feel secure from His devising if you disobey Him, for He subdues whoever disobeys Him.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: The youth is taught that all subjugation belongs to Allaah, and that every strong one is subdued before Him, so that there is founded in his mind [the understanding] that awe-filled fear is due to Allaah alone.
Through purification of the soul: Awe of Allaah’s subjugation and submission to Him are planted in him, so that his emotion grows up upon the fear of Allaah rather than of creation.
Through the training of the tongue: He is instilled with the veneration of Allaah and the drawing of might from Him, so that his tongue grows up submissive to al-Qahhaar.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained not to fear creation in [matters of] the truth, and to submit to Allaah’s command, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Qahhaar.
The name of Allaah: al-3Alie (the Most High)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-3Alie” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah exalted above His creation by the three kinds of highness: the highness of the Essence (for He is above His creation, established over His Throne), the highness of rank (for He has no peer), and the highness of subjugation (for everything is beneath His subjugation).
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of highness in its kinds.
The signification of entailment: It entails grandeur, might, and power, and the lowliness of all besides Him in relation to Him.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255], and He said: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Grand﴾ [Saba’ 34:23].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah is exalted above His creation in Essence, in rank, and in subjugation; there is none higher than Him and nothing above Him. So when the highness of Allaah becomes firmly rooted in the heart of the youth, he raises his aspiration to Him alone, and his heart does not submit to any lower than Him, and he knows that true elevation lies in attachment to al-3Alie.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that whoever attaches himself to al-3Alie, his rank is elevated — so seek elevation through His obedience. Warning: that whoever behaves arrogantly on the earth without right has contended with al-3Alie over His highness, so He abases him.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth the highness of Allaah above His creation and His aboveness, so that the transcendence of Allaah and His highness are founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: The emotion of venerating al-3Alie and loftiness of aspiration toward Him are planted in him, so that his soul grows up upon attachment to the Most High.
Through the training of the tongue: He is instilled with “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,” reflecting upon it, so that his tongue grows up upon venerating [Allaah’s] highness.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to raise his aspiration toward lofty matters and to abandon base ones, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-3Alie.
The name of Allaah: al-Kabier (the Most Great)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Kabier” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, Great in His Essence and His attributes with the supreme greatness of grandeur and majesty. He is greater than everything, and everything besides Him is small and lowly.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and of the attribute of supreme greatness and grandeur.
The signification of entailment: It entails highness, grandeur, and might, and the obligation of magnifying and revering Him.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿[He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra3d 13:9], and He said: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Grand﴾ [Saba’ 34:23].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah is greater than everything; when the servant says “Allaah is greater,” he affirms that He is greater than all that occupies him or turns him away. So when the heart of the youth is filled with the supreme greatness of Allaah, everything besides Him becomes small in his eyes, and he gives precedence to His command over every whim.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that whoever magnifies Allaah in his heart, the world becomes insignificant to him and he attains His good pleasure. Warning: that whoever is turned away from Allaah’s command by what is smaller than Him has been ignorant of the supreme greatness of Allaah.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth that Allaah is greater than everything, so that giving precedence to Allaah over everything is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: The emotion of magnifying Allaah and revering Him is planted in him, so that his soul grows up upon venerating Him above everything.
Through the training of the tongue: He is instilled with “Allaah is greater,” reflecting upon its meaning, so that his tongue grows up upon magnification (takbier).
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained to give precedence to Allaah’s command over every desire and distraction, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Kabier.
The name of Allaah: al-Muta3aalie (the Supremely Exalted)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
The signification of correspondence: “al-Muta3aalie” signifies, by correspondence, the Essence of Allaah exalted above every deficiency, likeness, and equal, elevated above what the wrongdoers and the deniers say. He is too magnificent and too majestic for any description to encompass Him or for any intellect to grasp Him.
The signification of implication: It comprises the affirmation of the Essence and its exaltedness above deficiencies and equals.
The signification of entailment: It entails highness, supreme greatness, and freedom from imperfection, and the falsehood of every deficiency ascribed to Him.
The evidences from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿[He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra3d 13:9], and He said: ﴿Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Nahl 16:1].
The scholarly and exhortative explanation: Allaah is exalted above all that does not befit Him: above partner and offspring, above deficiency and incapacity, and above the intellects’ encompassing of His true reality. So when the youth knows Allaah’s exaltedness, he declares Him free of imperfection in his heart and on his tongue, and does not dare to describe Him with what does not befit Him.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: that declaring al-Muta3aalie free of imperfection and venerating Him is among the noblest acts of worship. Warning: that ascribing deficiency to Him or associating [partners] with Him is a transgression against His exaltedness.
The pedagogical application through the four tracks in this group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the youth the exaltedness of Allaah above every deficiency and likeness, so that complete freedom from imperfection [ascribed to Him] is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: The emotion of declaring al-Muta3aalie free of imperfection and revering Him is planted in him, so that his soul grows up upon venerating Him.
Through the training of the tongue: He is instilled with “glorified and exalted is He” as a declaration of [Allaah’s] freedom from imperfection, so that his tongue grows up declaring [Him] free of imperfection.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained in venerating the rites of Allaah and in hallowing His station in his deeds, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muta3aalie.
The name of Allaah: al-Madjied (the All-Glorious)
The meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Madjied” (the All-Glorious) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of glory (majd); and glory is the vastness of His attributes and their greatness, and the abundance of good and beneficence. He is thus the Possessor of nobility, greatness, and generosity.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of glory, which combines greatness and generosity.
Signification by entailment: It entails greatness, generosity, might, and praise.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾ [al-Buroedj 85:15]; and He said concerning the People of the House: ﴿Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable﴾ [Hoed 11:73].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The glory of Allaah combines the greatness of His attributes and the vastness of His generosity; He is the Magnificent in His Essence, the Generous in His giving, the Praised in His deeds. So when the young learner comes to know the glory of his Lord, he venerates Him, loves Him, and praises Him as He deserves.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the All-Glorious honors whoever venerates and praises Him, so praise Him for His glory. Warning: whoever is heedless of the glory of Allaah and His greatness has fallen short in fulfilling His right.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The glory of Allaah, His greatness, and the vastness of His generosity are firmly established in the young learner, so that the joining of His veneration and His love is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of venerating the All-Glorious, loving Him, and praising Him is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon reverence and love.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to praise Allaah for His glory (as in the tashahhud: “madjied” — glorious), so that his tongue is nurtured upon glorifying Him.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to magnify the command of Allaah and to excel in doing good in emulation of His glory, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the All-Glorious.
The Name of Allaah: al-Hamied (the Praiseworthy)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Hamied” (the Praiseworthy) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, who is praised in every state, deserving of praise in His Essence, His attributes, and His deeds; He is praised even if the creation does not praise Him, for praise is an attribute inseparable from His perfection.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and its deserving of absolute praise.
Signification by entailment: It entails the perfection of all His attributes (for praise is for perfection) and absolute self-sufficiency.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿And know that Allaah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:267]; and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Hadjdj 22:64].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is praised for His blessings and His trials, in His giving and His withholding, because all His deeds are wisdom, justice, and mercy. So when the young learner comes to know that his Lord is Praiseworthy, he praises Him in every state — in ease out of gratitude, and in hardship out of contentment.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Praiseworthy increases those who praise Him out of His bounty: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]﴾. Warning: whoever denies the praise of Allaah and is ungrateful for His blessings deserves their removal.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is praised in every state, so that praising Him in ease and hardship is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of praise and contentment is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon praising Allaah in every state.
Through training the tongue: He is accustomed to abundantly saying “al-hamdu lillaah” (all praise is due to Allaah) in every state, so that his tongue is nurtured upon praising.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to use the blessings of Allaah in what pleases Him as an act of gratitude, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Praiseworthy.
The Name of Allaah: al-Waahid (the One)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Waahid” (the One) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, singular in oneness in His Essence, His attributes, His deeds, and His divinity; He has no partner, no peer, and no likeness. He is alone in creation, governance, and the right to be worshipped.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, its singularity, and the negation of any partner.
Signification by entailment: It entails the falsehood of every object of worship besides Him, and that worship is His right alone.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿and He is the One, the Prevailing﴾ [al-Ra3d 13:16]; and He said: ﴿And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:163].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is One in His lordship, so there is no creator besides Him; One in His divinity, so there is no rightful object of worship other than Him; One in His names and attributes, so there is no likeness to Him. This is the foundation of tawhied upon which the entire religion turns. So when the tawhied of the One takes firm root in the heart of the young learner, he devotes worship, love, fear, and hope to Him alone.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever affirms the oneness of Allaah and associates no partner with Him will enter Paradise, so make your tawhied sincere. Warning: associating partners with the One is the gravest of sins, unforgiven for the one who dies upon it.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The tawhied of Allaah and His singularity are firmly established in the young learner, so that the foundation of tawhied and the renunciation of shirk are founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The love of the One and devoting worship to Him alone are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon sincerity.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “laa ilaaha illaa Allaah” (there is no deity worthy of worship except Allaah) while pondering its meaning, so that his tongue is nurtured upon affirming oneness.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to devote worship to Allaah alone (supplication, sacrifice, vows, and reliance), so that his limbs act in accordance with the tawhied of the One.
The Name of Allaah: al-Ahad (the Unique)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Ahad” (the Unique) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, singular with a singularity in which nothing shares; He is the Unique who admits neither multiplicity, nor division, nor likeness, alone in His absolute perfection.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and its uniqueness, which has no peer.
Signification by entailment: It entails the negation of any likeness, equal, or offspring, and the perfection of singularity.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, “He is Allaah, [who is] One, Allaah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent.”﴾ [al-Ikhlaas 112:1-4].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Uniqueness (ahadiyyah) is more specific than oneness (waahidiyyah); He is the Unique who has no equal, no rival, and no likeness; He neither begets nor is born. Soerat al-Ikhlaas equals a third of the Qur’an because of the affirmation of this foundation that it contains. So when the young learner comes to know the uniqueness of Allaah, he declares Him free of all resemblance and likeness.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever realizes the uniqueness of Allaah in his tawhied is upon the foundation of salvation. Warning: whoever likens Allaah to His creation or sets up a rival to Him has strayed from the truth.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is Unique, having no likeness, so that declaring Him free of any likeness is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The love of the Unique and the veneration of His singularity are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon pure tawhied.
Through training the tongue: He is accustomed to reciting ﴿Say, “He is Allaah, [who is] One”﴾ and pondering it, so that his tongue is nurtured upon affirming His uniqueness.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to make his deeds sincerely for Allaah alone, without ostentation, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Unique.
The Name of Allaah: al-Samad (the Eternal Refuge)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Samad” (the Eternal Refuge) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, the Master perfect in His sovereignty, the One sought in [the fulfilment of] needs, to whom all creatures turn and upon whom they depend while He depends on no one; the Perfect in all His attributes.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, the perfection of its sovereignty and self-sufficiency, and the dependence of creation upon it.
Signification by entailment: It entails absolute self-sufficiency and the perfection of the attributes, and that everything is dependent upon Him.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Allaah, the Eternal Refuge﴾ [al-Ikhlaas 112:2]; and He (glorified is He) is Free of need of His creation, while all besides Him depends upon Him: ﴿O mankind, you are those in need of Allaah, while Allaah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Faatir 35:15].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: al-Samad is the perfect Master whom all creatures seek in their needs and to whom they turn in adversity, while He is Free of need of them: He neither eats, nor drinks, nor is in need; perfect in His knowledge, His forbearance, and His power. So when the young learner comes to know that his Lord is the Eternal Refuge, he seeks Him alone in his needs, and his heart depends on none besides Him.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Eternal Refuge fulfils the needs of whoever seeks Him, so seek Him alone. Warning: whoever seeks another for that which none but Allaah is able to grant has made himself dependent upon one as incapable as himself.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is the One sought in [the fulfilment of] needs, Free of need of all things, so that confining his seeking to Him alone is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of dependence upon the Eternal Refuge and of being enriched by Him from [need of] creation is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon attachment to Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to ask Allaah alone in his needs, so that his tongue is nurtured upon seeking the Eternal Refuge.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to raise his needs to Allaah without abasing himself before any creature, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Eternal Refuge.
The Name of Allaah: al-Hayy (the Ever-Living)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Hayy” (the Ever-Living) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah described with complete, perfect life that is touched by neither death, nor sleep, nor deficiency; a life that entails the perfection of all His attributes.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of perfect life.
Signification by entailment: It entails the perfection of knowledge, power, will, hearing, and sight (for perfect life entails the perfection of the attributes), and that He does not die.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Allaah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255]; and He said: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾ [al-Furqaan 25:58].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The Ever-Living who does not die is most deserving of being relied upon and worshipped; every living being besides Him dies, while He is the Everlasting. So when the young learner comes to know that his Lord is the Ever-Living who does not die, he attaches himself to Him rather than to the perishing creation, and places his trust in the One who does not pass away.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Ever-Living who does not die remains for you when everything perishes, so attach yourself to Him. Warning: whoever attaches himself to a living being that dies is forsaken at its death, so rely upon none but the Ever-Living, the Everlasting.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is Ever-Living, who neither dies nor sleeps, and that all besides Him is bound for perishing, so that attachment to the Everlasting is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of attachment to the Ever-Living and of tranquility in Him is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon reliance on Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “yaa Hayyu yaa Qayyoem, bi-rahmatika astaghieth” (O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek relief), so that his tongue is nurtured upon attachment to the Ever-Living.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to attach his hope and his deeds to Allaah rather than to the perishing creation, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Ever-Living.
The Name of Allaah: al-Qayyoem (the Sustainer of All Existence)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Qayyoem” (the Sustainer of all existence) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, self-subsisting, sustaining everything besides Him; He is Free of need of all else, the Upholder and Governor of every existent, by whom everything subsists.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of His self-subsistence and His sustaining of all else.
Signification by entailment: It entails absolute self-sufficiency, power, and knowledge, and the dependence of everything upon Him in its existence and its continuance.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Allaah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255]; and He said: ﴿And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾ [Taahaa 20:111].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: al-Qayyoem is self-subsisting, in need of none, and sustaining all else, so that everything is dependent upon Him in its existence and its continuance; were He to entrust the creation to itself for the blink of an eye, it would perish. So when the young learner comes to know that the subsistence of everything is by Allaah, he depends upon Him with every breath.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Sustainer upholds your affair and governs it when you entrust it to Him, so rely upon Him. Warning: whoever imagines that he subsists by himself or by other than Allaah is ignorant of his absolute dependence upon the Sustainer.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is self-subsisting, sustaining all things, and that everything subsists by Him, so that absolute dependence [upon Him] is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of dependence upon the Sustainer and of reliance on Him is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon attachment to Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “yaa Hayyu yaa Qayyoem” (O Ever-Living, O Sustainer) in his supplication, so that his tongue is nurtured upon [expressing] dependence on the Sustainer.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to entrust his affairs to Allaah, who sustains all things, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Sustainer.
The Name of Allaah: al-Qawiyy (the All-Strong)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Qawiyy” (the All-Strong) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah described with perfect strength and power; He is the All-Strong whom nothing can thwart, and whom no weakness, incapacity, or fatigue can touch.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of perfect strength.
Signification by entailment: It entails power, might, and dominance, and the weakness of all besides Him before Him.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Hadjdj 22:40]; and He said: ﴿Indeed, it is Allaah who is the [continual] Provider, the firm possessor of strength﴾ [al-Dhaariyaat 51:58].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The strength of the entire creation before the strength of Allaah is as nothing; whoever draws strength from the All-Strong becomes strong, and whoever is left to his own strength becomes weak. So when the young learner comes to know that all strength belongs to Allaah, he draws it from Him for [the sake of] obeying Him and striving against his own soul, and is not deluded by his own strength.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever seeks aid from the All-Strong is empowered over that which would otherwise overwhelm him, so draw your strength from Him. Warning: the strength of Allaah is above every strength, so do not employ your strength in disobeying Him, for He is stronger than you.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that all strength belongs to Allaah, and that his own strength is a blessing to be used as an aid toward obedience, so that the right directing of strength is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The resolve to seek aid from the All-Strong is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon strength in [upholding] the truth.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “laa hawla wa-laa quwwata illaa billaah” (there is no might nor power except through Allaah), so that his tongue is nurtured upon drawing strength from his Lord.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to direct his strength toward obedience and to restrain it from the forbidden, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the All-Strong.
The Name of Allaah: al-Matien (the Firm in Strength)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Matien” (the Firm in Strength) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, intense in a strength that neither ceases nor weakens; He is the All-Strong with a firm, unwavering strength that no feebleness or slackening can touch.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the intensity and firmness of its strength.
Signification by entailment: It entails complete power, might, and self-sufficiency, and the perpetuity of His strength without cessation.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is Allaah who is the [continual] Provider, the firm possessor of strength﴾ [al-Dhaariyaat 51:58].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The strength of Allaah is firm and intense, reached by neither weakness nor cessation; He is the All-Strong who does not grow feeble, the Firm in Strength whose grip does not diminish. So when the young learner comes to know the firmness of Allaah’s strength, he fears Him with the fear He truly deserves, and takes reassurance that whoever is taken into the care of the All-Strong, the Firm in Strength, will never be forsaken.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever takes refuge in the strength of the Firm in Strength finds it never cut off from him, for it is a strength that does not weaken. Warning: the grip of the Firm in Strength is intense, unbearable, so beware lest He seize you with His strength.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah’s strength is intense and firm, never ceasing, so that the perfection of fearing Him and relying upon Him is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): Awe of Allaah’s strength and reassurance in His aid are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon fear and reliance.
Through training the tongue: He is accustomed to venerating Allaah and seeking aid through His strength, so that his tongue is nurtured upon venerating the Firm in Strength.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to remain steadfast in the truth, seeking aid through Allaah’s firm strength, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Firm in Strength.
The Name of Allaah: al-Awwal (the First)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Awwal” (the First) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, which has no beginning; He precedes everything, there being nothing before Him, the Eternal, the Pre-existent, without commencement.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and its absolute priority (awwaliyyah).
Signification by entailment: It entails His freedom from need of all else, and that everything besides Him is originated, created, and preceded by non-existence.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing﴾ [al-Hadied 57:3]. The Prophet ﷺ explained it with his saying: “You are the First, so there is nothing before You” (Narrated by Muslim, no. 2713).
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The priority of Allaah precedes everything, for He exists before every existent, there being nothing before Him; and everything besides Him is preceded by non-existence, brought into being by Allaah after it was not. So when the young learner comes to know the priority of Allaah, he realizes that everything people worship besides Him is originated and created, and thus he devotes worship to the Eternal, the First, alone.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the First, who precedes everything, is most deserving of being worshipped and relied upon. Warning: whoever worships an originated, created thing has abandoned the First, the Eternal, his Creator.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is the First, having no beginning, and that all besides Him is created, so that distinguishing the Creator from the created is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of venerating the First, the Eternal, and of attachment to Him is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon devoting [worship] to Him alone.
Through training the tongue: He is taught the supplication before sleep: “You are the First, so there is nothing before You,” so that his tongue is nurtured upon venerating the First.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to devote worship to Allaah, the Eternal, alone, rather than to originated creatures, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the First.
The Name of Allaah: al-Aakhir (the Last)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Aakhir” (the Last) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, which has no end; He is the Everlasting after the perishing of everything, there being nothing after Him, the Eternal who does not pass away.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and its absolute finality (aakhiriyyah).
Signification by entailment: It entails His everlastingness and perpetuity, and the perishing of all besides Him: ﴿Everyone upon it [the earth] will perish﴾.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate﴾ [al-Hadied 57:3]; and the Prophet ﷺ explained it: “And You are the Last, so there is nothing after You” (Narrated by Muslim, no. 2713).
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The finality of Allaah remains after the perishing of everything; when all who are in the heavens and the earth are destroyed, His noble Face remains. So when the young learner comes to know that his Lord is the Last, the Everlasting, he makes Him the goal toward which he strives, and knows that his return is to Him, and so prepares for meeting Him.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Last, the Everlasting, is your goal and your return, so work for meeting Him. Warning: everything besides Him perishes, so whoever makes his goal something perishing has lost, and whoever is heedless of the return to Him will regret.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is the Last, the Everlasting after the perishing of everything, and that the return is to Him, so that preparation for meeting Him is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of attachment to the Everlasting and of preparing for the return is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon working for the Hereafter.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “And You are the Last, so there is nothing after You,” so that his tongue is nurtured upon venerating the Last.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to work for what endures with Allaah rather than for what perishes, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Last.
The Name of Allaah: al-DHaahir (the Ascendant)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
