Signification by correspondence: “al-DHaahir” (the Ascendant) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, exalted above everything; He is the One above whom there is nothing, the Ascendant through His highness, His subjugation, and His dominance over every existent.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, its highness, and its ascendance above everything.
Signification by entailment: It entails highness, subjugation, and greatness, and the lowliness of everything beneath Him.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate﴾ [al-Hadied 57:3]; and the Prophet ﷺ explained it: “And You are the Ascendant, so there is nothing above You” (Narrated by Muslim, no. 2713).
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The ascendance of Allaah is His highness and His subjugation; He is above everything, there being nothing above Him, subjugating and dominant over every existent. So when the young learner comes to know the highness of Allaah and His ascendance, he submits to His greatness, and realizes that however high any creature may be above him, Allaah is above them all.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever takes refuge in the Ascendant, the Most High, is in the highest sanctuary. Warning: He is above everything, subjugating and dominant, so no fugitive can defy Him and none can escape Him.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The highness of Allaah and His ascendance above everything are firmly established in the young learner, so that the veneration of His highness is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): Awe of Allaah’s highness and submission to Him are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon reverence for Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “And You are the Ascendant, so there is nothing above You,” so that his tongue is nurtured upon venerating the Ascendant.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to submit to Allaah, the Most High, and not to be arrogant, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Ascendant.
The Name of Allaah: al-Baatin (the Intimate)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Baatin” (the Intimate) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, near and encompassing everything; He is the One nearer than whom there is nothing, closer to everything than anything else, aware of the innermost depths and hidden things.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, its encompassing, its nearness, and its awareness of hidden things.
Signification by entailment: It entails all-encompassing [knowledge], knowledge of innermost secrets, and that He is nearer to the servant than his jugular vein.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing﴾ [al-Hadied 57:3]; and the Prophet ﷺ explained it: “And You are the Intimate, so there is nothing nearer than You” (Narrated by Muslim, no. 2713).
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The intimacy of Allaah is His all-encompassing [knowledge] and His nearness; He encompasses everything, is aware of hidden matters and innermost secrets, nearer to the servant than his own self, with nothing intervening to veil Him. So when the young learner comes to know the nearness of Allaah and His all-encompassing [knowledge], he feels ashamed to disobey Him in secret, and finds intimacy in His nearness. Through these four names the all-encompassing [presence] of Allaah over existence — in time and in space — is completed.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever finds intimacy in the nearness of the Intimate, the All-Encompassing, finds a companionship that nothing can equal. Warning: He is aware of your secret, nearer to you than your own self, so do not make light of a sin committed in seclusion.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The nearness of Allaah, His all-encompassing [knowledge], and His awareness of hidden things are firmly established in the young learner, so that the perfection of watchfulness [of Allaah] (muraaqabah) in secret is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The sentiment of intimacy in Allaah’s nearness and of shyness before Him in private is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon excellence (ihsaan) in secret.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “And You are the Intimate, so there is nothing nearer than You,” so that his tongue is nurtured upon venerating the Intimate.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to remain upright in his seclusion because of Allaah’s nearness and awareness, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Intimate.
The Name of Allaah: al-Qaadir (the Able)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Qaadir” (the Able) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah described with perfect power over everything; nothing on earth or in heaven can thwart Him; He does what He wills, however He wills.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of all-encompassing power.
Signification by entailment: It entails knowledge, will, and strength, and the execution of His will in everything.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:20]; and He said: ﴿Say, “He is the [one] Able to send upon you affliction from above you”﴾ [al-An3aam 6:65].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The power of Allaah is all-encompassing, thwarted by nothing; He created the heavens and the earth, gives life to bones when they are decayed, and resurrects those in the graves. So when the young learner comes to know the perfection of Allaah’s power, he fears Him, is certain of His power over resurrection and recompense, and deems nothing of His promise or His threat far-fetched.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Able is able to grant you all that you hope for, so do not deem any request too small [to ask]. Warning: He is able to punish you whenever He wills, so do not feel secure from His power when you disobey Him.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah is able over all things, thwarted by nothing, so that certainty in His power over resurrection is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): Awe of Allaah’s power and hope in His power are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon fear and hope.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to venerate the power of Allaah, so that his tongue is nurtured upon certainty in His power.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to act in accordance with certainty in Allaah’s power over recompense, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Able.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muqtadir (the Perfect in Ability)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Muqtadir” (the Perfect in Ability) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, perfect in power, reaching the utmost in ability; it is more emphatic than “al-Qaadir,” His ability being complete, neither opposed nor overcome.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the perfection of its ability.
Signification by entailment: It entails strength, might, and knowledge, and the completeness of dominance and execution.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability﴾ [al-Qamar 54:55]; and He said: ﴿so We seized them with a seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability﴾ [al-Qamar 54:42].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: The ability of Allaah is complete and utmost; when He seizes the wrongdoers, He seizes them with the seizure of One Exalted in Might, Perfect in Ability, letting none escape; His dominion is that of a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability, unchallenged. So when the young learner comes to know the completeness of Allaah’s ability, he stands in awe of Him, is not deluded by His granting of respite, and is certain that His seizure is severe.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: the Perfect in Ability delivers whoever seeks refuge in Him with an ability that cannot be overcome. Warning: the seizure of the Perfect in Ability upon the wrongdoers is severe, with no escape from it, so beware of being among them.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The completeness of Allaah’s ability and the inescapability of His seizure are firmly established in the young learner, so that awe of His punishment is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): Fear of Allaah’s ability is instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon wariness of disobedience.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to venerate and fear Allaah, so that his tongue is nurtured upon awe of the Perfect in Ability.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to abandon wrongdoing out of fear of the seizure of the Perfect in Ability, so that his limbs act in accordance with His veneration.
The Name of Allaah: al-Noer (the Light)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Noer” (the Light) — by correspondence it denotes that Allaah is Light, that His veil is light, that He has illumined the heavens and the earth, and that by His light He has guided the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth — in a manner befitting His majesty, without any resemblance [to creation].
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, the attribute of light befitting Him, and that He is the Illuminator of all else.
Signification by entailment: It entails guidance and perfection, and that every light — sensory or immaterial — is from Him.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Allaah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Noer 24:35].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is Light, and His veil is light; from Him comes the light of guidance by which the people of faith see their path, and the light of the heavens and the earth, both sensory and immaterial; whoever is deprived of His light remains in darkness. So when the young learner comes to know that guidance is a light from Allaah, he seeks it from Him, and strives after that which increases the light of his heart through obedience.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: whoever seeks the light of Allaah through obedience, Allaah illumines his heart, his grave, and his path. Warning: disobedience extinguishes the light of the heart and bequeaths darkness.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young learner that Allaah has illumined the universe and guided by His light, and that guidance is a light from Him, so that seeking light from Allaah is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The love of the light of faith and the aversion to the darkness of disobedience are instilled in him, so that his soul is nurtured upon seeking the light.
Through training the tongue: He is taught “Allaahumma idj3al fie qalbie noeran” (O Allaah, place light in my heart), so that his tongue is nurtured upon seeking the light.
Through training the limbs: He is trained upon acts of obedience that increase the light of the heart, and upon abandoning what extinguishes it, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Light.
The Name of Allaah: al-Baaqie (the Everlasting)
Its meaning and its three modes of signification:
Signification by correspondence: “al-Baaqie” (the Everlasting) — by correspondence it denotes the Essence of Allaah, perpetual, which neither perishes nor passes away; He is the Everlasting after the perishing of His creation, the Eternal whose existence has no end.
Signification by inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the perpetuity of its everlastingness.
Signification by entailment: It entails the perfection of life and self-sufficiency, and the perishing of all besides Him.
The proofs from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah the Exalted said: ﴿Everyone upon the earth will perish, And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor﴾ [al-Rahmaan 55:26-27].
The scholarly and exhortatory exposition: Allaah is Everlasting, He does not perish, while all besides Him is bound for cessation; wealth perishes, bodies decay, and what remains is His noble Face. So when the young learner comes to know that the Everlasting is Allaah alone, he works for what endures with Him, and does not prefer what perishes over what endures.
Encouragement and warning: Encouragement: what is with the Everlasting endures, so work for what lasts with Him and does not perish. Warning: everything besides Him perishes, so whoever prefers the perishing over the Everlasting has lost.
The pedagogical application through the four paths within this age group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah is the Everlasting and that everything else is perishing, so that the preference of the Everlasting over the perishing is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is planted in him the emotion of attachment to the Everlasting and detachment from the perishing, so that his soul is raised upon working for the Hereafter.
Through training the tongue: He is habituated to the remembrance of Allaah, the Everlasting, and to His veneration, so that his tongue grows up attached to the Everlasting.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to prefer the enduring righteous deeds over the perishing enjoyment of this world, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Everlasting.
The Name of Allaah: al-Walie (The Protecting Ally)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Walie” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who takes charge of His believing servants with aid, protection, and support, and who manages their affairs; so He is their Helper, their Protector, and the Administrator of their affairs.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of guardianship (wilaayah) and aid.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and mercy, and the aid of whoever takes Him as ally.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allaah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:257], and He said: ﴿and He is an ally of the righteous﴾ [al-A3raaf 7:196].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah takes charge of the believers: He aids them, protects them, and brings them out from the darknesses of disbelief and doubt into the light of faith; whoever has Allaah as his ally, there is no fear upon him. So when the young person knows that Allaah is his ally, he allies himself to Him through obedience, seeks His aid rather than that of creatures, and knows that the guardianship of Allaah is attained through faith and piety (taqwaa).
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that whoever allies himself to Allaah, He takes charge of him, aids him, and protects him, so seek His guardianship through piety. And Warning: that whoever allies himself to the enemies of Allaah, or takes another as ally, has renounced the guardianship of Allaah.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah is the ally of the believers and their helper, so that the seeking of Allaah’s guardianship through obedience is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the love of Allaah’s guardianship and pride in His aid, so that his soul is raised upon attachment to Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “Allaah is our Protector (mawlaa)” and “an excellent Protector,” so that his tongue grows up taking pride in the guardianship of Allaah.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to ally with the allies of Allaah and to show enmity toward what Allaah shows enmity to, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Walie.
The Name of Allaah: al-Waarith (The Inheritor)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Waarith” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah that remains after the perishing of His creation, to which the ownership of everything returns after the passing of its owners; so He is the Everlasting who inherits the earth and whoever is upon it.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and its remaining after the perishing of every owner.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails permanence and self-sufficiency, the perishing of all besides Him, and the return of ownership to Him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned﴾ [Maryam 19:40].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah inherits the earth and whoever is upon it; every owner’s ownership passes away and the ownership of Allaah remains, everything returns to Him after the perishing of its possessors. So when the young person knows that all ownership returns to Allaah, he is not deluded by the wealth in his hand, and knows that he is but a steward over it, so he spends it in what pleases its true Owner.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that whatever you have sent forth to the Inheritor remains for you with Him. And Warning: that whatever you have amassed you will leave behind, and Allaah will inherit it, so do not be miserly with it away from His obedience.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that all ownership returns to Allaah, and that he is but a steward over what is in his hand, so that the absence of delusion by wealth is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of detachment from the perishing and working for the Everlasting, so that his soul is raised upon giving.
Through training the tongue: He is habituated to the remembrance of Allaah, the Everlasting, the Inheritor, so that his tongue grows up undeluded by this world.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to spend what Allaah has made him steward over in His obedience, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Waarith.
The Name of Allaah: al-Badie3 (The Originator)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Badie3” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who originated creation and brought it into being upon no prior model; so He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth and of the marvels of craftsmanship within them.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of origination and bringing into being upon no model.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails knowledge, power, and wisdom, and His being uniquely alone in origination.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿[He is] the Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and it is﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:117].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah originated the heavens and the earth upon no prior model, and deposited within them of the marvels of His craftsmanship that which points to His greatness; so every marvel in the universe is a trace of His origination. So when the young person contemplates the marvels of Allaah’s creation, he increases in veneration for their Originator, and knows that this mastery cannot be in vain nor without a Maker.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that contemplating the marvels of Allaah’s craftsmanship increases faith and bequeaths love of Him. And Warning: that whoever sees these marvels and then denies their Maker, his heart has gone blind.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah originated the universe upon no model, so that inferring the Maker from the craftsmanship is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of wonder at Allaah’s origination and love of Him, so that his soul is raised upon veneration.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to glorify [Allaah] (tasbieh) upon seeing the marvels of creation, so that his tongue grows up glorifying al-Badie3.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to contemplate the creatures of Allaah and to take heed from them, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Badie3.
The Name of Allaah: al-Rashied (The Guide to Right Conduct)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Rashied” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah whose actions are all right guidance, soundness, and wisdom, the One who guides His servants to right conduct (rushd), who directs whoever seeks His direction; from Him proceeds no folly nor error.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, the perfection of right guidance in its actions, and its directing of the servants.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails knowledge, wisdom, and guidance.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and [that] He may guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath 48:2], and He said: ﴿you will never find for him a protecting guide﴾ [al-Kahf 18:17].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah is guiding (rashied) in His creation and His command; He directs His servants to that in which lies their well-being, and whoever seeks His direction, He directs him; so all right conduct is from Him. So when the young person knows that right conduct is from Allaah, he seeks it from Him, follows His guidance, and does not follow his caprice that plunges him into error (ghayy).
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that al-Rashied directs whoever asks Him for right conduct, so seek it from Him in your perplexity. And Warning: that whoever leaves the direction of Allaah and follows his caprice strays from right conduct.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that right conduct and soundness are from Allaah, so that seeking right conduct from his Lord and following His guidance is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the love of right conduct and hatred of error, so that his soul is raised upon seeking guidance.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “O Allaah, direct me to the right conduct of my affair,” so that his tongue grows up seeking right conduct.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to follow right conduct and to abandon what plunges him into error, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Rashied.
The Name of Allaah: al-Muntaqim (The Avenger)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Muntaqim” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who punishes the disobedient, criminal, persistent offenders with the severest punishment through His justice; and this name is not applied to Him in isolation, rather it is said: “Possessor of retribution (dhoe intiqaam)” or “the Avenger against the criminals,” for His vengeance is a matter of justice against the people of criminality after respite.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of just retribution against the criminals.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails justice, might, and power, and that His vengeance is by right after the establishment of the proof (hudjdjah).
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals﴾ [al-Sajdah 32:22], and He said: ﴿And Allaah is Exalted in Might, Possessor of Retribution﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:4].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So the vengeance of Allaah is only against the criminals who turn away, after respite and warning; it is justice, not injustice, and His mercy precedes His wrath, so He takes vengeance only against whoever persists and disbelieves. So when the young person knows that Allaah has retribution against the criminals, he fears the consequence of persisting in disobedience, and hastens to repentance before the vengeance befalls him.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that whoever repents before the vengeance is safe, for repentance repels the vengeance. And Warning: that Allaah’s vengeance against the persistent is severe after respite, so let not His forbearance delude you into persisting.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that Allaah takes vengeance against the persistent criminals through His justice, so that the fear of the consequence of persistence is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him dread (khashyah) of Allaah’s vengeance for disobedience, so that his soul is raised upon hastening to repentance.
Through training the tongue: He is habituated to seeking forgiveness and repenting, so that his tongue grows up oft-returning [in repentance] (awwaab) before the vengeance.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to abandon acts of disobedience and to hasten to repentance out of dread of the vengeance, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Muntaqim.
The Name of Allaah: al-Ghanie (The Free of Need)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Ghanie” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah that is sufficient in itself, independent of all besides it with absolute self-sufficiency; so He is the Free of need of the worlds, He needs no one for anything, and everything is in dire need of Him.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the perfection of its absolute self-sufficiency.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails the perfection of the attributes, power, and sovereignty, and the neediness of all besides Him toward Him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allaah is the Free of need, while you are the needy﴾ [Muhammad 47:38], and He said: ﴿O mankind, you are those in need of Allaah, while Allaah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Faatir 35:15].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah is free of need of His creation with absolute self-sufficiency; the obedience of the obedient does not benefit Him, nor does the disobedience of the disobedient harm Him — their obedience is for them and their disobedience is against them. So when the young person knows that his Lord is free of need of him, he knows that his worship is for the benefit of his own self and not out of any need of Allaah, and that he is the poor one in need of the Free of need with every breath.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that the Free of need enriches whoever is in need of Him from His treasuries that never run out. And Warning: that Allaah is free of need of you and of your obedience, so if you turn away He will replace you with another people.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that Allaah is free of need of everything, and that creation is in need of Him, so that the perfection of neediness toward Allaah is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of neediness toward the Free of need, so that his soul is raised upon humbling itself before Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to ask of Allaah and to express his neediness toward Him, so that his tongue grows up in need of the Free of need.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to raise his needs to Allaah, the Free of need, without abasing himself before one poor like himself, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Ghanie.
The Name of Allaah: al-Mughnie (The Enricher)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Mughnie” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who enriches whomever He wills of His servants, driving wealth to him from His bounty; so He is the One who enriched and made content, no one enriches another except by His leave.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of enriching.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails absolute self-sufficiency, generosity, and power, and that all enrichment is from Him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And that it is He who enriches and grants contentment﴾ [al-Najm 53:48], and He said: ﴿And if you fear poverty, then Allaah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:28].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So the Enricher enriches the poor from His bounty, and places in the heart a richness that is better than the richness of wealth; for true richness is the richness of the soul. So when the young person knows that the Enricher is Allaah, he seeks richness from Him, and his heart does not attach itself to the means, and he knows that the greatest richness is that Allaah enrich his heart of any need for what is in the hands of people.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that the Enricher enriches you from His bounty if you ask Him and rely upon Him. And Warning: that whoever seeks richness from other than Allaah, or through the unlawful, is deprived of its blessing.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: The young person is taught that richness is from Allaah, and that the richness of the soul is better than the richness of wealth, so that seeking richness from Allaah is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of attachment to the Enricher and of contentment, so that his soul is raised upon richness of the heart.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “O Allaah, enrich me by Your bounty of any need for any besides You,” so that his tongue grows up seeking richness from Allaah.
Through training the limbs: He is trained upon contentment and seeking lawful richness from Allaah, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Mughnie.
The Name of Allaah: al-Djaliel (The Majestic)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Djaliel” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described with the attributes of majesty, greatness, and grandeur; so He is the Magnificent before whom everything is diminished, the Possessor of majesty who fills the hearts with awe.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attributes of majesty and greatness.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails greatness, grandeur, and might, and the obligation of revering and venerating Him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor﴾ [al-Rahmaan 55:27], and He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor﴾ [al-Rahmaan 55:78].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So al-Djaliel is the Possessor of the attributes of majesty: greatness, grandeur, might, and subjugation, which fill the heart with awe and reverence; majesty is the attributes of greatness, and honor is the attributes of bounty, so He is the Possessor of Majesty and Honor. So when the heart of the young person is filled with the majesty of Allaah, he reveres Him, venerates Him, and stands in awe of Him, so that he does not dare to disobey Him nor to take His command lightly.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that whoever reveres Allaah in his heart, Allaah honors him and draws him near. And Warning: that whoever does not revere Allaah nor venerate Him is ignorant of His majesty.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the young person the majesty of Allaah and His greatness, so that His reverence and veneration is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him awe of the majesty of Allaah and reverence of Him, so that his soul is raised upon veneration.
Through training the tongue: He is taught the veneration of Allaah and reverence of Him (“Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor”), so that his tongue grows up revering Allaah.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to venerate the rites of Allaah and His sanctities, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Djaliel.
The Name of Allaah: al-Haqq (The Truth)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Haqq” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah that is firmly established, truly existent, which no falsehood nor passing away befalls; so He is the Truth in His Essence, His attributes, His actions, and His words, and His worship is the truth, and all besides Him is falsehood.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence, its firm establishment, and its absolute reality.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails the perfection of existence and the attributes, and the falsehood of everything worshipped besides Him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿For that is Allaah, your Lord, the Truth. And what can be beyond truth except error?﴾ [Yoenus 10:32], and He said: ﴿and they will know that it is Allaah who is the manifest Truth﴾ [al-Noer 24:25].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah is the Truth, the firmly established that does not pass away, and His existence is the truest of existence, and His worship is the truth, and everything worshipped besides Him is false and passing; for what is beyond the truth except error? So when the young person knows that his Lord is the Truth, he holds fast to His true religion, and does not turn to falsehood however many its adherents.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that whoever holds fast to the truth, Allaah makes him firm and he prospers. And Warning: that whatever is other than the truth is false and passing, so whoever prefers it over the truth loses.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah is the Truth, and His religion is the truth, and all besides it is falsehood, so that the discernment between truth and falsehood is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him love of the truth and hatred of falsehood, so that his soul is raised upon holding fast to the truth.
Through training the tongue: He is habituated to speaking the truth and supporting it, so that his tongue grows up uttering the truth.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to follow the truth and to remain firm upon it even if people oppose him, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Haqq.
The Name of Allaah: al-Wakiel (The Disposer of Affairs)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Wakiel” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah upon whom hearts rely in their affairs, the Guarantor of the provisions of His servants and their interests, the One who undertakes everything with protection and management; so whoever entrusts his affair to Him, He suffices him.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of undertaking the affairs of whoever relies upon Him.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails power, knowledge, and sufficiency, and that whoever relies upon Him, He suffices him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and sufficient is Allaah as Disposer of affairs﴾ [al-Nisaa’ 4:81], and He said: ﴿Those to whom people said, “Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.” But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, “Sufficient for us is Allaah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs”﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:173].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah is the best Disposer of affairs for whoever entrusts his affair to Him; He suffices him, manages his affair, and protects him. Reliance upon Him (tawakkul) is a great act of worship that combines sincere dependence upon Allaah with the exertion of the means. So when the young person knows that his Lord is the Disposer of affairs, he consigns his affair to Him after exerting what he is able of the means, and his heart is at ease and he does not fear creatures.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that whoever relies upon the Disposer of affairs, He suffices him and is enough for him, for He is the best Disposer of affairs. And Warning: that whoever relies upon other than Allaah is consigned to it and forsaken.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him, so that reliance [upon Him] together with the exertion of the means is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of dependence upon the Disposer of affairs and tranquility toward Him, so that his soul is raised upon reliance.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “Sufficient for us is Allaah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs,” so that his tongue grows up relying [upon Him].
Through training the limbs: He is trained to exert the means while consigning the outcome to Allaah, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Wakiel.
The Name of Allaah: al-Haadie (The Guide)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Haadie” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah who guides His servants: the guidance of indication and clarification for all creation, and the guidance of divine enabling and inspiration (tawfieq and ilhaam) for whomever He wills of the believers; so all guidance is in His hand.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the two attributes of guidance: clarification and divine enabling.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails knowledge, mercy, and wisdom, and that the guidance of hearts is in His hand alone.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper﴾ [al-Furqaan 25:31], and He said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allaah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 28:56].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah is the Guide; He guides by clarification and indication all creation through the sending of the messengers and the sending down of the books, and He guides by divine enabling the hearts of whomever He wills, expanding them for faith; even the Prophet ﷺ does not possess the guidance of divine enabling for anyone. So when the young person knows that guidance is from Allaah, he seeks it from Him in every prayer, does not rely upon himself, and knows that his steadfastness upon guidance is a favor from Allaah.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that the Guide guides whoever seeks guidance and turns toward Him, so ask Him for guidance always. And Warning: that whoever turns away from the guidance of Allaah, He consigns him to himself, so he strays.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that all guidance is from Allaah, so that seeking guidance from his Lord and neediness toward it is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him love of guidance and neediness toward the Guide, so that his soul is raised upon seeking steadfastness.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “Guide us to the straight path,” reflecting [upon it], so that his tongue grows up seeking guidance.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to follow guidance and to guide others to it (indication toward the good), so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Haadie.
The Name of Allaah: al-Waadjid (The Resourceful)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Waadjid” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah, the Free of need, whom nothing eludes and who is in need of nothing, who finds all that He wills and whom no object of desire escapes; so He is the Free of need, the All-Powerful, whose resourcefulness is complete and perfect.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the perfection of its self-sufficiency and power, so that nothing eludes it.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails self-sufficiency, power, and knowledge, and that He is in need of nothing and nothing escapes Him.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Its meaning is established by what indicates the perfection of Allaah’s self-sufficiency and power; Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allaah is the Free of need, while you are the needy﴾ [Muhammad 47:38], and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allaah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:20], and this name is among those counted within the ninety-nine.
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So al-Waadjid is Free of need, nothing He wills eludes Him, and He is in need of no one; All-Powerful, He finds all that He wills, no object of desire incapacitates Him. So when the young person knows that his Lord is al-Waadjid whom nothing escapes, he becomes needy toward Him, seeks from Him what he himself is incapable of, and knows that His treasuries never run out.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that al-Waadjid finds for you what you seek and nothing incapacitates Him, so do not deem any request too small before Him. And Warning: that whoever considers himself independent of al-Waadjid, the Free of need, is ignorant of his own poverty.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah is Free of need, whom nothing eludes, All-Powerful, whom nothing escapes, so that the perfection of neediness toward Him is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of neediness toward al-Waadjid, so that his soul is raised upon attachment to Him.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to ask of Allaah from His abundance, so that his tongue grows up in need of Him.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to raise his needs to Allaah, whom nothing incapacitates, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Waadjid.
The Name of Allaah: al-Maadjid (The All-Glorious)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Maadjid” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of glory (majd), that is, greatness together with generosity and nobility; it is close to “al-Madjied,” so He is the Great, the Generous, abundant in good and beneficence.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of glory, combining greatness and generosity.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails greatness, generosity, and might.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Its meaning is established by what indicates the glory of Allaah, His greatness, and His generosity; Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾ [al-Buroedj 85:15], and He said: ﴿Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious﴾ [Hoed 11:73], and this name is among those counted within the ninety-nine.
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So al-Maadjid is the Possessor of perfect glory: the Great in His Essence, the Generous in His giving, the One who combines majesty and honor; so His glory combines the greatness of the attributes and the amplitude of generosity. So when the young person knows the glory of his Lord, he venerates Him and loves Him, and praises Him with His glory, and combines in his heart awe and love.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that al-Maadjid honors whoever venerates Him and praises Him. And Warning: that whoever is heedless of the glory of Allaah and His greatness has fallen short in His right.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: There is firmly established in the young person the glory of Allaah, His greatness, and His generosity, so that the combining of His veneration and love is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of venerating al-Maadjid and loving Him, so that his soul is raised upon reverence and love.
Through training the tongue: He is taught to praise Allaah with His glory, so that his tongue grows up glorifying [Him].
Through training the limbs: He is trained to venerate the command of Allaah and to do good in emulation of His glory and generosity, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Maadjid.
The Name of Allaah: Maalik al-Mulk (Owner of Sovereignty)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “Maalik al-Mulk” — denoting, by way of correspondence, that Allaah is the absolute Owner of all sovereignty, the One who disposes of it however He wills; He gives sovereignty to whom He wills and strips it from whom He wills, unopposed in His sovereignty.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and its absolute, disposing ownership.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails power, might, and wisdom, and the efficacy of His disposal over all sovereignty.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, “O Allaah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will … In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent”﴾ [Aal 3Imraan 3:26].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So Allaah is the Owner of all sovereignty; He gives sovereignty to whom He wills and strips it from whom He wills, He honors and He abases, in His hand is all good; so every king on earth, his kingship is but a loan from the Owner of Sovereignty. So when the young person knows that all sovereignty belongs to Allaah, he is not deluded by any kingship nor rank, and knows that what is in the hands of people is to be reclaimed, so he submits to the Owner of Sovereignty alone.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that the Owner of Sovereignty gives to whoever obeys Him sovereignty and might in both abodes. And Warning: that He strips sovereignty from whoever becomes tyrannical through it, so let no one be deluded by what he has been given.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that all sovereignty belongs to Allaah, who disposes of it however He wills, so that the absence of delusion by this world is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of submission to the Owner of Sovereignty and detachment from its passing [portion], so that his soul is raised upon submission.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “O Allaah, Owner of Sovereignty,” reflecting [upon it], so that his tongue grows up venerating Allaah.
Through training the limbs: He is trained upon submission to Allaah and humility regarding whatever blessing he has been given, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Owner of Sovereignty.
The Name of Allaah: Dhoe al-Djalaal wa-l-Ikraam (Possessor of Majesty and Honor)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “Dhoe al-Djalaal wa-l-Ikraam” — denoting, by way of correspondence, that Allaah is the Possessor of Majesty (the attributes of greatness and grandeur that are held in awe) and the Possessor of Honor (the attributes of bounty and beneficence that are loved, and that He honors His allies and is [Himself] honored and venerated); so He combines that for which He is held in awe and that for which He is loved.
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the two attributes of majesty and honor together.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails greatness, generosity, might, and mercy, and that He is worthy to be revered and honored.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: Allaah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor﴾ [al-Rahmaan 55:27], and He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor﴾ [al-Rahmaan 55:78].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So He is the Possessor of Majesty who is held in awe for His greatness, and the Possessor of Honor who is loved for His bounty and beneficence; so He combines the two attributes, so His right is that He be revered and held in awe, and that He be honored and loved, and that He honor His allies. This name combines the perfection of awe and love. So when the young person knows his Lord as the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, he combines in his heart his fear of Him and his hope in Him, and his awe of Him and his love of Him.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that the Possessor of Honor honors whoever reveres Him and obeys Him with the greatest honoring. And Warning: that the Possessor of Majesty — His majesty is held in awe, so whoever does not stand in awe of His majesty exposes himself to His punishment.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging: It is firmly established in the young person that Allaah is Possessor of majesty that is held in awe and honor that is loved, so that the combining of awe and love is founded in his mind.
Through purification of the soul: There is planted in him the emotion of combining the fear of [His] majesty and the hope in [His] honor, so that his soul is raised balanced between fear and love.
Through training the tongue: He is taught [to say] “O Possessor of Majesty and Honor” in his supplication, so that his tongue grows up combining veneration and hope.
Through training the limbs: He is trained to venerate the sanctities of Allaah (out of [awe of His] majesty) and to hope in His bounty (out of [His] honor), so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of the Possessor of Majesty and Honor.
The Name of Allaah: al-Saboer (The Patient)
The Meaning and Its Three Denotations:
The Denotation of Correspondence: “al-Saboer” — denoting, by way of correspondence, the Essence of Allaah described with the perfection of patience; it is His forbearance toward the disobedient, and His not hastening to punish them despite the perfection of His power over that; a patience conjoined with the perfection of knowledge, power, and might, not out of incapacity nor heedlessness. A number of the scholars have affirmed this name by derivation from the authentic hadith, and it is close to al-Haliem (the Forbearing).
The Denotation of Inclusion: It includes the affirmation of the Essence and the attribute of patience together with the perfection of power.
The Denotation of Entailment: It entails power, forbearance, knowledge, and might, and that His patience is out of perfection, not out of incapacity.
The Evidence from the Book and the Sunnah: The Prophet ﷺ said: “There is none more patient over an injury he hears than Allaah; they attribute a child to Him, yet He grants them well-being and provides for them.” (Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhaarie (no. 7378) and Muslim (no. 2804)). And the Book affirmed its like from forbearance: ﴿And Allaah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:235].
The Scholarly and Exhortatory Explanation: So the patience of Allaah is the greatest of patience; He hears whoever ascribes to Him a child and a partner — which is the greatest of injuries — then He does not hasten to punish them, but rather grants them well-being and provides for them, hoping for their repentance; a patience out of the perfection of power, knowledge, and might, not out of incapacity. So when the young person knows the patience of his Lord toward His servants, he seizes His forbearance through repentance, and takes on the character of patience over what he dislikes without incapacity.
Encouragement and Warning: Encouragement: that the patience of Allaah grants you respite so that you may set yourself right, so seize His respite before it comes to an end. And Warning: that His patience is not heedlessness nor neglect, so when He seizes the persistent [offender] after the respite, He seizes him with the seizing of One mighty and omnipotent.
The Pedagogical Application across the Four Tracks in this Age Group:
Through purging (tasfiyah): The young one is taught that Allaah’s patience with the disobedient proceeds from forbearance and power, not from incapacity, so that there is established in his mind the seizing of the respite granted and wariness against being deluded.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is instilled in him the sentiment of hastening to repent during the time of respite, and of adorning himself with patience, so that his soul is nurtured upon deliberateness and self-restraint.
Through the upbringing of the tongue: He is accustomed to seeking forgiveness during the time of respite and to bearing harm patiently with good speech, so that his tongue is nurtured to be oft-returning [to Allaah] and forbearing.
Through the upbringing of the limbs: He is trained to be patient with what he dislikes without anxious dismay, and to seize the respite granted by Allaah through obedience, so that his limbs act in accordance with the veneration of al-Saboer (the Patient).
The detailed innate traits specific to this age stage, and how to direct them pedagogically towards the veneration of Allaah and the governance and direction of the deeds of the hearts
Children at this age stage possess a number of innate traits, among them:
1. Increased capacity for advance planning: He draws up plans for activities or projects and considers the probable outcomes.
Method of direction: We link planning to the intention of seeking Allaah’s pleasure, and we teach him that the believer orders his day just as he orders his path to Paradise.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that planning is an act of worship when it is coupled with the intention of Allaah’s pleasure. He clarifies for him that the believer orders his day just as he orders his path to Paradise.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart [the truth] that Allaah’s disposing of affairs is greater than his own planning. He rejoices before him when he links his plan to the obedience of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “in shaa’ Allaah (if Allaah wills)” with every plan. He asks him to repeat it before every project.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to draw up a plan for his day that includes a time for worship. He reviews it with him and praises him for his commitment.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught to plan while making the matter contingent upon the will of Allaah, so that he is led to take the means and to entrust the outcomes to Him.
Through leading the emotions: There is instilled in him tranquil trust in Allaah’s disposing of affairs alongside his own good planning, so that his emotion is nurtured upon reliance [upon Allaah].
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to plan for what pleases Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Planning for good is made beloved to him, and planning for falsehood is kept away from him, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient in carrying out his plans and not to be hasty for their fruit.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to press on with his plans and to counsel himself towards perseverance, so that he neither hastens for the fruit nor counsels others to rush.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to carry out his plan at its ordered times without haste, so that he is accustomed to disciplining his time and honouring his schedule.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan makes him promises and stirs vain desires in him, so that he is accustomed not to plan for disobedience and to seek the aid of Allaah.
2. Love of intellectual independence: He inclines to form his own opinion, even if it opposes the opinion of his parents.
Method of direction: We instill in him [the truth] that the greatest intellectual independence is following the truth, and that Allaah loves the one who governs his intellect by the light of revelation (wahy).
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that the greatest intellectual independence is following the truth. He clarifies for him that Allaah loves the one who governs his intellect by the light of revelation.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of the truth even if it opposes his desire. He rejoices before him when he yields an opinion in deference to the Sacred Law.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say “The truth is more deserving to be followed” at the time of disagreement. He repeats it with him in [various] situations.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to present his opinion to the Sacred Law before adopting it. He makes that a tangible habit.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught that the greatest intellectual independence is following the truth, so that his intellect is led to liberation from caprice through submission to revelation.
Through leading the emotions: The love of the truth is instilled in him even if it opposes his desire or the opinion of people, so that his emotion is nurtured upon preferring the truth.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to seek the truth for the sake of Allaah and not in vindication of himself, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The truth that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and falsehood is made hateful to him even if it is adorned in the name of freedom, so that he grows upon loving and hating for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient in seeking the truth and returning to it, and in respecting his parents alongside his right to an opinion.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to counsel his parents with courtesy and respect if he has an opinion, so that he presents the truth gently, without harshness or obstinacy.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to choose the suitable time to present his opinion to his parents, so that he does not thrust it upon them at a time when they are preoccupied.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan making opposition to the truth seem attractive to him in the name of independence, so that he is taught that [true] freedom lies in servitude to Allaah.
3. The growth of critical awareness: He asks about the reason behind rules and instructions.
Method of direction: We teach him that the religion is built upon wisdom, and that asking about the wisdom increases veneration of Allaah and understanding of His commands.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that the religion is built upon wisdom. He clarifies for him that asking about the wisdom increases him in veneration of Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart submission alongside the seeking of wisdom. He rejoices before him at an act of obedience even if he does not grasp the entire wisdom.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say “We hear and we obey, and perhaps within the wisdom is that which we do not know.” He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to carry out the legislated command and then to search for its wisdom. He praises him for [his] submission.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught that the religion is built upon wisdom, and that asking about the wisdom increases faith, so that his intellect is led to the veneration of the wisdom of the Lawgiver.
Through leading the emotions: Tranquil trust in Allaah’s wisdom within His rulings is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon contentment and submission.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to submit to the command of Allaah for the sake of Allaah while seeking the wisdom, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: Yielding out of love to what Allaah has commanded is made beloved to him, and it is made clear that submission is among the necessary concomitants of love, so that he grows upon love for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience and submission where the intellects fall short of grasping the wisdom.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to submit to Allaah where the intellects fall short, so that he counsels himself not to reject a ruling whose wisdom he has not grasped.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained not to waste his time in disputation over that which the intellects of humankind cannot reach, so that he directs it towards what is beneficial.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against a whispering [of Satan] that would make him reject the command of Allaah on account of not understanding its wisdom, so that he is taught the difference between critique and casting doubt.
4. The strength of conceptual memory: He memorises meanings and links them to events.
Method of direction: We seize [the opportunity of] his memory to instill the meanings of the beautiful names of Allaah and the episodes of the prophetic biography (sierah) that revive the heart.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator invests the memory of the young one in the memorisation of the beautiful names of Allaah and their meanings. He links his memorisation to pleasing Allaah.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of the names of Allaah and the episodes of the sierah. He rejoices before him when he is moved by them.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He has him memorise one of the names of Allaah along with its meaning each week. He asks that it be repeated daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He supplicates with him using the name of Allaah suited to the situation. He makes that a daily disposition.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: His memory is seized to instill the meanings of the beautiful names of Allaah and the episodes of the sierah, so that through the meanings he has stored up he is led to the knowledge of his Lord.
Through leading the emotions: What he stores up of the meanings of the names is linked to the love of Allaah and His veneration, so that his emotion is nurtured upon [His] exaltation.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to memorise the meanings in order to act upon them for the sake of Allaah, not for disputation, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: His store of meanings is filled with the beneficial knowledge that Allaah loves, and the storing up of falsehood is kept away from him, so that his memory grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience in acquiring the meanings, linking them, and reviewing them.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to study together with his companions and to counsel them to link the meanings and review them, so that he counsels through his very state, by his perseverance in [seeking] knowledge.
Through the disciplining of time: Regular times are designated for acquiring knowledge and reviewing it, so that his understanding becomes firmly rooted through constancy upon his [allotted] time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against his memory being filled with specious doubts (shubuhaat) that Satan casts, so that his store of meanings is filled with the meanings of tawhied.
5. A deepening in the concept of justice: He perceives that some situations may be “just” even if their outward appearance seems unequal.
Method of direction: We teach him that Allaah is absolute justice, and that what appears to us outwardly as an unjust apportionment may be a rabbaanie wisdom.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that Allaah is absolute justice. He clarifies for him that what appears to be an unjust apportionment may be a rabbaanie wisdom.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart contentment with the judgement of Allaah. He rejoices before him when he submits to the decree (qadar) of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “Allaah is the most just of judges.” He repeats it with him at [the arising of] specious doubts.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him upon fairness in his dealings with his siblings. He makes justice a daily disposition.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught that Allaah is absolute justice, and that whatever aspect of it is hidden, its wisdom lies with Allaah, so that he is led to contentment with His justice and to fairness in his own judgement.
Through leading the emotions: Tranquil trust in Allaah’s justice and His wisdom in what is hidden is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon submission.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to [act with] justice for the sake of Allaah and not to be praised, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The justice that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and injustice is made hateful to him, so that he grows upon loving and hating for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience and contentment with the decree of Allaah if the aspect of justice is hidden from him.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained upon contentment with the decree of Allaah if the aspect of justice is hidden from him, so that he counsels himself to think well of his Lord.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained not to consume his time in objecting to what is hidden from him, so that he directs it towards contentment and action.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan casting him into objecting to the wisdom of Allaah when the aspect of justice is hidden.
6. The expansion of social concern: It is not confined to the family but extends to the school and society.
Method of direction: We make him feel that the veneration of Allaah includes doing good to people, and that a righteous society is a path to collective worship.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that the veneration of Allaah includes doing good to people. He clarifies for him that a righteous society is a path to collective worship.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of benefiting people for the sake of Allaah. He rejoices before him when he serves his community.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say “I do good to people for the sake of Allaah” at [the time of] social work. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He involves him in a beneficial social act (cleaning a mosque, assisting someone in need). He makes it a disposition.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is made to feel that the veneration of Allaah includes doing good to people and the reform of society, so that he is led to realise his religion within his surroundings.
Through leading the emotions: The love of reform and of benefiting society is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon gathering together for good.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to benefit society for the sake of Allaah and not for reputation, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: Cooperation upon righteousness with the people of faith is made beloved to him, and cooperation upon sin is kept away from him, so that he grows upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience in reform and upon enduring the harm of people.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to strive in reform and to counsel people gently, and to endure their harm without reproach or despair.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to direct his time towards beneficial reform, so that he does not waste it in complaint or in returning harm for harm.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan divides and sows corruption among people, so that he is accustomed to reform and to preserving the community.
7. An increase in awareness of general moral values: such as truthfulness, trustworthiness, and courage.
Method of direction: We nourish these values by linking them to the Qur’aan and the Sunnah, and [by teaching] that they are commands from Allaah, not merely social morals.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that values are commands from Allaah, not merely social morals. He links them to the Qur’aan and the Sunnah.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of truthfulness, trustworthiness, and courage for the sake of Allaah. He rejoices before him at any deed of them.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “Truthfulness and trustworthiness are part of faith.” He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him upon truthfulness and trustworthiness in every situation. He praises him for the value by linking it to the pleasure of Allaah.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: His values of truthfulness, trustworthiness, and courage are nourished by linking them to the command of Allaah, so that he is led [to understand] that they are acts of worship, not merely noble traits.
Through leading the emotions: The love of these values is instilled in him because Allaah loves them, so that his emotion is nurtured upon what is good and wholesome.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to adorn himself with them for the sake of Allaah and not to be praised for them, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The character traits that Allaah loves are made beloved to him, and their opposites are made hateful to him, so that he grows upon loving and hating for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience in holding firm to values even if people oppose [him].
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to hold firm to his values even if people oppose [him], and to counsel them towards these values with wisdom, not by going along [with them].
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained not to squander his time in what contradicts his values in order to please people, so that he holds firm to what benefits him.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan makes the opposites of these values seem attractive, so that holding fast to them is made beloved to him as a means of repelling him [Satan].
8. A deeper perception of the long-term consequences of actions: He knows that negligence today may affect the morrow.
Method of direction: We firmly root in him [the truth] that Paradise and the Fire are the results of today’s deeds, and that Allaah does not let the reward of one who does good work go to waste.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that Paradise and the Fire are the results of today’s deeds. He clarifies for him that Allaah does not let the reward of one who does good go to waste.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the sense of responsibility for every action. He rejoices before him at [any] reflection upon the consequence.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say “What is the consequence of this with Allaah?” before [taking] a decision. He instructs him in the question.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him upon self-reckoning before sleep. He makes it a fixed routine.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: It is firmly rooted in him that Paradise and the Fire are the results of today’s deeds, and that Allaah does not let any deed go to waste, so that through heeding the consequence he is led to godfearingness (taqwaa).
Through leading the emotions: Hope for a good consequence and fear of an evil one are instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon watchfulness [of Allaah] (muraaqabah).
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to work for the abiding consequence for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: That whose consequence is praiseworthy with Allaah is made beloved to him, and that whose consequence is evil is made hateful to him, so that he grows upon loving and hating for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience and upon giving precedence to the abiding consequence over the fleeting pleasure.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to prefer the abiding consequence, so that he counsels himself and others to give precedence to the beneficial deferred [reward] over the fleeting immediate [one].
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to direct his time towards that whose consequence abides, so that he does not consume it in a fleeting pleasure that leaves no trace.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan beautifies the immediate [life] and makes one forget the Hereafter, so that he is accustomed to considering the ultimate outcomes.
9. Love of challenge: in sport, competitions, and intellectual discussions.
Method of direction: We direct him [to understand] that the true challenge lies in striving against the soul for the obedience of Allaah and in holding firm upon faith.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that the true challenge lies in striving against the soul for the obedience of Allaah. He redirects his inclination towards that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of striving against the soul. He rejoices before him when he triumphs over his caprice.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “I challenge my own soul for the obedience of Allaah.” He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He makes available to him challenges in good (memorising the Qur’aan, the night prayer). He praises him for [his] striving.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: His love of challenge is directed [to understand] that the greatest challenge is striving against the soul for the obedience of Allaah, so that his resolve is led towards the struggle against the soul.
Through leading the emotions: The joy of triumph over the soul and Satan is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon the love of striving.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to challenge his soul for the sake of Allaah and not for boasting, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: Challenge in the good that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and taking risks in disobedience is kept away from him, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience and steadfastness in facing challenges without despair.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained upon steadfastness amid challenges, so that he counsels himself against despair and towards trust in the aid of Allaah.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to divide the challenge over gradual [intervals of] time, so that he overcomes it through perseverance within his [allotted] time rather than through collapse.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that the most hostile of his enemies is his own soul that lies between his two sides, and Satan, so that his challenge is directed towards striving against them both.
10. The increasing importance of social acceptance: He cares about the opinion of friends.
Method of direction: We guide him [to understand] that the pleasure of Allaah is more important than the pleasure of people, and that Allaah loves the one who gives precedence to His obedience over praise and acceptance.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that the pleasure of Allaah is more important than the pleasure of people. He clarifies for him that Allaah loves the one who gives precedence to His obedience over praise.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the seeking of Allaah’s pleasure first. He rejoices before him when he abandons a going-along [with peers] that opposes the Sacred Law.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “The pleasure of Allaah is more important than the pleasure of people.” He repeats it with him at [times of] peer pressure.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him not to go along with peers in falsehood. He praises him for his steadfastness.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
