Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is guided [to understand] that the pleasure of Allaah is more important than the pleasure of people, so that he is led to weigh acceptance by the scale of the Sacred Law and not by the caprices of people.
Through leading the emotions: His eagerness for acceptance is disciplined so that it does not carry him to go along with falsehood, and the preferring of Allaah’s pleasure is instilled in him.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to work for the pleasure of Allaah and not for the acceptance of friends, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The acceptance of the people of faith is made beloved to him, and seeking the pleasure of the people of falsehood at the cost of the wrath of Allaah is kept away from him, so that he grows upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience in opposing the group when they are upon falsehood.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to oppose the group if they are upon falsehood and to counsel them with the truth, so that he does not go along with evil out of fear of opposing them.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained not to let the time [spent with] the group sweep him into falsehood, so that he safeguards his time through companionship that aids him upon the truth.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan employs peer pressure to drag him towards evil, so that he is accustomed to steadfastness upon the truth.
11. The ability to control the emotions for a longer period: compared with the earlier stages.
Method of direction: We link this to self-restraint for the sake of Allaah, and [teach] that whoever suppresses his rage for the sake of Allaah magnifies Allaah in his heart.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that self-restraint for the sake of Allaah is among the things that magnify Allaah in the heart. He clarifies for him that whoever suppresses his rage for the sake of Allaah, He raises him [in rank].
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of suppressing rage for the sake of Allaah. He rejoices before him when he controls his anger.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “I seek refuge in Allaah from the accursed Satan” at [the time of] anger. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him upon silence and ablution (wudoe’) at [the time of] anger. He makes that his manner.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: His control of his emotions is linked to its being for the sake of Allaah, so that he is led [to understand] that whoever suppresses his rage for the sake of Allaah, Allaah exalts him, so that his soul is led towards forbearance.
Through leading the emotions: He is taught to direct the emotion rather than to repress it: anger in its proper place, and joy in obedience, so that his feelings become upright.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to control his emotions in watchfulness of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The forbearance that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and blameworthy agitation is made hateful to him, so that he grows upon loving and hating for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience and the suppression of rage in [times of] hardship.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to suppress rage in [times of] hardship, so that he counsels himself towards forbearance and away from corrupting agitation.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to grant himself time to calm down at [the moment of] rage, so that he controls his agitation and does not act in the heat of the moment.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that anger is from Satan, so that he is accustomed to seeking refuge [in Allaah], to stillness, and to ablution at [its onset].
12. Emotional responsiveness to moving stories: He may be affected, or his eyes may well with tears, upon hearing moving accounts.
Method of direction: We employ this to strengthen faith through the Qur’aanic and prophetic stories, so that his heart may grow humble and increase in love for Allaah.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator invests the young one’s emotional responsiveness in strengthening faith through the Qur’aanic and prophetic stories. He explains them to him with care.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart humility and love for Allaah at [the telling of] the stories. He rejoices before him when he is moved by them.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to recount the lesson of the story to his siblings. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He, together with him, follows a lesson from the story in real life. He makes that a practical entrenchment.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: His emotional responsiveness is employed in strengthening faith through the Qur’aanic and prophetic stories, so that through the humility of his heart he is led to the veneration of Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: Tenderness of heart and its awe are instilled in him upon hearing the verses of Allaah and His exhortations, so that his emotion is nurtured upon humble submission.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to benefit from the exhortation for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: That which softens the heart of what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and that which hardens it is kept away from him, so that he grows familiar with good.
Through patience: He is trained to translate his emotional response into action rather than a mere tear, so that he is accustomed to patience upon obedience.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained to translate his emotional response into action and not a passing tear, so that he counsels himself to follow the feeling with obedience.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to channel the effect of the exhortation, in its [own] moment, into a righteous deed, so that his emotional response does not go to waste.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan stirring his emotions towards falsehood, so that his emotional response is directed towards the truth.
13. Love of heroic role models, both real and historical: such as the prophets, the Companions, and [great] leaders.
Method of direction: We present to him role models who venerated Allaah and submitted to Him, so that he may know that true heroism lies in the obedience of Allaah and steadfastness upon the truth.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator presents to the young one role models who venerated Allaah and submitted to Him. He clarifies for him that heroism lies in the obedience of Allaah and steadfastness upon the truth.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of the prophets, the Companions, and the righteous leaders. He rejoices before him when he is moved by them.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to recount the story of a Companion hero each week. He instructs him in the stories.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He, together with him, emulates a deed from the heroic feats of the Companions. He makes that a disposition.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: Role models who venerated Allaah and submitted to Him are presented to him, so that he is led [to understand] that true heroism lies in servitude to Allaah.
Through leading the emotions: The love of the true heroes from among the people of faith is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon the veneration of the people of good.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to emulate them for the sake of Allaah, and he is taught that the axis of their heroism rests upon their sincerity, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The friends (awliyaa’) of Allaah from among the prophets, the Companions, and the [righteous] leaders are made beloved to him, and their enemies are made hateful to him, so that he grows upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: The episodes of their patience and steadfastness are brought to his attention, so that patience is made beloved to him and is emulated.
Through sincere counsel: The episodes of the patient ones are brought to his attention so that he emulates them, and he is counselled to convey them to others so that they may benefit from their steadfastness.
Through the disciplining of time: A regular time is designated for the biographies of the steadfast, so that the love of emulating them becomes firmly rooted through constancy.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught from their biographies how they struggled against the enemies of Allaah, so that he is made acquainted with his enemy and they are emulated in repelling him.
14. The beginning of concern for personal reputation.
Method of direction: We teach him that a good reputation is a provision from Allaah, and that the fundamental principle in his intention is to please Allaah, not people.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that a good reputation is a provision from Allaah. He clarifies for him that the fundamental principle in his intention is to please Allaah, not people.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart care for the inner self. He rejoices before him when he purifies his inner being.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He instructs him to say “O Allaah, make me better than what they think.” He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him upon a righteous deed that he conceals from people. He praises him for [his] sincerity in secret.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is taught that a good reputation is a provision from Allaah, and that the fundamental principle in his intention is seeking the Face of Allaah, so that he is led to seek good praise as a consequence and not as an aim.
Through leading the emotions: His eagerness for reputation is disciplined so that it does not turn into ostentation (riyaa’), and sincerity of purpose is instilled in him.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to work for the sake of Allaah and not for reputation, and he is taught the danger of the love of status, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: The sincerity that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and ostentation is made hateful to him, so that he grows upon loving and hating for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience in the face of people’s blame if he is upon the truth, and not to sell his religion for his reputation.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained upon patience in the face of blame if he is in the right, so that he counsels himself not to sell his religion for the sake of his reputation among people.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained not to occupy his time with what people say about him, so that he directs his concern towards perfecting his work and its sincerity.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that the love of status is a gateway to ostentation that Satan exploits, so that he is accustomed to sincerity in [his] work.
15. A better ability to work in organised groups.
Method of direction: We direct him [to understand] that cooperation upon righteousness and godfearingness is worship, and that Allaah loves the one who works with his brethren for His obedience.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator explains to the young one that cooperation upon righteousness is worship. He clarifies for him that Allaah loves the one who works with his brethren for His obedience.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of cooperation upon good. He rejoices before him when he cooperates in a righteous deed.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say “We cooperate upon righteousness and godfearingness.” He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing — the upbringing of the limbs
He involves him in a beneficial collective work. He makes cooperation upon good a disposition.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the soul and seeking knowledge: He is directed [to understand] that cooperation upon righteousness and godfearingness is worship, so that through his collective work he is led to what Allaah loves.
Through leading the emotions: The love of cooperating with his brethren upon good is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon brotherhood.
Through sincerity: He is accustomed to work with the group for the sake of Allaah and not to be seen, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal: Cooperation upon righteousness with the people of faith is made beloved to him, and cooperation upon sin is kept away from him, so that he grows upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained upon patience and excellence in collective work, and upon bearing with its members.
Through sincere counsel: He is trained upon excellence in collective work and upon counselling its members gently, and bearing with what issues from them.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to organise his time within collective work and to fulfil his role in it, so that he is accustomed to disciplining his time with his team.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan sows corruption among those who work [together], so that he is accustomed to reconciliation and to preserving the ranks of good.
16. The beginning of resistance to direct guidance: He prefers to be convinced rather than commanded.
Method of direction: We address him with wisdom and show him that Allaah is not pleased with him merely through outward obedience but through the conviction of the heart.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) addresses the young one with wisdom, not with bare commands. He clarifies to him that Allaah is pleased with him through an obedience born of conviction.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of obedience born of conviction. He rejoices before him when he obeys with understanding.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I obey Allaah out of conviction.” He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him in obedience after persuasion, not coercion. He praises him for his obedience born of understanding.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is addressed with wisdom, and it is clarified that Allaah is not pleased with merely coerced obedience but with heartfelt obedience, so he is led to submission born of conviction.
Through leading the emotions: The love of the truth of which he has become convinced is instilled in him, so his emotions grow upon preferring it.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to submitting to the truth for Allaah’s sake out of conviction, not merely to please the one directing him, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Submission to the command of Allaah out of love is made beloved to him, and he is taught that yielding is part of love, so he grows upon love for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in receiving direction, and in respecting the one who directs him while seeking persuasion.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to accept direction and to respect the one who directs him while courteously seeking persuasion, so that he neither rejects counsel out of arrogance nor accepts it without understanding.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to set aside a time for receiving direction and benefiting from it, so that he does not squander the opportunity to profit from the counsel of sincere advisers.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s making the rejection of truth seem fair to him under the pretext of a lack of conviction, so he is taught that the truth is to be accepted even from an opponent.
17. Increased capacity for keeping personal secrets.
The method of direction: We instill in him that keeping a secret is a trust (amaanah), and that Allaah loves the one who safeguards trusts and preserves the rights of others.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that keeping a secret is a trust. He clarifies to him that Allaah loves those who safeguard trusts.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of safeguarding the trust. He rejoices before him when he guards a secret.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “Trustworthiness is part of faith.” He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to safeguard what he is entrusted with. He makes the guarding of a trust a second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that keeping a secret is a trust, and that Allaah loves the safeguarding of trusts, so he is led to guard the trust for Allaah’s sake.
Through leading the emotions: The love of trustworthiness and the hatred of betrayal are instilled in him, so his emotions grow upon what is good.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to safeguarding the trust for Allaah’s sake and not to be praised, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The keeping of a secret and the trust which Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and the divulging of them is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in keeping what must be kept, even if it weighs heavily upon him.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to keep what must be kept, even if it weighs heavily upon him, so that he counsels himself to keep the secret and guard the trust.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to spend his time divulging what does not concern him, so that he guards his tongue and his time together.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan draws him toward divulging what causes harm, so he is accustomed to governing his tongue and keeping the secret.
18. A love for the practical experience of skills: such as carpentry, drawing, and using the computer.
The method of direction: We connect every skill to the mastery of work for the sake of Allaah’s countenance, and to the fact that every effort, when we intend it for Allaah, becomes an act of worship.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that mastering work for the sake of Allaah’s countenance is an act of worship. He clarifies to him that every effort intended for Allaah becomes an act of worship.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the love of excellence for Allaah’s sake. He rejoices before him when he masters a beneficial skill.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I master this for the sake of Allaah’s countenance,” before working. He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him in beneficial, lawful (halaal) skills. He connects them to the mastery of work for Allaah’s sake.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: Every skill is connected to the mastery of work for the sake of Allaah’s countenance, so that through his skill he is led to realize that every effort by which good is intended is an act of worship.
Through leading the emotions: His skill is connected to the veneration of the One who granted him the ability, so that his emotions grow upon gratitude rather than self-conceit.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to mastering the skill for Allaah’s sake and for the benefit of people, not for boasting, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): What is beneficial from that which Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept from employing the skill in what causes harm, so that he grows accustomed to good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and perseverance in mastering the skill.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to master his skill and to persevere in it, so that he counsels others toward excellence and counsels them by his own state through his perseverance.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to designate fixed times for practice, so that he develops his skill through steady diligence with his time and not through sporadic bursts.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against having his skill employed in what causes harm through Satan’s beautification, such as tampering with the computer in what is forbidden (haraam).
19. Being affected by signs of respect or humiliation: he regards it as an important personal matter.
The method of direction: We teach him that his true honor lies in the sight of Allaah, and that whoever humbles himself for Allaah, Allaah raises him, even if people humiliate him.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that his true honor lies in the sight of Allaah. He clarifies to him that whoever humbles himself for Allaah, Allaah raises him, even if people humiliate him.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart humility before Allaah. He rejoices before him when he bears a humiliation with gentleness.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “My honor lies in obedience to Allaah.” He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him in self-restraint when humiliated and in refraining from revenge. He praises him for his forbearance.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that his true honor lies in the sight of Allaah, and that whoever humbles himself for Allaah, Allaah raises him, so he is led to weigh his worth by obedience to his Lord.
Through leading the emotions: His being affected by humiliation is governed so that it does not drive him to blameworthy revenge, and forbearance is instilled in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to seeking his honor with Allaah and not with people, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): That which honors him with Allaah is made beloved to him, and the seeking of might through falsehood is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience over humiliation and in pardoning, and in not being deluded by honor.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to pardon when humiliated and not to be deluded by honor, so that he counsels himself that his worth lies with Allaah and not with people.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to squander his time avenging his honor, so that he directs it toward pardon and beneficial work.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan provokes his pride when he is humiliated, so he is accustomed to forbearance and pardon for Allaah’s sake.
20. The beginning of awareness of major world events: such as news and public affairs.
The method of direction: We connect this to the universal laws of Allaah in the cosmos, and to the fact that the believer has a role in reform, supplication, and action in accordance with the pleasure of Allaah.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one the universal laws of Allaah in the cosmos. He clarifies to him that the believer has a role in reform, supplication, and action in accordance with the pleasure of Allaah.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart concern for the affairs of the Muslims. He rejoices before him when he supplicates for his brethren.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to supplicate for the Muslims upon hearing news of them. He instructs him in that.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him in beneficial work for his ummah within the limits of his capacity. He makes that a second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: This is connected to the universal laws of Allaah in the cosmos, and to the fact that the believer has a role in reform and supplication, so he is led to weigh events by the revelation.
Through leading the emotions: Concern for the affairs of the Muslims and supplication for them are instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon the brotherhood of faith.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to caring about the affairs of the ummah for Allaah’s sake, not out of idle curiosity, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The support of the believers, even if only through supplication, is made beloved to him, and injustice and disbelief are made hateful to him, so he grows upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and trust in the victory of Allaah, and in not despairing at the ganging up of the enemies.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained in trusting the victory of Allaah and in not despairing at the ganging up of the enemies, so that he counsels himself to steadfastness and reliance upon Allaah (tawakkul).
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to consume his time in fear of the enemies, so that he directs it toward preparation and obedience.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that the truth has enemies who scheme and that the outcome of the matter rests with Allaah, so he is made to know the laws governing conflict and is fortified against despair.
21. The desire to shoulder greater responsibilities to prove one’s maturity.
The method of direction: We teach him that shouldering responsibility is a path to empowerment, and that Allaah does not grant leadership except to the one who has earned it.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that shouldering responsibility is a path to empowerment. He clarifies to him that Allaah does not grant leadership except to the one who has earned it.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the intention of serving people through responsibility. He rejoices before him when he shoulders a responsibility.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “This is a trust for Allaah,” when shouldering a responsibility. He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He entrusts him with real responsibilities suited to his age. He praises him for his trustworthiness.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that shouldering responsibility is a path to empowerment, and that Allaah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste, so he is led to bear the trust of servitude to Allaah (3uboediyyah).
Through leading the emotions: The delight of trustworthiness and the joy of being of benefit are instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon responsibility.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to bearing responsibility for Allaah’s sake and in hope of His reward, not to prove himself, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The fulfillment of the trust which Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and negligence is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in bearing responsibility and enduring its consequences.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to bear responsibility and endure its consequences, so that he counsels himself to discharge the trust and not to shirk it.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to organize his time so as to discharge his responsibilities in their due times, so that he becomes accustomed to the governance of time in bearing them.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan either discourages him or drives him to pride through responsibility, so he is accustomed to humility and steadfast vigilance (muraabatah).
22. A growing sense of the value and importance of time.
The method of direction: We instill in him that time is a blessing about which he will be questioned, and that the most precious thing on which it may be spent is seeking the pleasure of Allaah.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that time is a blessing about which he will be questioned. He clarifies to him that the most precious thing on which it may be spent is seeking the pleasure of Allaah.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart gratitude for time and the avoidance of wasting it. He rejoices before him when he invests a portion of time in obedience.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “O Allaah, bless my time.” He repeats it with him daily.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to schedule his day with time for worship and knowledge. He calls him to account gently for wasted time.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: It is instilled in him that time is a blessing about which he will be questioned, and that the most precious thing on which it may be spent is obedience to Allaah, so he is led to seize the opportunity of his lifetime.
Through leading the emotions: The love of seizing time and the hatred of wasting it are instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon earnest diligence.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to seizing his time for Allaah’s sake, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The spending of time in what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and the wasting of it in what He detests is made hateful to him, so that he grows accustomed to good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and perseverance in seizing his time in obedience.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to persevere in obedience and to counsel others to seize time, so that he counsels by his own state through his consistency in his devotional litanies (awraad).
Through the governance of time: He is trained to seize his time in obedience and to maintain his devotional litanies, so that he fills his day with what brings him nearer to Allaah.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan induces procrastination and wastes the times, so he is accustomed to promptness and to repelling procrastination.
23. The tendency to relate events to one’s personal beliefs.
The method of direction: We firmly establish in him that sound belief leads to sound understanding, and that Allaah guides the one who takes refuge in Him so as to show him the truth.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that sound belief leads to sound understanding. He clarifies to him that Allaah guides the one who takes refuge in Him so as to show him the truth.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the veneration of sound creed (3aqiedah). He rejoices before him when he refers events back to the scale of the Sacred Law (Sharie3ah).
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “Everything is by the decree of Allaah and His wisdom.” He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to understand events by the scale of sound creed. He makes that a second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: It is firmly established in him that sound belief leads to sound understanding, and that Allaah guides whoever follows the truth, so he is led to interpret events by his creed.
Through leading the emotions: The tranquility of sound creed amid the vicissitudes of events is instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon steadfastness.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to referring matters back to his creed for Allaah’s sake, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The interpretation of events by the scale of revelation is made beloved to him, and their interpretation by falsehood is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and steadfastness upon his creed amid tribulations (fitan) and events.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained in steadfastness upon his creed amid tribulations, so that he counsels himself to hold fast to the truth and not to waver.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to consume his time in that which shakes his certainty, so that he directs it toward the knowledge that firmly establishes his creed.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against specious doubts (shubuhaat) that link events to false interpretations propagated by the enemies of the creed, so that his understanding is founded upon the revelation.
24. An increased sense of responsibility toward younger children.
The method of direction: We connect it to the way (sunnah) of mutual mercy, and to the fact that Allaah is in the aid of the servant so long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the young one that Allaah is in the aid of the servant so long as he is in the aid of his brother. He connects it to the way (sunnah) of mutual mercy.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart mercy toward those younger than him. He rejoices before him when he shows mercy to those beneath him.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I show mercy to the young one for Allaah’s sake.” He repeats it with him.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He entrusts him with caring for a younger sibling or assisting him. He makes mutual mercy a daily second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: It is connected to the way of mutual mercy, and to the fact that Allaah is in the aid of the servant so long as he is in the aid of his brother, so he is led to care for those beneath him for Allaah’s sake.
Through leading the emotions: Mercy toward the younger ones and compassion for them are instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon gentleness.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to caring for the younger ones for Allaah’s sake and in hope of His reward, not for praise, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Kindness toward the young ones, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and wronging them is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in caring for the younger ones and bearing with them.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to care for the younger ones and to counsel them with gentleness and by example, so that he is patient with them and treats them well.
Through the governance of time: He devotes a portion of his time to caring for his younger siblings, so that he is accustomed to giving his time for their benefit and kindness toward them.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that he is a role model for those beneath him, so he is warned against being a doorway through which Satan brings evil to them.
25. Posing questions about customs, traditions, and religion.
The method of direction: We encourage him to question with the mind of one who seeks the truth, and we teach him that the religion is reason, innate disposition (fitrah), and a light from Allaah.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) encourages the young one to question with the mind of one who seeks the truth. He clarifies to him that the religion is reason, innate disposition (fitrah), and a light from Allaah.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart a tranquil certainty that the truth is with Islam. He rejoices before him when his certainty increases.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to question the people of knowledge about whatever perplexes him. He instructs him in the etiquette of questioning.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He takes him to the gatherings of knowledge for the answering of his questions. He makes easy for him the path of sound knowledge.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is encouraged to question with the mind of one who seeks the truth, and he is taught that the religion is reason and revelation, so he is led to distinguish which customs accord with the Sacred Law and which contradict it.
Through leading the emotions: A tranquil certainty that the truth lies in the revelation is instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon finding intimacy in the truth.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to seeking the truth in his questioning for Allaah’s sake and not for the sake of disputation, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Those customs that accord with the Sacred Law of Allaah are made beloved to him, and those that contradict it are made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in seeking the truth, and in submission once the proof has been established.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is trained to seek the truth with courtesy and to submit once the proof has been established, so that he does not persist obstinately after the evidence has become clear.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to prolong disputation after the truth has been made clear, so that he guards his time and returns to what is correct.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s dragging him, under the cover of questioning, into casting doubt upon the established fundamentals, so he is taught the difference between the question of seeking guidance and the question of objection.
The age group from thirteen to fifteen years
The application of the governance of time in this group across the four tracks (which the educator (murabbie) embodies and directs):
Through purging/refinement (tasfiyah): His mind is addressed with the value of one’s lifetime and the accountability for it, and the understanding (fiqh) of priorities, the balancing of rights (worship, study, and rest), and the foundations of the governance of time are deepened; so that he is persuaded by proof and not by compulsion.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): The taking of one’s soul to account and the awareness of being watched by Allaah (muraaqabah) are firmly established, along with the remedy for procrastination, laziness, and languor, and the calling to mind of the questioning about one’s youth—as to how one expended it; and the love of seizing time is instilled by his own choice.
Through the training of the tongue: He is trained to leave what does not concern him, to govern the times of social media and of speech, and to guard his tongue in his free time.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained upon a daily and weekly schedule that he draws up himself and is held to account for, and upon the governance of screen times, and upon perseverance in righteous deeds even if they be few, while preserving his dignity in the course of direction.
The application of the moral character of sincere counsel (nasiehah) in this group across the four tracks (which the educator (murabbie) embodies and directs):
Through purging/refinement (tasfiyah): He is treated as a person of reason, so that he is persuaded by proof and not by compulsion, and his conception is corrected through calm dialogue; for reproach at this age repels him, and compulsion arouses his stubbornness, whereas persuasion opens his heart.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): Care is taken to preserve his dignity and not to expose him before others, his mind and his innate disposition (fitrah) are addressed, and the love of good is instilled by his own choice and conviction, not by force.
Through the training of the tongue: Calm dialogue and questioning are given precedence over direct command, one begins with praise of his good qualities, and he is counseled in private and not in public, out of regard for his dignity.
Through the training of the limbs: He is made a partner in responsibility and is consulted, he is given a role model from among the righteous elders to emulate, and one is patient with the fluctuations of his temperament; for counsel by conduct is more eloquent than counsel by speech at this age.
The detailed innate characteristics particular to this stage of life, and how to direct them pedagogically toward the veneration of Allaah and the governance and direction of the deeds of the hearts
In this stage of life, the majority live through the period of early youthful puberty, and they possess a number of the characteristics of the innate disposition (fitrah), among which are:
1. The acceleration of physical growth: as the stage of puberty brings about hormonal changes that directly affect feelings and behavior.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) explains to the mature youth that growth is a blessing from Allaah for the sake of worship. He engages him in dialogue through demonstrative reasoning concerning the channeling of physical energy toward obedience to Allaah.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart gratitude for the blessing of his newfound strength. He rejoices before him when he uses it in obedience and worship.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “O Allaah, bless my strength and make it for Your obedience.” He repeats it with him daily at a fixed time.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him in physical acts of worship such as the night prayer (qiyaam al-layl) or fasting. He makes that a means of governing his newfound energy.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that the onset of his puberty is a blessing and a legal responsibility (taklief) from Allaah, so he is led to steward his strengthened body through obedience to his Lord and to guard it from the unlawful (haraam).
Through leading the emotions: His new feelings and desires are governed so that they are channeled, not suppressed, and it is instilled in him that governing them for Allaah’s sake is a source of elevation.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to using his strength and his youth for Allaah’s sake, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The guarding of his body in what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and its use in disobedience is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patient abstention from unlawful desires and in self-restraint when they surge, and he is encouraged toward fasting.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is engaged gently in dialogue about the danger of unlawful desires and is persuaded to restrain himself, so that he counsels himself to chastity and reminds his peers of it with wisdom, not with public shaming.
Through the governance of time: He is encouraged to fill his time with fasting and worship, so that he expends the surge of his youth in beneficial time that breaks desire.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan provokes his nascent desire, so he is accustomed to lowering his gaze, fasting, seeking refuge in Allaah, and avoiding temptations.
2. The eruption of the love of independence: a strong desire to make decisions in every detail of his life.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the mature youth in dialogue about the fact that the best independence is that which lies in obedience to Allaah. He harnesses this feeling of his to direct him through demonstrative reasoning.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that servitude to Allaah (3uboediyyah) is the very goal of true independence. He rejoices before him at righteous independent decisions.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I take charge of my affair for obedience to Allaah,” in his decisions. He repeats it with him in every situation.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He grants him independent decisions within the bounds of the Sacred Law. He praises him for his righteous decisions with joy.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught that the most complete independence is to be independent of his own whim through obedience to Allaah, so he is led to master himself before he becomes independent in his decision.
Through leading the emotions: His desire for independence is governed so that it does not turn into rebellion, and the preferring of truth over whim is instilled in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to being independent in good for Allaah’s sake, not to vindicate himself, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): He is granted decision-making within the bounds of the Sacred Law in what Allaah loves, and he is kept from independence in disobedience, so that he grows accustomed to good.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in bearing the consequences of his decision, and in respecting his parents alongside his independence.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is engaged in dialogue about bearing the consequences of his decision and respecting his parents alongside his independence, so that he learns to present his opinion and accept counsel with courtesy.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to give his decision time for reflection and consultation before proceeding, so that he does not act hastily in the moment of his agitation.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s making rebellion seem fair to him in the name of independence, so he is taught that true might lies in obedience to Allaah.
3. A heightened sense of self-identity: he poses questions such as: “Who am I?” and “What is my worth?”
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the mature youth in dialogue about the fact that his identity is to be a servant of Allaah. He harnesses his questioning of “Who am I?” to teach him that.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart pride in servitude to Allaah. He rejoices before him when he holds firm to his identity of faith.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I am the servant of Allaah; I was created for His worship.” He repeats it with him daily.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He keeps close company with him in an act of worship that consolidates his identity (the congregational prayer, the memorization of the Qur’an). He makes it a tangible daily reality.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: His question about his identity is answered with the fact that he is a servant of Allaah created for His worship, so he is led to build his selfhood upon tawhied.
Through leading the emotions: The tranquility of belonging to Allaah and His religion is instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon a sense of might through Islam.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to letting his belonging to his identity of faith be for Allaah’s sake, not mere imitation, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): It is made beloved to him that his identity be love for the sake of Allaah and hatred for His sake, for that is its very core, so he grows upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and steadfastness upon his identity of faith in the face of the currents of doubt-mongering.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is engaged in dialogue with proof so as to hold firm to his identity in the face of doubt-mongering, and he is persuaded to counsel the doubter with knowledge rather than by going along with him.
Through the governance of time: He is trained not to spend his time on what shakes his certainty, so that he directs it toward what firmly establishes his faith and answers the specious doubts raised against him.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan and the callers to falsehood dissolving his identity, so that his belonging is founded upon the revelation and not upon whims.
4. Mood swings: the rapid shifting between enthusiasm, anger, and sorrow.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the mature youth in dialogue about the fact that mood swings are a trial testing his patience. He harnesses the situation through demonstrative reasoning in teaching him.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart patience and the seeking of Allaah’s reward. He rejoices before him when he governs his feelings for Allaah’s sake in a difficult situation.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “All praise is due to Allaah in every state,” when his mood shifts. He repeats it with him gently in the moment.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to perform ablution (wudoe’) when angry and to keep silent when agitated. He makes that his constant method.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is taught to master himself when his mood fluctuates, so he is led to realize that the steadiness of the heart is through the remembrance of Allaah, not through the whims of the self.
Through leading the emotions: He is taught to channel his fluctuating feelings rather than to be led by them, so he is trained to return them to tranquility through remembrance (dhikr).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to governing his mood out of awareness of Allaah’s watching (muraaqabah), so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Forbearance and steadfastness, which Allaah loves, are made beloved to him, and loss of self-control is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and in restraining his rage when his mood flares up, and in not making decisions while angry.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is engaged in dialogue about restraining his rage when his mood flares up, and is persuaded not to make a decision while angry, so that he counsels himself to deliberateness.
Through the governance of time: He is trained to postpone his decision for a time until he calms down, so that he governs himself and does not settle the matter in the moment of his anger.
Through knowing the enemies: He is trained to perform ablution when angry and to keep silent when agitated, and he is taught that anger is from Satan, so he is accustomed to seeking refuge in Allaah.
5. The capacity for complex abstract thought: the discussion of moral ideas.
Firstly: Treating it through purging/refinement (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the mature youth in dialogue with proof concerning moral questions. He harnesses his intellectual capacity in establishing the evidence.
Secondly: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the veneration of the Sacred Law above bare reason. He rejoices before him when he submits to a ruling of the Sacred Law.
Thirdly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say, “The Sacred Law of Allaah knows best,” when opinions crowd in upon one another. He instructs him in submission with joy.
Fourthly: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He seats him in the gatherings of Islamic legal knowledge and their discussions. He keeps to that with him weekly.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leading the self and seeking knowledge: He is seated in the gatherings of Islamic legal knowledge and their discussions, so that his mind is led to make the revelation the arbiter in the great questions.
Through leading the emotions: The love of truth and the veneration of the wisdom of the Sacred Law are instilled in him, so that his emotions grow upon reverence.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is accustomed to employing his mind in pursuit of knowing the truth for Allaah’s sake, not for disputation and outdoing others, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Beneficial reflection, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and disputation by falsehood is made hateful to him, so he grows upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in seeking knowledge, in the careful investigation of issues, and in deliberateness before judging.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is engaged in dialogue and encouraged to investigate issues with deliberateness, so that he counsels himself to be patient in acquiring knowledge before he judges or counsels.
Through the governance of time: He designates regular times for seeking and investigating knowledge, so that his understanding bears fruit through constancy and not through haste.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s dragging him into making reason the arbiter so as to reject the revelation, so he is taught that sound reason does not contradict authentic transmitted texts (naql).
6. A conscious challenging of authority: not a childish obstinacy but a testing of boundaries.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the mature young man in dialogue concerning the fact that obedience to elders in what is not disobedience [to Allaah] is obligatory in the Sharie3ah. He establishes the proof demonstratively and with gentleness.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that submission to the law of Allaah is nobler than the assertion of the self. He shows joy before him at an act of obedience [performed] in hardship.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “To hear is to obey, in what is not disobedience” to his parents. He repeats it with him joyfully.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him to carry out the command of the Sharie3ah even if it opposes his desire. He proceeds gradually with him in [his] rectification should he refuse.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is trained to carry out the command of the Sharie3ah even if it opposes his desire, so that he is led to submission to the truth alongside a gradual [approach] in persuading him.
Through the leadership of the emotions: His desire to test limits is disciplined so that it does not turn into rebellion against the Sharie3ah, and there is instilled in him the preferring of obedience to Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to submit to the truth for the sake of Allaah out of conviction, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): He is taught that the limits of Allaah are to be venerated and not tested, and adherence to them is made beloved to him out of love, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained in patience in receiving the truth, and one proceeds gradually with him through wisdom, not through coercion.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): One proceeds gradually with him through wisdom in receiving the truth, not through coercion, so that he is persuaded to accept counsel and is trained to counsel others likewise.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to set aside a time for listening to the truth and reflecting upon it, so that he neither rejects it in haste nor squanders the opportunity of benefiting [from it].
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s making the transgressing of the limits of Allaah appear pleasing to him in the name of liberation, so that he is taught the difference between critiquing a considered opinion (idjtihaad) and rejecting the Sharie3ah.
7. A strong influence of friends: Acceptance by peers becomes a priority.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the mature young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the best acceptance is the acceptance of Allaah. He establishes the proof for that with gentleness.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that the pleasure of Allaah should be more important than the pleasure of peers. He shows joy before him when he abandons a conformity that contravenes the Sharie3ah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “The pleasure of Allaah is more important than the pleasure of people.” He repeats it with him at [times of] peer pressure.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He selects for him righteous companionship. He increases his sitting with them, whether in his [own] presence or without his presence, so that he grows accustomed to an environment of goodness.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: His choice of friends is directed toward the people of goodness, so that through their companionship he is led to what aids him in his religion, for a person is upon the religion of his intimate friend.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him love of righteous companionship and intimacy with it, so that his emotion is raised upon brotherhood for the sake of Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to befriend for the sake of Allaah and not for desire, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The companionship of the people of goodness and allegiance to them is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from evil companions, so that he is raised upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained in patience upon opposing his peers if they call him to falsehood, and upon counseling them.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is engaged in dialogue so that he remains firm upon the truth should his peers call him to falsehood, and he is persuaded to counsel them with gentleness rather than to go along with them.
Through the disciplining of time: He is trained to guard his time from companionship that drags him into falsehood, so that he selects those who help him to seize [the benefit of] his time.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that the evil companion is among the greatest of Satan’s gateways, so that he is habituated to the criterion of companionship [being] by religion and not by desire.
The age group from sixteen to eighteen years
The application of the disciplining of time in this group across the four tracks (which the educator (murabbie) embodies and directs):
Through purging (tasfiyah): There is deepened [in him] the fiqh of priorities and the balancing of rights (of Allaah, of the self, of the family, and of study), and the three foundations of the disciplining of time, and [the awareness] that he is responsible for his lifetime before Allaah; for he has drawn near to full [legal] accountability (taklief), so he is addressed with the address of the mature adult.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): There is firmly established in him the calling of the self to account and the watchfulness of Allaah (muraaqabah), and the remedy for procrastination and laziness, and the bringing to mind of the questioning about one’s lifetime and one’s youth—in what he wore it out—and he is addressed with the address of one who is [held] responsible.
Through the training of the tongue: He is trained to leave that which does not concern him, to discipline the times of [using] the means of [social] communication, to cultivate his tongue with what is beneficial, and to keep balance in his speech.
Through the training of the limbs: He is trained upon a daily and weekly schedule that balances rights, upon calling the self to account periodically, upon perseverance in righteous deeds even if they be few, and upon sustained continuity rather than intermittent bursts; so that he bears the responsibility for his time himself.
The application of the character-trait of sincere counsel (nasiehah) in this group across the four tracks (which the educator (murabbie) embodies and directs):
Through purging (tasfiyah): He is treated with the treatment of a mature adult, so he is reminded and consulted, not commanded like a child; and his counsel is built upon the affirmation of personal responsibility before Allaah, for he has drawn near to full accountability (taklief) and has borne the trust, so he is addressed with the address of men.
Through purification of the soul (tazkiyah): His sense of honor (muroe’ah) and his responsibility are addressed, and there is instilled in him that he himself should be a counselor to others and not merely one who is counseled, and his dignity is safeguarded with the safeguarding of men, and he is entrusted with the confidence [placed in] one who is relied upon.
Through the training of the tongue: With him, reminding, consultation, and persuasion by evidence are put forward, and he is addressed with the address of adults, and one begins with praise, and it is left to him to deduce what is correct himself, so that it becomes more firmly rooted in his heart.
Through the training of the limbs: He is entrusted with such responsibilities as make him feel confidence, and he is made a partner in the affairs of the family and in counsel within it, and [he is led] by example through action, and one is patient with his opinion until he attains sound judgment; for the mature adult is led through honoring, not through belittling.
The detailed innate characteristics (fitrah) particular to this age stage, and how to direct them pedagogically for the veneration of Allaah and the governance and direction of the deeds of the hearts
People in this age stage are living through the stage of advanced youthful maturity, which is the gateway to the stage of [full] adulthood, and they possess a number of characteristics of the innate disposition (fitrah), among them:
1. The completion of most physical growth: Bodily strength reaches its first peak.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the peak of strength is a blessing for worship, for independence, and for preparation for marriage. He establishes the proof with gentleness.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart gratitude for the blessing and the expending of it in what Allaah loves. He shows joy before him at a beneficial endeavor that prepares him for marriage.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “O Allaah, bless my strength and make it for Your obedience, for my independence, and for my preparation for marriage.” He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon lawful earning and a daily bodily act of worship. He prepares him for complete independence and for the household of marriage.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught that the peak of his strength is a blessing for worship and preparation, so that he is led to govern his strength through the obedience of Allaah and to guard it from the unlawful.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him gratitude for strength and the expending of it in what Allaah loves, so that his emotion is raised upon gratitude and not upon insolent ingratitude.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to use his strength for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The expending of his strength in what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and the spending of it in disobedience is made hateful to him, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience away from [forbidden] appetites through his strength, and upon using it in a bodily act of worship such as the night prayer (qiyaam) and fasting.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded to expend his strength in chastity and worship, so that he is a counselor to his peers toward chastity as a role model, not as an affected preacher.
Through the disciplining of time: He is consulted concerning the filling of his time with a bodily act of worship such as the night prayer (qiyaam) and fasting, so that he expends the surge of his strength in [something occupying] a time that draws him near to Allaah.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan entices him to expend his strength in falsehood, so that he is habituated to struggling against desire and to expending [his] strength in obedience.
2. The completion of awareness of self-identity: “I am so-and-so, and these are my values.”
The method of direction: fixing the identity upon the reference-point of faith in Allaah, and orienting the self toward the knowledge of Allaah and the love of His attributes, which sets aright the station of “watchfulness (muraaqabah).”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue that his original identity is to be a servant of Allaah. He establishes the proof by the demonstration of the innate disposition (fitrah).
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart pride in the identity of Islam. He shows joy before him when he holds fast to his faith-based values.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I am a servant of Allaah, and this is my identity” when he is asked about himself. He repeats it with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He keeps close to him in an act of worship that embodies his identity (the congregational prayer, the memorization of the Qur’an). He makes it tangible and daily.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: His identity is firmly established upon [the fact] that he is a servant of Allaah, a Muslim, so that he is led to have his values and stances follow his religion.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him dignity through Islam and tranquility in belonging to Allaah, so that his emotion is raised upon pride in his religion.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to have his belonging to his faith-based identity be for the sake of Allaah, not out of imitation, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): It is made beloved to him that his values be love for the sake of Allaah and hatred for His sake, for that is the core of his identity, so that he is raised upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon steadfastness in his faith-based identity and its values in the face of the currents of doubt-casting.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of steadfastness upon his identity and its values, and he is consulted concerning how to counsel the doubt-casters with knowledge and proof, not with going along [with them].
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded not to spend his time in that which dissolves his identity, so that he directs it toward the acquisition of what confirms his certainty and repels specious arguments (shubuhaat).
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is fortified against the callers to the dissolution of identity, who are among the soldiers of falsehood, so that his belonging is founded upon revelation (wahy).
3. The capacity to make fateful decisions: such as choosing one’s field of study, or one’s first job, or one’s course in life.
The method of direction: harnessing the decision toward the veneration of what Allaah wills in [one’s] life, and giving precedence to good opinion of Allaah and reliance [upon Him] (tawakkul) in the station of “resolve (3aziemah).”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the fateful decision ought to be referred back to the Sharie3ah. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart reliance upon Allaah (tawakkul) together with the prayer for guidance (istikhaarah). He shows joy before him at [his performing] an istikhaarah before a decision.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him in the supplication of istikhaarah before every fateful decision. He repeats that with him at every choice.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon consulting the people of knowledge before a decision. He makes that a [regular] practice in every decision.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught to build his fateful decisions upon what pleases Allaah and brings benefit, so that he is led to bind his destiny to the obedience of his Lord.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him tranquility in the [wise] management of Allaah together with good choosing, so that his emotion is raised upon reliance [upon Allaah] (tawakkul).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to choose what pleases Allaah even if it opposes his desire, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The choosing of what Allaah loves, of beneficial lawful things, is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from choosing the unlawful, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon the istikhaarah, consultation, and patience upon the fruit of his decision.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is consulted and reminded of the istikhaarah before his decision, so that he accepts counsel and seeks the counsel of the people of experience with the etiquette of the mature adult.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to give his decision the time of istikhaarah and consultation, so that he does not hasten a fruit before its season.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan makes appealing to him what harms him in his destiny, so that he is habituated to seeking out the lawful and to seeking the aid of Allaah.
4. Love of complete financial independence: the desire to earn one’s own income and to dispense with support.
The method of direction: binding the earning of provision to the intention of dispensing with what is in people’s hands and to the magnifying of gratitude for the blessing, which purifies the station of “asceticism (zuhd)” and “dependence upon Allaah.”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that financial independence is an act of worship by the intention of dispensing with people. He invests his passion toward that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart gratitude for provision and the non-reliance upon other than Allaah. He shows joy before him at a lawful provision.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “Praise be to Allaah who has provided me this without any might or power on my part.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon lawful earning and preparing a personal budget. He prepares him financially for marriage and independence.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught that lawful earning is an act of worship and that the Provider (al-Razzaaq) is Allaah, so that he is led to a financial independence whose foundation is reliance [upon Allaah] and wholesome earning.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him contentment and abstinence from the unlawful, so that his emotion is raised upon contentment (ridaa) and not upon greed.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to earn for the sake of Allaah, to keep himself chaste [from begging], and to spend on good [causes], so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Lawful earning, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and the unlawful and usury (ribaa) are made hateful to him, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience in seeking the lawful and upon not hastening toward the unlawful.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of patience in seeking the lawful, so that he counsels himself not to hasten toward the unlawful, and he counsels his peers toward chastity and the lawful.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to expend his time in seeking lawful provision and in preparing himself, so that he does not squander it in the paths of the unlawful.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan promises him poverty and makes unlawful earning appear pleasing, so that he is habituated to chastity and reliance [upon Allaah].
5. A relative maturity in social relationships: a deeper understanding of friendship and faithfulness.
The method of direction: making faithfulness and sincerity an act of devotion by which one draws near to Allaah, so that the heart is purified of ostentation (riyaa’) and hypocrisy.
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that faithfulness is among the [natural] traits of the believer and not an affectation. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that his faithfulness should be to Allaah first. He shows joy before him at the sincerity of his faithfulness to his brothers.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I love you for the sake of Allaah; I fulfill my covenant with you for the sake of Allaah.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon guarding the trust of friendship and upon not betraying [it]. He makes that a daily practice.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught that the best companionship is that which is for the sake of Allaah, so that he is led to establish his relationships upon God-consciousness (taqwaa) and faithfulness to Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him love of his brothers for the sake of Allaah and faithfulness to them, so that his emotion is raised upon faith-based brotherhood.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to love and to befriend for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
