Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Allegiance to the people of faith and faithfulness to them are made beloved to him, and he is kept away from allegiance upon falsehood, so that he is raised upon loyalty for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience and excellence (ihsaan) in companionship, and upon counsel and faithfulness.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of excellence in companionship, of counsel toward it, and of faithfulness, so that he is a trustworthy counselor to his brothers—privately, not by exposing [them].
Through the disciplining of time: He allocates a portion of his time to righteous, beneficial companionship, so that he fills his times with those who help him toward goodness.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that allegiance upon sin is among the beautifications of Satan, so that he is taught the [governing] criterion of loyalty and faithfulness for the sake of Allaah.
6. A broader awareness of the long-term consequences of actions.
The method of direction: the cultivating of the calling of the self to account and the remembrance of the Day of Reckoning, which strengthens the station of “reflection upon [ultimate] outcomes.”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the Day of Resurrection is the scale of every act. He reminds him of the ultimate fate of the deed by [means of] demonstration.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart awe [and fear] of the Hereafter. He shows joy before him at [his] reflecting upon a consequence before the act.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “Am I content for this to be displayed before Allaah?” He repeats that with him before the act.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon the weekly calling to account of his deeds. He makes it a fixed, regular routine.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: There is firmly established in him [the awareness] that every deed has a consequence with Allaah, so that through consideration of [ultimate] outcomes he is led to God-consciousness (taqwaa).
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him hope for a good outcome and fear of an evil one, so that his emotion is raised upon watchfulness (muraaqabah).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to act for the lasting outcome for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): That whose outcome is praiseworthy with Allaah is made beloved to him, and that whose outcome is evil is made hateful to him, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon giving precedence to the lasting outcome over the immediate pleasure.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of preferring the lasting outcome, so that he counsels himself and others to give precedence to the beneficial deferred [reward] over the immediate pleasure.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to expend his time on that whose outcome endures in the Hereafter, so that he does not consume it in a passing thing that brings no benefit.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan makes the immediate [life] appear pleasing and makes [one] forget the Hereafter, so that he is habituated to consideration of [ultimate] outcomes.
7. The beginning of strategic thinking: planning for several years ahead.
The method of direction: bringing the Hereafter to mind within every plan, and binding every future vision to the realization of servitude [to Allaah] (3uboediyyah), so that this yields the station of “sincerity (ikhlaas).”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the plan ought to realize servitude [to Allaah]. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that the plan of Allaah is greater than his [own] plan. He shows joy before him when he is content with the [wise] management of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “If Allaah wills, and my success is only through Allaah” in every plan. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon drawing up an annual plan that guarantees worship within it. He reviews it with him periodically.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught to plan for his coming years in the obedience of Allaah while attaching the matter to His will, so that he is led to taking the [appropriate] means and to reliance [upon Allaah] (tawakkul).
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him tranquility in the management of Allaah together with good management [on his part], so that his emotion is raised upon reliance [upon Allaah] (tawakkul).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to make the goal of his planning the pleasure of Allaah and the abode of the Hereafter, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Planning for the good which Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from contriving for falsehood, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience in carrying out his long-range plans and upon not despairing.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of pressing on with his long-range plans and of not despairing, so that he counsels himself to persevere and to trust in the aid of Allaah.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to apportion his long-range project across ordered times, so that he attains it through perseverance, not through a sudden surge, nor through despondency.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan fills him with [false] hopes and induces procrastination, so that he is habituated to promptness and to placing the Hereafter within the reckoning of his planning.
8. A serious concern for the major issues: such as justice, values, and politics.
The method of direction: harnessing this awareness in the aiding of the religion of Allaah and its values, and magnifying the station of “protective zeal for the sake of Allaah (ghayrah).”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the measure of [these] issues is the law of Allaah, not the desires of people. He establishes the proof by demonstration.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart protective zeal for the sake of Allaah (ghayrah) in [these] issues. He shows joy before him when he aids the truth with gentleness.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “The truth is what Allaah has said” when discussing an issue. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon aiding the wronged through the Sharie3ah and the good word. He makes that a part of his interaction.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught to weigh the major issues by the scale of revelation (wahy), so that his intellect is led to the arbitration of the Sharie3ah in [matters of] justice and values.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him protective zeal for the religion of Allaah and concern for the affair of the Muslims, so that his emotion is raised upon brotherhood and mutual aid.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to be concerned with the affair of the ummah for the sake of Allaah, not for [self-]display, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The aiding of the truth and its people is made beloved to him, and injustice and falsehood are made hateful to him, so that he is raised upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience and wisdom in the major issues and upon not [acting with] recklessness.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of wisdom in the major issues, so that he counsels himself to [act with] deliberateness and to seek the opinion of the people of knowledge before proceeding.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to give the major issues their due of reflection and consultation, so that he does not act rashly and thereby cause corruption.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is fortified against specious arguments and slogans that the enemies of the religion make appear pleasing in the major issues, so that his stance is founded upon revelation (wahy).
9. The emergence of leadership or organizational inclinations.
The method of direction: orienting leadership toward serving people with justice and mercy, and refining the self of arrogance, which purifies the station of “scrupulous piety (wara3)” and “humble submission to Allaah.”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that leadership is service, not mastery. He establishes the proof by the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart humility and scrupulous piety (wara3) in leadership. He shows joy before him when he serves those below him.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “I am your servant” when he takes charge of a matter. He instructs him in that instead of arrogance.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He affords him the leadership of a small charitable project. He trains him upon mercy and justice in managing people.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught that the best leadership is that which is for the sake of Allaah and in [the service of] the truth, so that he is led to lead himself through obedience before he leads others.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him love of benefiting people and guiding them, so that his emotion is raised upon mercy and reform.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to seek leadership for the service of the truth for the sake of Allaah, not for chieftaincy and exaltation [over others], so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): It is made beloved to him to lead toward what Allaah loves, and he is kept away from being a head in falsehood, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience in leadership and upon bearing its burdens and the harm of people.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of patience in leadership and of bearing harm, so that he counsels those under him with gentleness and endures what issues from them.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to organize his time for discharging the burdens of leadership, so that he distributes it over its due rights and falls short in nothing.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that the love of chieftaincy is Satan’s gateway to arrogance and injustice, so that he is habituated to humility and to the will to reform, not to exaltation [over others].
10. The recession of purely emotional decisions compared to the stage of 13–16 (if directed with sound direction).
The method of direction: using this equilibrium to discipline the impulses and to magnify the standing of “forbearance (hilm)” and “patience for the sake of Allaah.”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that forbearance (hilm) is a quality that Allaah loves. He invests his equilibrium in teaching him that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart patience and forbearance for the sake of Allaah. He shows joy before him when he restrains himself in a difficult situation.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “O Allaah, grant me forbearance and deliberateness.” He repeats that with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon deliberateness before making an angry decision. He makes that his permanent manner.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: His intellectual maturity is directed toward the arbitration of revelation (wahy) together with the intellect, so that he is led to weigh his affairs by the Sharie3ah and not by emotion alone.
Through the leadership of the emotions: He is taught to make his emotion subordinate to his correct conception, so that it becomes upright upon the truth and not upon desire.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to seek the truth in his decision for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The truth is made beloved to him even if it opposes his emotion, and the following of desire is made hateful to him, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon deliberateness and upon not [making] a decision in the surge of emotion.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded not to decide in the surge of his emotion, so that he counsels himself to defer judgment until his opinion settles.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to grant himself time until his emotion calms, so that he makes the decision in the time of his clarity, not of his surge.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan stirs up emotion in order to make the intellect slip, so that he is habituated to referring matters back to revelation (wahy).
11. The capacity for sacrifice for the sake of a principle.
The method of direction: harnessing the spirit of sacrifice for the aiding of the truth and the religion, so that it is translated into the station of “loyalty to Allaah” and “truthfulness.”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the best of principles is that which is for the sake of Allaah. He establishes the proof by the life-accounts of the prophets.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart loyalty to Allaah and His Messenger above every loyalty. He shows joy before him at a sacrifice for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “Allaah is sufficient for me, and how excellent a Trustee He is” at [the paying of] the price of a principle. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon leaving what he loves of the worldly life for what pleases Allaah. He praises him for sincere sacrifice.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: His readiness for sacrifice is directed toward the greatest principle, which is tawhied, so that he is led to give [of himself] in the path of Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him love of the truth and of sacrifice for its sake, so that his emotion is raised upon giving [of oneself] for the sake of Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to have his sacrifice be for the sake of Allaah, not for reputation and heroism, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Giving [of oneself] for what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from sacrifice for a false principle, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience and steadfastness at [times of] giving [of oneself] and trial in the path of the truth.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of steadfastness at [times of] giving [of oneself] and trial in the path of the truth, so that he counsels himself to be patient and to seek the reward [from Allaah].
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to give of his time and effort in the aiding of the truth, so that he sets for his times a portion of beneficial striving (djihaad).
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s making sacrifice for false principles appear pleasing to him, so that he is taught the criterion of principle by revelation (wahy).
12. An increase in the sense of responsibility toward the family and society.
The method of direction: orienting this sense toward the worship [inherent] in responsibility, and cultivating the station of “intention (niyyah)” and “endurance in the path of Allaah.”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that responsibility is a trust for which he will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the intention of serving the family and the ummah for the sake of Allaah. He shows joy before him when he shoulders a responsibility.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He asks him to say “This is a trust upon my neck [owed] to Allaah” when shouldering a responsibility. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He charges him with tangible responsibilities in the family (maintenance, care). He praises him for [his] trustworthiness.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught that fulfilling the rights of the family and society is an act of worship, so that he is led to bear the trust of responsibility for the sake of Allaah.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him love of dutifulness toward his family and of benefiting his society, so that his emotion is raised upon mercy and mutual support.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to discharge his responsibility for the sake of Allaah and in hope of [His] reward, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Dutifulness to his family and aiding the people of faith are made beloved to him, and undutifulness [to parents] and negligence are made hateful to him, so that he is raised upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience (sabr): He is trained upon patience in fulfilling the rights of the family and society and upon bearing their burdens.
Through sincere counsel (nasiehah): He is reminded of fulfilling the rights of his family and his society, so that he counsels them sincerely and is patient with their burdens as a discharge of the trust.
Through the disciplining of time: He is reminded to distribute his time over the rights of his Lord, of himself, of his family, and of his society, so that he gives to every possessor of a right his right in [its proper] time.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan discourages [one] from dutifulness and makes the severing [of ties] appear pleasing, so that he is habituated to steadfast persistence upon the maintaining of kinship ties and [upon] benefiting [others].
13. An awareness of [one’s] capacities and personal weakness.
The method of direction: deepening humility and brokenness before Allaah, so that this yields “utter neediness [of Allaah] (iftiqaar)” and “reverent awe (khashyah).”
First: Addressing it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that neediness of Allaah is worthier than self-conceit. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Addressing it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the humility of one who is [utterly] needy of Allaah. He shows joy before him at his brokenness before Allaah.
Third: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the tongue
He instructs him to say “O Allaah, I am weak, so strengthen me; lowly, so honor me.” He repeats that with him daily.
Fourth: Addressing it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — the training of the limbs
He trains him upon manifesting [his] neediness of Allaah in the prayer and in supplication. He makes that a [second] nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the seeking of knowledge: He is taught to be grateful for his capacities and to seek the aid of Allaah against his weakness, so that he is led to knowledge of himself in order to govern it by the truth.
Through the leadership of the emotions: There is instilled in him humility at [times of] strength and neediness of Allaah at [times of] weakness, so that his emotion is raised upon servitude [to Allaah] (3uboediyyah).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to employ his capacities for the sake of Allaah and to ask Him for aid against his deficiency, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, and loyalty and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The employing of his capacities in what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from using them in disobedience, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in striving against his weakness and developing his capacities.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to strive against his weakness and to develop his capacities, so that he counsels himself to strive toward his perfection rather than resigning himself to his incapacity.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to invest his time in developing his capacities, so that he fills his hours with what strengthens his usefulness.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan comes to him through the gate of his strength by means of self-admiration (3udjb) and through the gate of his weakness by means of despair, so that he is habituated to humility and hope.
14. Forming a selective circle of friends: He carefully chooses those around him.
The method of direction: choosing righteous companionship that assists in the veneration of Allaah, which strengthens the station of “vigilant awareness (muraaqabah)” and “righteous companionship.”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that a person follows the religion of his close friend. He establishes the proof by the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for righteous companionship. He shows joy before him when he sits in the company of the righteous.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I seek the companionship of the righteous for the sake of Allaah.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He assists him in choosing righteous companions. He makes it easy for him to sit with them in the mosque and in the gatherings of remembrance (dhikr).
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His selection of his companions is directed toward the people of goodness, so that through their company he is led to what aids him in his religion.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love for righteous companionship and intimacy with it are instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon brotherhood in Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to select his companions for the sake of Allaah and not for [worldly] benefit, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): The companionship of the people of goodness and allegiance to them are made beloved to him, and evil comrades are avoided, so that he grows up upon allegiance and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and excellence (ihsaan) in companionship and in giving sincere counsel to it.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to show excellence in his companionship and to counsel it truthfully, so that he becomes a truthful mirror for his brethren rather than a flatterer.
Through the management of time: He sets aside regular times for his righteous companionship, so that his intimacy with it bears fruit within beneficial time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that an evil comrade is among the greatest gateways of Satan, so that he is habituated to the criterion of selection by religion.
15. The desire to test one’s capacities in real situations (work, volunteering).
The method of direction: investing that in the fields of goodness and seeking reward (ihtisaab), and cultivating the self upon “sincerity” in [one’s] work.
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the best fields for [testing] capacities are the fields of goodness. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart sincerity in work and volunteering. He shows joy before him at a pure intention.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say, “I volunteer for the Face of Allaah,” before any work. He instructs him in that.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him in real, regular volunteer work. He chooses for him tangible fields of goodness.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His testing of his capacities is directed toward the fields of goodness and benefit, so that he is led to test them in what pleases Allaah.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of work, benefit, and excellence is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon giving.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to work and volunteer for Allaah and in hope of reward, not for show, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Beneficial work that Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and the employment of his capacities in what harms is avoided, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained in patience, mastery (itqaan), and perseverance through hardship in the fields of work.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded of mastery and perseverance in the fields of work, so that he counsels others toward excellence and counsels by his state through his mastery.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to allot to his work times in which he masters it, so that he perfects its accomplishment through steadfastness over his time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against employing his capacities in what turns [him] away from Allaah through Satan’s beautification [of it].
16. A relative balance between the need for social acceptance and the desire for distinctiveness.
The method of direction: regulating the intention behind [seeking] acceptance so as to make it for the Face of Allaah and not for the people, which purifies the heart of “ostentation (riyaa’).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the best acceptance is the acceptance of Allaah. He establishes the proof for giving precedence to the pleasure of Allaah.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart that distinctiveness should be through truth and not through deviance. He shows joy before him at his steadfastness upon the truth.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, bring me to Your good pleasure even if the people oppose [me].” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him not to go along with people in falsehood, even if he must differ from them. He praises him for [his] steadfastness.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that his criterion is the pleasure of Allaah, so that he is led to agree with people in truth and to stand apart from them in falsehood.
Through the leading of the emotions: His eagerness for acceptance and his love of distinctiveness are regulated so that they do not drive him to falsehood, and preferring the pleasure of Allaah is instilled in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to act for the pleasure of Allaah and neither for acceptance nor for distinction, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Agreement with the people of truth is made beloved to him, and seeking acceptance at the cost of Allaah’s displeasure is avoided, so that he grows up upon allegiance and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience with the estrangement [that comes] in [holding to] the truth when the people differ.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to be patient with the estrangement [that comes] in the truth if the people differ, so that he counsels them toward it with wisdom and stands firm alone if need be.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to waste his time going along with people in falsehood, so that he preserves his hours for what pleases Allaah even if he stands alone.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan employs the pressure of acceptance at times and the love of distinction at [other] times to drag him [into falsehood], so that he is habituated to steadfastness upon the truth.
17. The ability to control the image one presents to others.
The method of direction: striving against the self toward truthfulness and consistency between the outward and the inward, in order to realize “truthfulness with Allaah.”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that truthfulness between the outward and the inward is among the conditions of salvation. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart hatred of hypocrisy and love of truthfulness with Allaah first and foremost. He shows joy before him at the truthfulness of his intention.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, make my inner state better than my outer appearance.” He repeats that with him daily.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to unify his outward with his inward. He holds him to account gently for any discrepancy.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that the best image is the image of one who is truthful with Allaah, so that he is led to make his inner state like his outer appearance.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of truthfulness and dislike of affectation are instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon what is wholesome.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to act for Allaah and not to beautify his image before people, so that sincerity is instilled in him and he is warned against ostentation.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Inner truthfulness, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and hypocrisy and duplicity are made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience to appear in his true image and to refrain from affectation.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to be truthful with himself and to appear in his true image without affectation, so that he counsels himself toward sincerity rather than showing off before people.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to spend his time on affectation before people, so that he directs it toward reforming his inward rather than merely beautifying his outward.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan pushes him toward beautifying the outward and corrupting the inward, so that he is habituated to reforming the inner state.
18. A broader understanding of the concept of the role model: he begins, with awareness, to emulate influential persons.
The method of direction: choosing rabbaanie role models and venerating the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, which grows in the heart “love” for Allaah and His Messenger.
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the best role model is the Prophet ﷺ. He establishes the proof for that by the biographies of the Salaf.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart love for the Prophet ﷺ, his family, and his Companions. He shows joy before him when he is influenced by their way.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say, “My beloved is the Messenger of Allaah,” when he is mentioned. He repeats with him the sending of blessings upon him daily.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to perform a daily prophetic Sunnah (the tooth-stick [siwaak], breaking the fast with dates). He makes the Sunnah second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that the true role model is the one who venerates Allaah, so that he is led to take the prophets and the righteous as his models rather than the people of falsehood.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of righteous role models is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon esteeming the people of goodness.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to emulate the righteous for the sake of Allaah, and he is taught that his foremost role model is the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Emulating the friends (awliyaa’) of Allaah is made beloved to him, and he is warned against the role models of falsehood however dazzling they may be, so that he grows up upon allegiance and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in emulating the righteous and remaining steadfast upon their guidance.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to emulate the righteous and to remain steadfast upon their guidance, so that he counsels himself to cleave to their trace and directs others to them.
Through the management of time: He sets aside time for their life-accounts and their guidance, so that his emulation of them becomes firmly rooted through his constancy over his time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against evil role models whom Satan beautifies through the means of influence [i.e., the media], so that he is taught the criterion of the role model by the Sacred Law.
19. An improved ability to regulate one’s reactions before strangers.
The method of direction: harnessing this self-control for the sake of Allaah, so that it yields the station of “forbearance (hilm)” and “modesty (hayaa’).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that forbearance and modesty are among the traits of the Prophet ﷺ. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart forbearance and modesty. He shows joy before him at his self-control before people.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, I feel shame before You to give way to anger.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him in self-control before everyone, especially in the mosque and at work. He makes it second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught to master his reactions out of vigilant awareness of Allaah in every state, so that he is led [to understand] that forbearance is a character trait by which he governs himself.
Through the leading of the emotions: He is taught to direct his reactions rather than suppress them, so that he is trained to return them to tranquility through remembrance (dhikr).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to regulate his reactions for Allaah in private and in public, and not only before people, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Forbearance, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and loss of self-control is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and in restraining anger in all settings, not only before strangers.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to restrain anger in all settings, not only before strangers, so that he counsels himself to make his forbearance a genuine character trait and not an affectation.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to grant himself time to calm down when angered in every state, so that he regulates his reactions in private and in public.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that anger is from Satan, so that he is habituated to seek refuge [in Allaah] and to remain still when it arises.
20. Psychological readiness to bear the consequences of personal decisions.
The method of direction: linking outcomes to the divine decree and magnifying the station of “contentment with [Allaah’s] decree (al-ridaa bi-l-qadaa’).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that contentment with [Allaah’s] decree is part of the nobility of servitude to Allaah. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart contentment with the decree of Allaah after exerting the [means and] causes. He shows joy before him at his contentment with a bitter outcome.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “Allaah has decreed, and what He willed He has done; praise be to Allaah in every state.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him not to grieve over the decree. He makes that second nature at every outcome.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that the responsible person bears the consequence of his deed before Allaah, so that he is led to deliberate carefully and then bear [the consequences of] what he chose.
Through the leading of the emotions: Contentment with the decree of Allaah, together with bearing responsibility, is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon submission (tasliem).
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to bear the consequence of his decision for Allaah without casting blame on others, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Bearing the consequence of the good he has chosen is made beloved to him, and a decision [leading] into disobedience whose burden he would bear is avoided, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained in patience with the outcomes of his decisions and in not despairing.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to be patient with the outcomes of his decisions and not to despair, so that he counsels himself to be content with the decree of Allaah after exerting his utmost.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to squander his time in grief over what has passed, so that he directs it toward retrieving what can be retrieved and working for what remains.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan beautifies [a thing] and then disowns [it], so that he is habituated to deliberate before deciding and to bear its consequence.
21. The ability to analyze complex moral situations.
The method of direction: directing [such] analysis toward the understanding of the Sacred Law and the striving to please Allaah, which strengthens “spiritual insight (basierah).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the moral criterion is the Sacred Law of Allaah. He establishes the proof by the [scriptural] texts.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the veneration of scrupulousness (wara3) and God-consciousness (taqwaa). He shows joy before him at his leaving a doubtful matter for the sake of Allaah.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He asks him to say, “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt,” when doubtful matters arise. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to ask the people of knowledge in complex situations. He makes that path easy for him.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught to weigh complex situations by the scale of the Sacred Law, so that his intellect is led to make revelation the arbiter in newly arising matters (nawaazil).
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of the truth and veneration of the ruling of Allaah are instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon reverent awe.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to seek the truth in his analysis for the sake of Allaah and not for the sake of disputation, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Judging by what Allaah has revealed is made beloved to him, and making [personal] desire the arbiter is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in investigating questions [thoroughly] and in asking the people of knowledge about what is unclear.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to investigate questions [thoroughly] and to ask the people of knowledge about what is unclear, so that he counsels himself not to issue verdicts or give counsel out of ignorance.
Through the management of time: He sets aside times for investigating his questions and asking those qualified in them, so that his knowledge bears fruit through his constancy over his time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan dragging him into diluting the [Sacred Law’s] rulings under the name of complexity, so that he is taught to refer newly arising matters to the people of knowledge.
22. Mental flexibility in the face of change.
The method of direction: transforming flexibility into “contentment with vicissitudes” and trust in the governance of Allaah.
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that change is part of the governance of Allaah. He establishes the proof for the obligation of trusting in Allaah.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart trust in the governance of Allaah. He shows joy before him at his contentment with a change he dislikes.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “Allaah chooses for me what is best.” He repeats that with him at [times of] change.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to adapt to the new with an open heart. He praises him for [his] flexibility.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that the fixed principles do not change and that flexibility lies in the means, so that he is led to remain steadfast upon the fundamentals while dealing well with what is changeable.
Through the leading of the emotions: The serenity of steadfastness upon the truth amid the fluctuation of circumstances is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon steadfastness.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to adapt in permissible matters for the benefit of the religion, for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Steadfastness upon what Allaah has established is made beloved to him, and inconstancy in religion is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in remaining steadfast upon the fundamentals, however much reality changes.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to remain steadfast upon the fundamentals however much reality changes, so that he counsels himself to distinguish between what is fixed and what is changeable.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to consume his time in changeable matters that dislodge him from his fundamentals, so that he directs it toward what firmly establishes them.
Through knowing the enemies: He is fortified against Satan beautifying for him the diluting of the fixed principles under the name of flexibility, so that he is taught the difference between what is fixed and what is changeable.
23. The possibility of mature participation in religious or charitable activities.
The method of direction: investing it in magnifying the standing of acts that draw one near [to Allaah] (qurubaat) and deepening the meaning of “seeking reward (ihtisaab).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that participation in acts of drawing near [to Allaah] requires sincerity. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the seeking of reward. He shows joy before him at a pure intention in a good deed.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “I intend this for Allaah alone,” before every religious activity. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He involves him with himself in good works and da3wah projects. He makes that a weekly habit.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is directed toward participation in goodness and da3wah, so that through his work he is led to benefit the religion and the people for the sake of Allaah.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of da3wah, reform, and benefiting people is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon giving for the sake of Allaah.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to work in goodness for the sake of Allaah and not for reputation, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Cooperation upon righteousness with the people of faith is made beloved to him, and cooperation upon sin is avoided, so that he grows up upon allegiance and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in charitable work and in bearing its burdens.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to be patient in charitable work and to bear its burdens, so that he counsels his companions in it toward sincerity and seeking reward.
Through the management of time: He sets aside part of his time for beneficial charitable work, so that he gives his hours an impact whose benefit extends to others.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan discourages and corrupts, so that he is habituated to stand guard steadfastly upon goodness and to preserve [his] intention.
24. Love of personal achievement as a source of satisfaction.
The method of direction: transforming this love into “the seeking of Allaah’s good pleasure” rather than [the pleasure of] the self, which cleanses the heart of self-admiration (3udjb).
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the best achievement is that with which Allaah is pleased. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the cleansing of the heart from self-admiration. He shows joy before him when he ascribes the merit to Allaah.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “Praise be to Allaah; this is from the bounty of my Lord,” upon an achievement. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him in an achievement that he conceals from people. He praises him for the sincerity in it.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His love of achievement is directed toward what benefits him in his religion and his worldly life, so that he is led to make the greatest achievement [the attainment of] the pleasure of Allaah.
Through the leading of the emotions: His joy at achievement is regulated so that it does not turn into self-admiration, and ascribing the merit to Allaah is instilled in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to achieve for Allaah and for the benefit of people, not for pride, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Achievement in goodness, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and achievement in falsehood is avoided, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and perseverance to realize beneficial achievement.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to persevere in realizing beneficial achievement, so that he counsels himself not to slacken and directs others to earnest striving.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to keep constant at his work in ordered times, so that his achievement bears fruit through constancy rather than through fleeting enthusiasm.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan turns the pleasure of achievement into self-admiration and arrogance, so that he is habituated to humility and gratitude.
25. The ability to distinguish between life priorities.
The method of direction: ordering priorities according to the scale of the Sacred Law and giving precedence to what draws [one] near to Allaah, so that it yields “understanding of the religion (fiqh fie al-dien).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that the criterion of priorities is the Sacred Law of Allaah. He establishes the proof by the jurisprudence of priorities (fiqh al-awlawiyyaat).
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the giving of precedence to what Allaah loves first. He shows joy before him when he gives precedence to the obligatory over the merely permissible.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “What pleases Allaah has the greater claim.” He repeats that with him whenever [priorities] compete.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to order his day according to the priorities of the Sacred Law (the obligatory acts, then the voluntary acts, then the permissible). He makes that second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught to give precedence to the more important in the scale of Allaah — the obligatory acts, then what follows them — so that he is led to order his life according to the guidance of the Sacred Law.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of giving precedence to what Allaah loves is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon preferring the more important.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to order his priorities for the pleasure of Allaah and the abode of the Hereafter, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Giving precedence to what Allaah has given precedence to is made beloved to him, and giving precedence to the worldly life over the religion is avoided, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience in giving precedence to the priorities of the Sacred Law even if they run counter to his desire.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to give precedence to the priorities of the Sacred Law even if they run counter to his desire, so that he counsels himself to give precedence to what Allaah wills over what he himself wills.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to order his time according to the priorities of the Sacred Law, so that he gives precedence to the obligatory over the recommended and to the compulsory over the supererogatory.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan inverts priorities and gives precedence to the worldly life, so that he is habituated to giving precedence to the Hereafter.
26. Awareness of the importance of reputation and one’s personal record.
The method of direction: directing this awareness toward the purification of the inner state more than the outer, which sets right “sincerity.”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that one’s reputation with Allaah is more important than one’s reputation with people. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart care for the inner state. He shows joy before him when he purifies his inward.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, make me righteous in the eyes of people, and, in Your sight, better than what they think.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to abandon whatever blemishes his religiously [sound] reputation, even if it is hidden. He makes care for the inward second nature.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that good repute follows righteous deeds and that the [proper] foundation is seeking the Face of Allaah, so that he is led to make his reputation a fruit rather than an aim.
Through the leading of the emotions: His eagerness for reputation is regulated so that it does not turn into ostentation, and sincerity of intent is instilled in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to work for Allaah and not for [his] record and reputation, so that sincerity is instilled in him and he is warned against the love of prestige.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Sincerity, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and ostentation is made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience with people’s censure if he is upon the truth, and in not selling his religion for his reputation.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to be patient with censure if he is in the right, so that he counsels himself not to sell his religion for his reputation among people.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to occupy his time with what people say about him, so that he directs his concern toward the sincerity of his work for Allaah.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that the love of prestige is the gateway of ostentation that Satan exploits, so that he is habituated to sincerity in [his] work.
27. A profound awareness of the passing of time and the value of life.
The method of direction: investing time in obedience, calling the self to account, and firmly establishing the station of “spiritual striving (mudjaahadah).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that time is a blessing about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection. He establishes the proof by the [scriptural] texts.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart gratitude for time and [the resolve] not to waste it. He shows joy before him when time is invested in obedience.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, bless my time,” daily. He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to schedule his day with investment in obedience and work. He holds him to account for wasted time.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that his lifespan is his capital and that he will be questioned about it, so that he is led to seize [the opportunity of] his life in obedience to Allaah.
Through the leading of the emotions: Love of seizing [the opportunity of one’s] lifespan and fear of squandering it are instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon taking the initiative.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to seize [the opportunity of] his lifespan for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Spending his lifespan in what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and squandering it in what He detests is made hateful to him, so that he grows familiar with goodness.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and perseverance in filling his time with obedience.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to persevere in filling his time with obedience, so that he counsels others to seize [the opportunity of] time and becomes for them a role model in safeguarding it.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to fill all his hours with obedience and what is beneficial, so that he guards his lifespan from waste and calls himself to account for it.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan induces procrastination and holds out the false hope of a long life, so that he is habituated to shortness of [worldly] expectation and to taking the initiative.
28. The beginning of thinking about starting a family or planning for a stable future.
The method of direction: linking the intention of marriage and stable living to the realization of repose and tranquility upon the methodology of Allaah, which activates “the righteous intention.”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that marriage is the way (sunnah) of the messengers and a field of tranquility. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the intention of religiously [sanctioned] repose. He shows joy before him at his aspiration toward righteous marriage.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, provide me with a righteous wife and wholesome offspring.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him to save up the marriage dowry and to prepare for independence. He motivates him toward marriage through the lawful.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that marriage is a Sunnah, an act of worship, and a means of chastity, so that he is led to prepare himself to build a home upon God-consciousness.
Through the leading of the emotions: His innate desire is directed toward the lawful, and seeking the one of religion [as a spouse] is instilled in him, so that his emotion is nurtured upon chastity.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to intend by marriage the guarding of his own chastity and the establishment of a Muslim household for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): What Allaah has legislated regarding marriage is made beloved to him, and the unlawful and forbidden relationships are made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience and chastity until Allaah makes [matters] easy, and in preparing to bear the responsibility of a family.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded of patience and chastity until Allaah makes [matters] easy, so that he counsels himself to prepare to bear the responsibility of a family through knowledge and good character.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to spend his time in preparing for his future and his family, so that he readies himself for the burdens of responsibility within his time.
Through knowing the enemies: He is taught that Satan beautifies the unlawful and discourages [one] from the lawful, so that he is habituated to chastity, fasting, and lowering the gaze.
29. An intense sensitivity toward any insult that touches upon [one’s] dignity.
The method of direction: purifying the self through humility before Allaah and accepting criticism for the sake of Allaah, which cleanses the heart of “blameworthy disdain (al-anafah al-madhmoemah).”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator (murabbie) engages the young man in dialogue concerning the fact that humility before Allaah is an honor and that criticism is a blessing. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart humility and the acceptance of criticism. He shows joy before him when he bears criticism gently.
Third: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the tongue
He teaches him to utter, “O Allaah, make me gentle and soft [in nature].” He repeats that with him daily.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing (tarbiyah) — the upbringing of the limbs
He trains him in self-control upon [being subjected to] insult and in not taking revenge. He praises him for [his] forbearance.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through the leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that his dignity is with Allaah and that forbearance and pardon are [a source of] elevation, so that he is led to control himself upon [being subjected to] insult.
Through the leading of the emotions: His being affected by insult is regulated so that it does not drive him to blameworthy revenge, and forbearance is instilled in him.
Through sincerity (ikhlaas): He is habituated to pardon and to restrain [his anger] for the sake of Allaah, so that sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, allegiance, and disavowal (al-walaa’ wa-l-baraa’): Pardon and forbearance, which Allaah loves, are made beloved to him, and transgression and blameworthy revenge are made hateful to him, so that he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained in patience with harm and in pardoning while [having the] power [to retaliate].
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to pardon harm while [having the] power [to retaliate], so that he counsels himself that pardon is nearer to God-consciousness and greater in reward.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to squander his time in avenging himself, so that he directs it toward pardon and beneficial work.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan provokes his pride when he is insulted, so he is habituated to forbearance, seeking refuge (with Allaah), and pardoning for the sake of Allaah.
30. The desire to prove one’s competence before elders.
The method of direction: transforming this desire into proving one’s competence before Allaah, and striving for acceptance with Him rather than with creation.
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator engages the youth in dialogue about how the best competence is competence in the sight of Allaah. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the seeking of Allaah’s acceptance first. He rejoices before him at a hidden effort done for Allaah.
Third: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — formation of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “O Allaah, accept it from me.” He repeats that with him after every deed.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — formation of the limbs
He trains him in a deed that he conceals from people with excellence. He praises him for sincerity in secret.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: His desire to prove his competence is directed toward seeking Allaah’s pleasure and mastery of the deed, so he is led to work for Allaah and not for display.
Through leadership of the emotions: His eagerness to prove himself is regulated so that it does not turn into showing off and pride, and humility is instilled in him.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to perfect his deed for Allaah and not to prove his competence to people, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty and disavowal: Excellence, which Allaah loves, is made beloved to him, and the seeking of praise is made hateful to him, so he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient with a lack of appreciation while still doing well, and to respect his elders.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to do well even if he is not appreciated, and to respect his elders, so he counsels himself that his reward is with Allaah and not with people.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to occupy his time waiting for people’s praise, so that he directs his concern toward doing well by which he seeks the Face of Allaah.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that the love of proving oneself is the gateway to showing off and pride, which Satan exploits, so he is habituated to sincerity and humility.
31. A greater capacity to resist peer pressure once values have taken root.
The method of direction: holding fast to the truth and remaining steadfast upon it, which yields “steadfastness” and “resolve upon right guidance.”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator engages the youth in dialogue about how steadfastness upon the truth is among the matters of firm resolve. He establishes the proof for that.
Second: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the resolve of right guidance. He rejoices before him at his steadfastness in the face of peer pressure.
Third: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — formation of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “O Allaah, make me firm upon Your religion.” He repeats that with him daily.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — formation of the limbs
He trains him to abandon bad company even if it is dear to him. He praises him for steadfastness with joy.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that honor lies in obedience to Allaah and not in conforming to peers, so he is led to remain steadfast upon the truth even if he opposes them.
Through leadership of the emotions: Strength of heart through faith is instilled in him in the face of peer pressure, so that his emotion grows up upon steadfastness.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to remain steadfast upon the truth for Allaah and not so that it be said he is brave, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty and disavowal: Steadfastness upon what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and he is kept away from conforming to peers in falsehood, so he grows up upon loyalty and disavowal.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient in opposing his peers and in the loneliness of remaining steadfast upon the truth.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded to remain steadfast upon the truth even if opposing his peers makes him feel lonely, so he counsels them toward it with wisdom and does not go along with them.
Through the management of time: He is reminded not to let time spent with peers drag him into falsehood, so he guards his time with company that helps him toward steadfastness.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is taught that Satan uses peer pressure to drag him into evil, so he is habituated to steadfastness and to seeking help from Allaah.
32. The beginning of the realization that true freedom is bound to responsibility.
The method of direction: venerating the concept of servitude to Allaah as the highest form of liberation, which firmly establishes “submission to Allaah.”
First: Treating it through purging (tasfiyah)
The educator engages the youth in dialogue about how true freedom lies in servitude to Allaah. He establishes the proof for that through a rational demonstration.
Second: Treating it through purification of the soul (tazkiyah)
He plants in his heart the loftiest meanings of servitude to Allaah. He rejoices before him at his submission to the law of Allaah.
Third: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — formation of the tongue
He instructs him to say, “I am a servant of Allaah; my freedom lies in His worship.” He repeats that with him.
Fourth: Treating it through upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) — formation of the limbs
He trains him to adhere to the law of Allaah in his freedoms. He makes servitude the ceiling of his freedom.
Direction through the branches of veneration:
Through leadership of the self and the pursuit of knowledge: He is taught that true freedom is servitude to Allaah and liberation from desire, so he is led to use his freedom in obedience to his Lord.
Through leadership of the emotions: It is instilled in him that the heart’s ease lies in servitude to Allaah and not in following desire, so that his emotion grows up upon love of obedience.
Through sincerity: He is habituated to use his freedom in what pleases Allaah, so sincerity is instilled in him.
Through love, fear, loyalty and disavowal: Using his freedom in what Allaah loves is made beloved to him, and using it in disobedience is made hateful to him, so he grows up upon love and hatred for the sake of Allaah.
Through patience: He is trained to be patient in bearing the responsibility of his freedom and in not misusing it.
Through sincere counsel: He is reminded that his freedom is a trust for which he will be held accountable, so he counsels himself not to misuse it in what angers Allaah.
Through the management of time: He is reminded to spend his freedom and his time in what benefits him in his religion and his worldly life, so that he does not make idleness a gateway to corruption.
Through knowledge of the enemies: He is fortified against Satan’s making unrestraint seem attractive to him in the name of freedom, and he is taught that freedom without responsibility is chaos and enslavement to desire.
The Conclusion: Findings and Recommendations
After this journey in establishing the foundations of the veneration of Allaah (glorified and exalted is He) and applying it to the reality of upbringing and formation across its various stages, this study arrives at a number of findings and recommendations:
First: The most important findings
That the veneration of Allaah (glorified is He) is the foundation of all foundations and the very spirit of tawhied, and that the soundness of the heart and its deeds depends upon its being filled with reverence for Allaah, awe of Him, and love of Him.
That true veneration is a comprehensive system embracing the heart, the tongue, and the limbs; an inward feeling without outward action does not suffice, nor does outward action without a firmly rooted foundation in the heart.
That the innate disposition (fitrah) upon which Allaah created people is furnished with energies and inclinations — such as curiosity, movement, imitation, attachment, and independence — and that these energies are neither to be suppressed nor neglected, but rather directed and steered toward the end for which they were created: the veneration of Allaah and His worship.
That the rabbaanie methodology in building souls rests upon three integrated stages: purging (tasfiyah) (correcting the conception and building the intellect through proof), purification of the soul (tazkiyah) (planting sound feelings in the heart of love, fear, and hope), and upbringing and formation (tarbiyah) (forming the tongue and the limbs through righteous action).
That every age stage has its own innate physical and psychological characteristics suited to it, and that taking these characteristics into account in upbringing is more conducive to firm rooting and further removed from clashing and suppression.
That the child in the stage before religious accountability (from birth to two years) is raised by preparing the faith-filled environment saturated with the remembrance of Allaah and His veneration around him, so that the treatment of his characteristics along the four tracks is directed at the educator himself.
That correction and discipline proceed gradually according to the age stage: from preparing the environment in infancy, to instruction and habituation in childhood, to demonstrative dialogue and gradual pedagogical punishment (3iqaab) in youth, while safeguarding the pedagogical companionship and intending reform rather than revenge.
That instilling the veneration of Allaah in the young is not merely the inculcation of concepts, but rather a purification of the intellect, the heart, and the limbs, and that the righteous role model and tying motivation to Allaah’s pleasure are among its greatest means.
Second: The most important recommendations
The study recommends that educators and teachers begin by building the pupil’s conception of Allaah and love of Him before demanding action of him, and that they keep in mind that guidance is in the Hand of Allaah and that their role is instruction, direction, being a role model, and seeking the reward (from Allaah).
It recommends that guardians look upon their children’s innate characteristics as energies that need direction rather than suppression, that they tie the rewarding of their children to Allaah’s pleasure and love rather than to material gifts alone, and that they be patient and supplicate abundantly for them.
It recommends that creators of pedagogical content make every innate trait the subject of content grounded in its legislative evidence, that they take the age groups into account in the language and level of the content, and that they intend the veneration of Allaah in the hearts rather than mere dissemination.
It recommends that pedagogical institutions build their curricula upon this gradual methodology that takes into account the innate disposition and the age stages, and that they prepare educators according to its principles.
It recommends that researchers continue applying this great foundation to the remaining fields of upbringing and formation, and enrich it with applied and field studies.
It recommends everyone to make their foremost intention the Face of Allaah, and to seek His help and take refuge in Him in the turning of the hearts of those they raise, for hearts are between two of the Fingers of the Most Merciful, which He turns however He wills.
In closing, we ask Allaah the Exalted to make this work sincerely for His Noble Face, beneficial to His servants, a means of His veneration — majestic is His majesty — upon the earth, and to benefit through it its writer, its reader, and everyone who strives to spread it. May Allaah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his Companions, and all praise is due to Allaah, Lord of the worlds.

sections.title: المسارات الأربعة للتربية الربّانية لهذه الفئة العمرية
sections.content: هذه المسارات الأربعة هي الإطار التأصيليّ الذي تُسيَّر به الخصال الفطرية لهذه الفئة وتُوجَّه؛ فالتربية الربّانية لا تتعامل مع الخصال الفطرية مفردةً مبعثرة، بل تَنظِمها في أربعة مساراتٍ منبثقةٍ من منهج التصفية والتزكية والتربية المقرَّر في الباب الثاني: مسارِ تطبيق التصفية (تكوين الفكر)، ومسارِ تطبيق التزكية (تكوين القلب)، ومسارِ تطبيق تربية اللسان (تكوين الأقوال)، ومسارِ تربية الجوارح (تكوين الأفعال). ولكلِّ مسارٍ تأصيلٌ بقواعده وأدلّتها من الكتاب والسنّة مع وجه الدلالة وتعليلٍ فطريٍّ يربط القاعدة بالخصلة الحاكمة، ثمّ ثلاثُ طرقٍ لتطبيقه بتسع وسائل، ثمّ ثلاثةُ تحدّياتٍ وعلاجُها بما يوافق الخصال الفطرية. ثمّ تأتي الخصائصُ الفطرية لهذه الفئة مفصَّلةً، لتُقرأ وتُسيَّر في ضوء هذه المسارات الأربعة.

sections.title: أولًا: التأصيل — قواعد تطبيق المسار لهذه الفئة
sections.content:
القاعدة الأولى: التصفية في هذه السنّ تجمع بين الغرس الابتدائي للتصوّر الصحيح والوقاية من دخول الباطل معًا.
 الدليل من الكتاب: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُم مِّن بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [النحل: ٧٨].
 وجه الدلالة: أخبر سبحانه أنّ الإنسان يبدأ خاليًا من العلم، وأنّ الحواسّ والفؤاد آلاتُ تحصيله؛ فدلّ على أنّ وظيفة المربّي في هذه السنّ ملءُ هذا الخلاء بالتصوّر الصحيح ابتداءً، لا مجرّد دفع الخطأ.
 الدليل من السنّة: حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه مرفوعًا: «ما مِن مولودٍ إلا يُولَد على الفطرة، فأبواه يُهوّدانه أو يُنصّرانه أو يُمجّسانه».
 وجه الدلالة: أثبت أنّ الطفل يُولَد على أصلٍ سليم، وأنّ المؤثّر الخارجيّ إمّا أن يصونه أو يحرّفه؛ فاجتمع في الحديث الأمران: تنميةُ الأصل الصحيح وحجبُ المحرِّف.
 التعليل الفطري: إنّما اختير هذان الدليلان لهذه الفئة لاجتماع جملةٍ من خصالها الفطرية: فسرعةُ التأثّر بصور البيئة تجعل الطفل كاللوح المهيّأ للنقش فيوافق ﴿لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا﴾، وحبُّ التقليد يجعله ينقل ما يراه بلا تمحيصٍ فيوافق «فأبواه يُهوّدانه»، وخلوُّ ذهنه من الشبهة الراسخة يفتح بابَ الغرس. والأنسبُ في تسمية الخصلة الحاكمة: سرعةُ التأثّر والتلقّي.
